job.title: Data Reporter, Texas
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Data Journalism department seeks an experienced journalist with programming and data analysis skills to be based in Texas and work in close collaboration with Times reporters across the Lone Star State.

You'll combine traditional reporting with data collection and analysis to shed light on major storylines. You'll demonstrate a strong command of key Texas datasets. You'll have excellent data analysis skills, with the news judgment to match, and can design rigorous methodologies, bulletproofing your analyses and handling thorny data issues.

Collaboration is at the heart of this role; you'll pair up with other reporters on virtually every story you pursue. You'll also help these colleagues to level-up their own data skills. And you'll be excited, in turn, about learning from them.

This role requires you to be based in Texas. Although The Times does not yet have an office in the state, this position may later involve regular office attendance if The Times establishes an office in the city where you are based. You will report to the Data Editor, who is based in New York City.

Important application requirement: Please submit a cover letter that highlights three relevant stories to which you made substantial contributions. For each story, please provide a link to the story and describe your contribution in one to three paragraphs. Aim to demonstrate a range of skills and variety of deadlines. Your cover letter should be no more than three pages long in total. In it, you are also welcome to provide a more traditional (but brief) description of your career and talents.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the Data Journalism department's Texas-focused reporting collaborations
  • Pitch and report data-driven stories that illuminate the day's news events, explain difficult concepts and investigate wrongdoing
  • Obtain and build datasets through records requests, web scraping, document parsing and shoe-leather approaches
  • Develop an understanding of these datasets, enabling you to mine them for reporting leads, meaningful insights, and newsworthy findings
  • Be comfortable working on stories both independently and in diverse teams
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world
  • You will report to the Data Editor

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of data journalism experience
  • Deep knowledge of Texas
  • Experience finding, requesting, cleaning and analyzing complex datasets
  • Ability to communicate data findings powerfully, accurately, and succinctly
  • Proficiency working with data in Python and/or R, spreadsheets, and relational databases

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Substantial track record reporting on Texas
  • Spanish language proficiency
  • Experience with, and a preference for, working collaboratively on multidisciplinary teams
  • Experience reporting in response to major news cycles
  • Comfort with command-line tooling, version control, working with large language models, and other important technical skills

job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Election Analytics team produces flagship, standard-setting elections coverage, including the live, election night statistical model known as the Needle and The New York Times/Siena Poll. The department is looking to hire an experienced data developer to contribute to data creation, management and architecture across our products.

Underneath our poll and the Needle are massive amounts of data. This includes the voter file, as well as demographics for different localities, hundreds of scrapers collecting precinct data and countless pipelines for processing and cleaning data. Our understanding of the electorate is only as good as the data we have access to, including the data we create to test our systems and the election night model itself.

You will have a central role in creating and cleaning these data sources for use in our products. You will help knit together data from different sections of the team to build our understanding of what may happen on election night throughout the year. And you will ensure we have proper observability into how data is being used.

Election Analytics is a multidisciplinary team of reporters, developers, statisticians and modelers who work on written coverage, graphics, our polls and the election-night model. This is a highly collaborative role that will involve working with colleagues from Election Analytics, the Graphics department and Interactive News.

This is an in-office position in New York City or Washington, D.C., and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

To apply, you MUST include a cover letter of no more than 300 words that…

  • Explains how you approached a specific instance where you had to balance engineering principles with the need to meet a deadline; and

  • Explains specifically why you are interested in covering elections

Responsibilities:

  • Create test data for the election-night mathematical model and for live election-night Graphics

  • Build and improve pipelines for ingesting, processing, and displaying large data sets, precinct data or absentee files.

  • Build and maintain observability tools for the model that allow for fast debugging on election night and clear monitoring of precinct data entering the model

  • Work with stakeholders to understand the data needs and schema requirements

  • Develop and maintain libraries in R that form the basis of our apps

  • Balance engineering principles with the need to move at the speed of news

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

  • You will report to the Director of Election Analytics

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of relevant experience

  • Familiarity working with large datasets and with best practices in data management

  • Experience working with data-oriented programming languages, such as R or Python

  • Experience working with cloud computing providers such as Google Cloud Platform or Amazon Web Services

  • Experience working collaboratively with people of different skills and backgrounds

  • Willingness to work a flexible schedule as needed to support coverage of elections and polls

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience working with election data

  • Experience developing ETL pipelines, working with orchestration tooling, and ensuring reliability and observability

  • Experience with Google BigQuery or other OLAP databases

  • Experience building productionized apps

job.title: Research Lead, Wirecutter
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

We are looking for a Research Lead with experience ensuring that shopping-centric insights are at the heart of product development. You will lead a variety of end-to-end research projects that inform Wirecutter's strategy. Your projects will focus on helping connect our visitors to Wirecutter across the full shopping experience. Your research will inform audience strategy, content prioritization, and the Wirecutter Store, amongst other areas. You will be an important partner with Design, Product, Engineering, Marketing, Data, Editorial, guiding decision-making and informing the teams' strategies.

We at The New York Times seek the truth and help people understand the world. This mission is rooted in our belief that great journalism has the power to make each reader's life richer and more fulfilling, and all of society stronger and more just.

The mission of the New York Times Audience Insights team is to help The Times grow by understanding our audience. The Audience Insights team is a team of researchers that employ tools, methods and approaches across a wide variety of research domains, including product, human-centered design, innovation, market and UX research, and we draw from principles in the social sciences (Psychology, Anthropology, Sociology and Behavioral Economics). We believe that the best work is achieved when we support healthy work-life balance. We support people in managing their workload and encourage team members to take all of their personal and vacation time each year.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead research through a human-centered design approach to identify opportunity areas, alongside Product, Design, and Editorial teams
  • Test prototypes, create surveys, and run alpha and beta programs
  • Evaluate impact on trust and relationships with Wirecutter
  • Complement research with behavioral data, proprietary and industry research, and A/B testing results to provide a holistic view of our users.
  • Be a resource and partner to researchers across Marketing, Cooking, News Product, The Athletic and Games to identify opportunities to collaborate and avoid duplicative product work.
  • Manage external research vendors to support moderation, fieldwork, and analysis, ensuring high-quality and efficient project execution.
  • Contribute to the collaborative culture of Audience Insights and Wirecutter; help The New York Times understand, and build empathy for, our audiences.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Managing Director, Games and Wirecutter Audience Insights

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor of Arts/Bachelor of Science in a relevant field
  • 8+ years of research and insights experience.
  • 8+ years of experience implementing a range of research methods (qualitative and quantitative) and design thinking techniques based on the problem to be solved
  • 3+ years of experience in the e-commerce industry, or shopping experiences.
  • 3+ years of experience moderating qualitative research and facilitating brainstorms and workshops with partners.
  • 3+ years of experience summarizing complex findings into compelling narratives and visualize insights for diverse audiences with actionable insights.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of experience in the e-commerce industry, or shopping experiences
  • 2+ years of experience working on a product with a subscription-based model
  • 2+ years of experience using behavioral data alongside research (either qualitative or quantitative) to provide a holistic picture
  • Experience creating buy-in with cross-functional partners
  • 1+ years understanding the role of AI within the shopping experience

Position Overview

Cox Media Group (CMG) Atlanta Radio has an exciting opportunity for a Digital Journalist for WSB-FM News. We are building something big at CMG, connecting audiences to the content they rely on and creating solutions that help our advertisers reach the customers they want to reach. We invite you to join us!

 

This role focuses on researching, reporting, and publishing stories across online platforms, including websites, social media, and mobile apps. Our Digital Journalists work within a 24-hour news cycle, prioritizing speed and real-time updates while integrating multimedia elements such as video, audio, and interactive graphics. The Digital Journalist will engage audiences with timely, compelling content and play a key role in expanding our digital footprint and online engagement.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Manages the regular flow of timely news content on station websites; engages our audience on major social media platforms; drives traffic to our streaming channels; otherwise assists in growing stations’ online presence.
  • Produces digital content that supports and enhances station initiatives, including writing breaking and trending news articles, creating social media content, contests, newsletters, videos, and podcasts.
  • Collaborates with WSB Programming, News, and Promotions teams.
  • Manages the official social media accounts for WSB, including posting on behalf of the station.
  • Brings an array of original ideas and concepts to help create new content that promotes listener participation, builds the online audience, and supports digital business goals.
  • Managing reader interactions through comments and social media and using analytics (such as click rates) to understand which content resonates.
  • Fact-checking viral claims and identifying misinformation to maintain credibility in a fast-paced environment.
  • Edits video and creates graphics for social media as needed.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 1–2 years of experience in news journalism in broadcast media (or a closely related newsroom environment).
  • Firsthand experience creating digital-first news content in a 24-hour news cycle (breaking and trending coverage with rapid updates).
  • Demonstrated experience managing content across websites, social platforms, newsletters, video, and podcasts.
  • Solid news judgment: the ability to prioritize, spot trends, and decide what to publish quickly and responsibly.
  • Research and reporting skills, including sourcing and verifying information under a deadline.
  • Proven record in fact-checking and the ability to identify misinformation and viral false claims to protect credibility.
  • Proficient writing, editing, proofreading, and copywriting (news, plus lifestyle/entertainment as needed).
  • Ability to manage day-to-day publishing via content management systems (CMS) and to learn new systems quickly.
  • Knowledge in managing and posting for official social media accounts (Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, X).
  • Demonstrated audience engagement skills, including managing comments and reader interactions appropriately.
  • Ability to use analytics (e.g., click rates and engagement) to understand what performs well and adjust content accordingly.
  • Must have a valid driver's license and clean driving record

Minimum Qualifications (continued)

  • Adept at supporting digital goals such as increasing traffic, expanding the streaming audience, and strengthening overall online presence.
  • Ability to create/edit multimedia elements, including:
    • Basic video editing (Adobe Premiere or similar)
    • Simple graphics creation (Photoshop or similar)
    • Integrating audio/video/interactive elements into stories when relevant
  • Proven project management, organizational, and attention to detail skills.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal guidance.
  • Strong cross-team collaboration with Programming, News, and Promotions.
  • Flexibility to work a fluid schedule, including occasional evenings/weekends.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree, preferably in journalism, digital media, or communications.

About Cox Media Group 

CMG Media Corporation (d/b/a Cox Media Group) is an industry-leading media company with unparalleled brands, award-winning content, and exceptional team members. CMG provides valuable local and national journalism and entertainment content to the people and communities it serves. The company's businesses encompass 17 high-quality, market-leading television brands in 9 markets; 45 top-performing radio stations delivering multiple genres of content in 9 markets; and numerous streaming and digital platforms. CMG's TV portfolio includes multiple primary affiliates of ABC, CBS, FOX, NBC, Telemundo and MyNetworkTV, as well as several valuable news and independent stations. For more information about CMG, visit www.coxmediagroup.com

job.description:
The Physical Sales & E-Commerce Executive will support Sony Music’s growth of the physical market across Southeast Asia. The role will support the development and operation of physical sales channels for Vinyl, CDs and other physical products, working across both wholesale/distribution and D2C channels.

The role focuses on developing and operating sales channels, ensuring products are priced appropriately, inventory is forecasted and managed effectively, order are fulfilled and collected, and sales channels are maintained and optimised. This includes supporting the development of D2C infrastructure and storefronts using Shopify.

What you'll do:

  • Develop and grow physical sales channels across Southeast Asian territories, supporting the sale of Vinyl, CDs and other physical products.
  • Manage the day-to-day operational requirements of sales channels, including pricing, inventory management, forecasting, orders, delivery and collection of payments.
  • Support the development and management of wholesale/distribution channels, working with local distributors and retail partners to increase physical distribution and sales.
  • Support the development and operation of D2C sales channels, including the ongoing maintenance and optimisation of Shopify powered storefronts.
  • Act as a key operational contact for local and international stakeholders, working across labels, artist teams, merchandise companies, distributors, retail partner and platform partners.
  • Assist in the delivery of album launches, pre-orders, bundles and release activity across wholesale and D2C sales channels, working closely with artist, label and merchandise company partners.
  • Oversee the operational flow of physical products into sales channels, collaborating with fulfilment, logistics and other partners to maintain high service standards.
  • Support sales channel performance, contributing to sales targets, inventory optimisation, forecasting and commercial performance.

Who you are:

  • 2+ years experience in a physical sales, e-commerce or online retail role.
  • Strong hands-on experience managing sales channels and/or e-commerce stores.
  • Sales and operational experience, ideally with physical music products or consumer products.
  • Experience working with distributors, retail partners and D2C sales channels.
  • Comfortable working across multiple projects, artists and stakeholders in a fast-paced environment.  
  • Strong understanding of sales performance, inventory and forecasting and using data to guide decisions.
  • Highly organised, detail oriented, and confident working with numbers, spreadsheets, and Microsoft tools such as Excel, Teams, and Copilot.  
  • Hands-on Shopify experience.
  • Familiarity with the Southeast Asian retail or consumer landscape is advantageous.
 

What we give you:

  • You join a vibrant global community with the opportunity to channel your passion every day

  • Investment in your professional growth and development enabling you to thrive in our vibrant community

job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role:  

As part of the Commercial Business and Legal Affairs team and reporting to the SVP, Associate General Counsel & Strategic Partnerships, the Vice President, Head of Privacy (Privacy, Cyber Security, Consumer Compliance) is responsible for all legal aspects of data privacy, information security, and consumer marketing and subscriptions-related compliance across the company and for managing the Company's privacy compliance function. You will work closely with senior executives and operational leads as well as the working team, including the areas of marketing operations, subscription growth, product, engineering, technology, data governance, information security, commercial contracts, and marketing and advertising technology. In this position, you will manage a team. 

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Advise all internal clients on the risks and operational controls related to the development, collection, use, transfer, and governance of personal data of consumers, employees, and other stakeholders. This will include privacy, online safety, and cybersecurity (from both U.S. and international perspectives). 

  • Advise key business stakeholders on the company’s data governance, cybersecurity, marketing and subscriptions compliance efforts in a manner consistent with the Company’s goals and culture.

  • Drive measurable improvements in privacy program maturity, incident readiness, vendor governance, compliant product launches, and privacy risk reduction. Manage privacy program resourcing, vendor support, and outside counsel engagement for privacy matters, as applicable.

  • Draft and/or update privacy program-related policies and standards, public-facing and internal; as well as terms of use, terms of sale, and other consumer-facing acceptable use and moderation policies.

  • Supervise and oversee the preparation and updating of Data Protection Impact Assessments and other risk assessment and audit activities as needed. Conduct comprehensive business risk assessments; develop/implement risk mitigation and corrective action plans where needed.

  • Advise on privacy regulatory and contractual compliance in marketing, ad sales, direct and programmatic advertising, identity resolution, data clean rooms, and third-party data and ad tech integrations to help ensure compliance with privacy and consumer protection laws and industry standards.

  • Review, draft and negotiate data protection agreements and security exhibits and work closely with the appropriate teams to advise on third party risk reviews. 

  • Advise on all relevant consumer protection, subscriptions and marketing laws, regulations and best practices.

  • Provide product counseling to include privacy, cybersecurity and consumer compliance legal advice as well as other areas of related legal need – in connection with product and platform developments and releases. 

  • Regularly track and counsel clients on legal US and international developments in areas of data privacy, cybersecurity and consumer marketing and subscription compliance.

  • Serve as legal lead for all security incident response, working closely with the company’s Chief Information Security Officer and other key stakeholders; draft and update information security policies and procedures.

  • Provide advice and guidance to data science and analytics teams on privacy-compliant deployment of machine learning models and personalization.

  • Oversee and develop company-wide training strategy and execution for areas of coverage.

  • Serve as point of contact for data protection authorities, regulatory inquiries, and industry groups.

  • Excellent judgment and professional integrity.

  • Handle high-volume workload efficiently.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • Juris Doctor is required and must be a member of the New York Bar.

  • 15+ years of experience in US and international data privacy and protection; negotiating data privacy-related agreements, building, implementing, and maintaining a global privacy program; supporting cybersecurity. 

  • 5+ years of experience managing people with proven experience effectively managing cross-functional relationships and competing priorities.

  • 5+ years of previous in-house experience.

  • Experience advising on online safety laws such as age-appropriate design codes and app store age signals laws, and sensitive data privacy regulations such as laws governing health data in ad tech and biometric privacy.

  • Experience advising or managing legal professionals who advise on a wide variety of consumer-related issues both domestic and international, including payflow, subscription offerings, marketing, auto-renewal and click-to-cancel laws, anti-spam, Telephone Consumer Protection Act, unfair and deceptive practice laws, customer care complaints and escalations, and payment card rules.

job.title: Business Director
job.description:
Who We Are

We are an award-winning independent creative solutions company that aspires to be the most culturally-influential company in the world. We help ambitious brands harness the power of culture to solve their biggest challenges. As a unique mix of experts in culture, technology, and storytelling, we are united by a passion to grow brands in ways that advertising alone can never do.

We are an entrepreneurial business, not a traditional “ad agency.” That means we value resourcefulness and tenacity just as much as we value creativity and intelligence. We’re unapologetically ambitious!

We are looking for a Business Director to join Translation and help lead our growing Eli Lilly partnership, bringing culturally relevant creative work to life for brands that impact people’s health.

Position Summary

As a Business Director, you will serve as a strategic leader and trusted client partner across assigned Eli Lilly brands and workstreams. You will build a deep understanding of the client’s business, patient audiences, and category, translating those insights into clear direction and creative opportunities that connect brands with people in meaningful ways.

Working with the account’s Executive Director, you will lead client relationships, guide cross-functional teams, develop Business Leadership talent, and identify opportunities for growth. You will partner closely with Program Management on delivery and account financial health, balancing creative ambition with the rigor of a regulated category and the needs of a fast-growing business.

What You Will Do

Drive Business and Strategic Leadership

  • Act as the day-to-day senior business lead across assigned Lilly brands and workstreams, building trusted relationships with mid-to-senior client stakeholders and proactively shaping the business agenda.
  • Develop a strong understanding of brand priorities, patient experiences, barriers to engagement, and competitive dynamics to inform strategic counsel and creative development.
  • Translate complex client needs and feedback into clear priorities and actionable direction, constructively challenging clients when needed to strengthen the work.
  • Monitor relationship health and business performance, anticipating risks and partnering with the Executive Director to address issues before they affect the partnership.

Lead Creative Solutions with Business Impact

  • Partner with Strategy, Context, Creative, and Analytics to develop culturally relevant work grounded in business objectives, audience insights, and clear measures of success.
  • Champion communication that reflects real patient experiences and makes complex health topics understandable, empathetic, and relevant to everyday life.
  • Ensure work is strategically sound and client-ready, with compelling rationale and alignment to client-provided medical, legal, and regulatory guidance.
  • Work with Lilly’s brand teams, internal creative team, and agency partners to clarify roles, align recommendations, and maintain continuity across the work.
  • Partner with Production and Program Management to bring approved concepts to life within agreed scope, timing, and budget, advocating for additional investment when warranted.

Lead Teams and Strengthen Partnerships

  • Guide cross-functional teams with clear priorities, expectations, and decisions, creating a collaborative environment with shared accountability for the work.
  • Lead, coach, and develop Business Supervisors and other assigned Business Leadership team members through regular feedback and meaningful development opportunities.
  • Partner with Program Management, which leads operational planning and delivery, to align client expectations with scopes, schedules, staffing, and review requirements.
  • Work with client stakeholders and Program Management to anticipate approval needs, consolidate feedback, and help teams understand review decisions and their implications.
  • Navigate competing stakeholder needs and resolve day-to-day challenges independently, escalating significant relationship, commercial, or delivery risks appropriately.

Champion Growth and Financial Health

  • Develop and action growth plans for assigned brands and workstreams, connecting unmet client needs with Translation’s capabilities.
  • Co-own account financial health with Program Management, contributing to scope development, staffing recommendations, forecasting, and profitability management.
  • Identify scope changes and investment needs early, leading clear client conversations about the associated fees, priorities, and trade-offs.
  • Contribute to new business, recruiting, and departmental improvements that strengthen the agency and develop future Business Leadership talent.

Knowledge Skills and Abilities

  • Strong business judgment and strategic fluency, with the ability to learn complex categories and turn ambiguity into clear direction.
  • Exceptional relationship-building and communication skills, including the confidence to advise clients, explain creative rationale, and navigate sensitive conversations.
  • Ability to balance creative ambition with accuracy and client review requirements, partnering effectively with medical, legal, and regulatory stakeholders.
  • Experience leading integrated campaigns across channels, with a strong understanding of creative development and production.
  • Commercial acumen across scopes, staffing, budgets, and account performance, paired with a collaborative approach to Program Management.
  • A proactive, hands-on leadership style, with sound prioritization, attention to detail, and the ability to develop others in a fast-moving environment.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 7-10 years of experience in an agency or communications-related industry, with a well-rounded understanding of advertising, marketing, media, creative, production, and agency finance.
  • Proven success managing integrated campaigns, partnering with mid-to-senior-level clients, and leading cross-functional teams.
  • Hands-on production experience with large-scale, multi-channel initiatives.
  • Experience coaching junior account team members and contributing to scope development, account financial management, and organic growth.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting pharmaceutical, healthcare, or other regulated brands, including familiarity with medical, legal, and regulatory review processes. Direct pharma experience is a plus, not a requirement; curiosity about the category and an eagerness to learn are valued.
  • Experience with consumer-facing health communications, patient storytelling, or brand launches.
  • Experience partnering with in-house creative teams and working within a multi-agency environment.
  • Experience developing culturally relevant campaigns, including talent partnerships, social content, or experiential work.
  • Bachelor’s degree in marketing, business, or a related field.

About UnitedMasters, Inc.

UnitedMasters Inc. represents the creative solutions company, Translation, and the leading software and services platform for independent creators, UnitedMasters. UnitedMasters enables ownership, exposure, and new paths for financial return for independent creators, while Translation helps brands leverage the power of contemporary culture to achieve transformational growth. Combined, UnitedMasters, Inc. is the world’s leading marketplace for cultural capital, connecting independent artists and brands to realize a future in which all creators own their future. Backed by Alphabet, Andreessen Horowitz, and Apple, UnitedMasters, Inc. is reimagining how brands and artists come together to tell their stories, build profitable growth, and push culture forward.

Salary Hiring Range: $115,000 - $135,000

Our salary ranges are based on paying competitively for our size and industry, and are one part of many compensation, benefits and other reward opportunities we provide (e.g. bonus, stock options, 401(k) match, etc.)

Individual pay rate decisions are based on a number of factors, including qualifications for the role, experience level, skillset, and balancing internal equity relative to peers at the company.  We expect the majority of the candidates who are offered roles at our company to fall healthily throughout the range based on these factors. 

The range above is for the expectations as laid out in the job description, however we are often open to a wide variety of profiles, and recognize that the person we hire may be less experienced (or more senior) than this job description as posted.  If that ends up being the case, the updated salary range will be communicated with you as a candidate.

The salary range above is for the NY/CA.  As a company, we have a location based strategy, which means the salary range could be lower or higher than this if the role is hired in another location.

job.title: Overnight/Live Broadcasting Supervising Editor, Morning Edition & Up First
job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide. 

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Application Instructions:

Please submit your resume and cover letter. In your cover letter please share your philosophy for leading a newsroom overnight in order to deliver the most up-to-date morning broadcast possible.

Intro to Position

Morning Edition and Up First are looking for a resilient journalist with strong news judgment, excellent writing skills and a willingness to work overnights as the Overnight/Live Broadcast Supervising Editor, managing  a production team that executes what is needed to get the live radio show to air and the Up First podcast to publication.

Millions of listeners depend on Morning Edition and Up First to set the news agenda to start their day. We deliver the latest national and international news stories paired with analysis to put headlines into context. Morning Edition is a platform for accountability through interviews with government officials and decision makers who make or influence policy that affect people's lives. The show also features culture stories about music, movies and books that bring joy and provoke thoughtful conversations about who we are in this world.

The right candidate for this position is committed to daily news, and is eager to deliver the freshest, most important stories to listeners. They put the needs and wants of audiences first. They believe in the mission of public media.

As the Overnight/Live Broadcast Supervising Editor, you will join a team of managers who collaboratively lead news and editorial coverage of events in the U.S. and around the world for Morning Edition and Up First. You ensure that the show is at the leading edge of the conversation across a range of issues. Most importantly, you work directly with our hosts to edit and make final changes to the show before and while it is live on air to ensure we are broadcasting our best journalism and editorial work.

Duties for this position include assigning stories and segments to hosts, producers and editors; editing show scripts, crafting live coverage and breaking news plans; leading the control room during the live broadcast; finding guests and reporters to feature on the show when needed; monitoring news and responding with show coverage plans as needed; mentoring and editing producers’ and editors’ writing for stories and show segments; managing staff work schedules as emergencies arise; coordinate and collaborate with other newsroom editors, leaders and journalists on show coverage plans, projects; upload editorial standards and ethics as the lead show manager during your shift. As a manager, you will be assigned direct reports and are expected to evaluate and develop staff.

This is an overnight position with a shift scheduled from approximately 11:30pm - 8:30am Eastern Time Sunday-Thursday.

Morning Edition is a 24/6 news operation. Successful candidates can work holidays and may be asked to temporarily change their work schedule to cover other show shifts and special assignments as needed.

This is an NPR editorial role covered under the terms of the NPR Ethics Handbook. All editorial staff are bound by this guidance. Editorial staff are defined as staff members who play a role in shaping the journalistic or creative direction of NPR's content, including events.    

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Lead the show production team in bringing the live radio show and podcast to air, including the most listened to segment that airs during the 7a ET hour
  • Manage the editorial operation of the control room during the live broadcast
  • Coordinate with teams for live updates for later news feeds
  • Work directly with show hosts, guests and reporters to prep, record and edit live and taped interviews for the show and podcast on a tight deadline
  • Line edit various scripts for the live show while maintaining NPR’s editorial standards for all parts of the final product
  • Make editorial, programming and news judgment decisions about edits and show coverage plans, especially during breaking news situations
  • Provide written and verbal editorial feedback to staff on work
  • Evaluate, develop, and manage staff performance
  • Collaborate with multiplatform news teams to maximize reach of show content
  • Participate in the hiring of individual staff
  • Cultivate, promote and advance diversity, equity, and inclusion in one’s work and in the workplace.
  • Demonstrated awareness of intersectional identities and ability to collaborate with people from diverse backgrounds
  • Other duties as assigned

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

  • At least 3  years of experience managing direct reports in a newsroom or operation
  • At least 5  years of experience writing and editing broadcast journalism content
  • At least 5 years of experience producing daily news journalism content for a national or international news organization

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with audio production and mixing techniques
  • Experience working in a live control room
  • Experience being the lead producer or editor for a radio or podcast show 
  • Experience editing news content for various platforms
  • Familiarity in another written language other than English, such as Spanish or Mandarin

EDUCATION REQUIREMENT

Bachelor's degree or equivalent in work experience.

WORK LOCATION

On-site: This is an on-site role based in Washington, DC .

REQUIRED SKILLS

  • Mastery in project management such as managing deadlines and time management
  • Expert knowledge and demonstrated skill in news-writing techniques for varied formats such as guest interviews, breaking news,  feature stories
  • Mastery in AP style writing and editing skill for broadcast and digital platforms.
  • Demonstrated ability and experience in writing and editing news copy for varied platforms including broadcast, podcast, social, mobile, newsletters and other digital platforms, especially during breaking news situations
  • Proficiency in people management skills such as delivering constructive feedback, clear communication and conflict resolution.
  • Proficiency in independent, problem solving. 
  • Ability to adapt and accommodate differing styles of editorial workflows and communication.
  • Ability to negotiate and compromise.
  • Professional communication skills when representing the NPR organization.

Job Type

  • This is a full time, exempt position.

Compensation

Salary Range: The U.S. based anticipated salary range for this opportunity is $145,000-155,000 a year plus benefits. The range displayed reflects the minimum and maximum salaries NPR expects to provide for new hires for the position across all US locations.

Benefits: NPR offers access to comprehensive benefits for employees and dependents. Regular, full-time employees scheduled to work 30 hours or more per week are eligible to enroll in NPR’s benefits options. Benefits include access to health and wellness, paid time off, and financial well-being. Plan options include medical, dental, vision, life/ accidental death and dismemberment, long-term disability, short-term disability, and voluntary retirement savings to all eligible NPR employees. 

Does this sound like you? If so, we want to hear from you.

Principal Software Engineer, Pub Admin

UK & Ireland, United Kingdom, London

Sony Music’s Product, Design, Engineering & Global Operations (PDEGO) organisation is seeking a Principal Software Engineer within our Pub Admin product team in our London King’s Cross office (hybrid/three days a week).

Pub Admin (Publishing Administration) is our future product for a unified, modern rights platform - where our engineers help transform the complex domain of music publishing administration into simple, scalable, high-performance product solutions for Sony Music’s global creator community. You’ll shape what we build as well as how we build it, working directly with product and design on problems where the right answer isn’t yet known.

What you'll do:

  • Work cross-functionally across multiple teams in our Royalty Accounting organisation to build and own a new business vertical that will help rights holders register, manage, and monetize their catalogues worldwide
  • Lead design, implementation, and scaling of complex distributed systems end-to-end from early-stage ideation to market
  • Partner with product management and design to understand client and stakeholder needs, challenge requirements where necessary, help decide what not to build, and turn the decisions into clear technical direction
  • Design, communicate and execute a vision in collaboration with the wider organisation
  • Contribute to all tiers of our architecture to produce high-quality and robust user experiences
  • Mentor engineers across all levels and contribute to a culture of continuous learning and engineering best practices

The ideal candidate has:

  • Driven technical strategy and alignment across multiple teams as a principal engineer or equivalent
  • Measured success by user and business outcomes, not only uptime and latency
  • Designed systems to ensure testability, reliability, and observability at cloud scale
  • Shaped a product roadmap or influenced prioritisation, not just delivered against one
  • Led data modelling decisions for complex domains, grounded in user and business impact, that adapted as requirements changed
  • Deep expertise in at least one database technology (we use Neo4j, MySQL, Snowflake, and OpenSearch)
  • Worked extensively with microservices, APIs, and related standards such as REST, HTTP, and OAuth

  • A modern office environment designed for you, empowering you to bring your best 
  • Investment in your professional growth and development enabling you to thrive in our community 
  • Mandate to accelerate progress, positively disrupt and create what happens next

  • An excellent range of benefits like private medical cover, a generous pension scheme, life assurance, income protection, plus loads of music industry perks. There’s also time off over winter break

At Sony Music Entertainment, we fuel the creative journey. We’ve played a pioneering role in music history, from the first-ever music label to the invention of the flat disc record. We’ve nurtured some of music’s most iconic artists and produced some of the most influential recordings of all time.

From our position at the intersection of music, entertainment, and technology, we bring imagination and expertise to the newest products and platforms, embrace new business models, employ breakthrough tools, and provide powerful insights that help our artists push creative boundaries and reach new audiences. job.description:
Job Title

Director, Talent Development

Job Description

Position Summary

The Director, Talent Development is a strategic, hands-on learning and talent leader responsible for designing, delivering, and continuously improving high-impact development experiences across People Inc.. Reporting to the VP, Talent Development, this role partners closely with HR Business Partners, and business leaders, to translate business priorities into practical, engaging, and measurable learning and talent solutions.

The Director will help strengthen manager capability, employee growth, leadership pipelines, and a culture of continuous learning. The ideal candidate brings strong business acumen, excellent facilitation presence, modern learning-design expertise, and a demonstrated ability to execute enterprise-wide talent and development initiatives in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.


This position is hybrid in-office, with the ability to work remotely for up to 2 days per week.


Essential Job Functions

Weight % - Accountabilities, Actions and Expected Measurable Results

Learning Strategy, Program Design, and Facilitation — 40%

  • Design, develop, facilitate, and evaluate learning programs, workshops, leadership offsites, cohort-based experiences, and virtual learning solutions for employees, managers, and leaders.
  • Lead engaging, high-energy, inclusive facilitation for audiences at all levels, adapting delivery in real time based on participant needs, business context, and group dynamics.
  • Conduct needs assessments with HRBPs, leaders, and subject-matter experts to identify capability gaps, performance needs, and development opportunities.
  • Translate business priorities into clear learning objectives, practical curricula, participant materials, facilitator guides, toolkits, and reinforcement resources.
  • Build and evolve learning pathways for key populations, including early-career employees, new and experienced managers, high-potential talent, and senior leaders.
  • Create scalable learning experiences using a blended approach that may include instructor-led training, virtual workshops, on-demand content, peer learning, coaching, mentoring, and experiential development.
  • Apply adult learning principles, inclusive design practices, and sound instructional design methodology to ensure learning is relevant, accessible, engaging, and actionable.
  • Establish clear success measures for learning programs, including participation, learner feedback, knowledge or skill gain, behavior change, manager feedback, and business impact.

Talent Management and Leadership Development — 30%

  • Partner with the VP, Talent Development, HRBPs, and leaders to execute core talent management processes, including performance feedback, goal setting, midyear reviews, year-end reviews, 360-degree feedback, talent calibration, and development planning.
  • Lead the operational planning, communication, tools, resources, training, and stakeholder support required for successful performance management cycles.
  • Support the facilitation and ongoing refinement of the organization’s 9-box talent-review process, helping leaders calibrate performance and potential, identify development priorities, and create actionable follow-up plans.
  • Partner with the HRBP team and business leaders to identify high-potential talent, critical roles, readiness needs, and targeted development actions.
  • Support the design and delivery of succession-planning processes in partnership with the VP, Talent Development, including talent-pipeline development, successor readiness, and individual development planning.
  • Leverage internal or external coaching programs to strengthen manager effectiveness, leadership capability, and individual development.
  • Develop practical tools and resources that help leaders conduct high-quality career conversations, performance discussions, feedback conversations, and development planning.

Talent Consulting and Business Partnership — 20%

  • Serve as a trusted learning and talent development consultant to HRBPs and business leaders, helping diagnose needs and recommend appropriate solutions before escalation to the VP, Talent Development.
  • Partner with HRBPs to develop learning strategies for client groups that support organizational goals, career growth, manager capability, team effectiveness, and employee engagement.
  • Advise leaders on effective approaches to leadership development, change adoption, team dynamics, communication, feedback, influence, and emotional intelligence.
  • Collaborate with the Communications team to develop clear, compelling, and timely messaging that drives awareness, participation, and sustained engagement in learning opportunities.
  • Build productive relationships with internal stakeholders, external vendors, facilitators, coaches, and subject-matter experts.
  • Stay current on emerging learning, leadership development, and talent management practices; bring forward practical innovations that fit People Inc’s culture and business needs.

Learning Operations, Technology, and Measurement — 10%

  • Own and optimize the learning management system (LMS) to ensure an intuitive, well-organized, and engaging learner experience.
  • Curate and promote learning playlists, on-demand resources, and development content for employees and managers.
  • Expand and enhance the People Inc. onboarding experience to accelerate new-hire connection, productivity, and cultural integration.
  • Track participation, adoption, learner satisfaction, completion, and other key indicators; synthesize insights and recommend improvements.
  • Manage program plans, timelines, budgets, vendor relationships, and project communications to ensure high-quality delivery.

Minimum Qualifications and Job Requirements | All must be met to be considered

Education: Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Organizational Development, Business, Psychology, Education, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience will also be considered.


Experience / Specific Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Eight or more years of progressive experience in talent development, learning and development, organizational development, talent management, leadership development, or a related HR discipline.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and facilitating high-impact learning experiences for employees, managers, and/or senior leaders.
  • Proven ability to lead enterprise-wide learning, leadership-development, performance-management, or talent-management initiatives from concept through implementation and evaluation.
  • Experience partnering with HRBPs and business leaders to diagnose needs and develop practical, business-aligned development solutions.
  • Experience supporting talent reviews, succession planning, performance management, high-potential development, or other talent-management processes.
  • Strong knowledge of adult-learning principles, instructional design, facilitation methods, and learning evaluation.
  • Experience using learning technologies, including an LMS, virtual-learning platforms, and digital or on-demand learning resources.
  • Excellent written, verbal, presentation, facilitation, consulting, and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Demonstrated project-management ability, including the capacity to manage multiple priorities, stakeholders, timelines, and vendors in a fast-paced environment.

job.title: Senior Product Manager, Audience Lifecycle Tools
job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide. 

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Intro to Position

NPR is scaling and maturing our audience engagement practice into a unified, data-driven, cross-platform growth and engagement engine, and lifecycle management is at the center of that transformation. This role owns the lifecycle activation tools, with a mandate to replace manual, campaign-by-campaign execution with scalable, AI-enabled (where appropriate) processes, and their work focuses on key touchpoints of engagement such as email acquisition, repeat engagement and donation conversion/retention. This role works in daily partnership with Data, Editorial, Marketing, Design, Engineering and Product teams with a mission to make every relationship touchpoint personalized, measurable, user-friendly and tied to business outcomes.

This is a union-represented role covered under the terms of a collective bargaining agreement with NABET-CWA DMU. 

Responsibilities

  • Product Strategy & Roadmap Ownership: Lead the product roadmap for NPR's audience lifecycle and martech ecosystem (including Piano.io and Salesforce Marketing Cloud), translating stakeholder requirements into prioritized engineering backlogs.
  • Martech Operationalization & Tooling: Build, configure, and operationalize internal-facing audience activation tools, establishing intuitive self-serve processes, user permissions, and governance guardrails for content and marketing leads.
  • Audience Journey Optimization: Partner with cross-divisional teams to design scalable automation rules and capabilities that enhance the full listener journey—from email discovery and content re-engagement to recurring donation conversion and win-back.
  • Data Integration & Measurement Alignment: Collaborate with Data and Analytics teams to enhance customer data platform (CDP) segmentation, tracking taxonomy, and attribution modeling to measure the direct impact of activation campaigns.
  • Newsletter Product Infrastructure: Drive technical development and platform enhancements for the NPR editorial newsletter suite in close coordination with newsroom and product leadership.
  • AI & Workflow Efficiency Integration: Evaluate and deploy practical, responsible AI and automation capabilities within lifecycle workflows to minimize repetitive manual execution.
  • Diverse Audience Engagement: Support audience diversification goals by designing personalization and segmentation workflows that welcome and sustain cross-generational and diverse audiences across digital touchpoints.
  • Standard Operating Procedures & Enablement: Author product documentation, establish lifecycle governance best practices, and conduct internal training sessions to ensure cross-departmental adoption of activation tools.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

Minimum Qualifications 

  • 3+ years of digital product management experience managing complex platforms, with a track record of driving measurable business or audience outcomes.
  • Substantive experience managing enterprise marketing automation platforms, customer data platforms (CDPs), or audience lifecycle suites (e.g., Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Piano.io, Braze, Segment).
  • Demonstrated experience translating complex cross-departmental requirements into structured user stories, technical specifications, and prioritized roadmaps.
  • Proven track record leading technical software migrations, vendor integrations, or enterprise tooling rollouts.
  • Strong background in data-informed product development, including experience with digital analytics, cohort tracking, and structured A/B testing.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior experience within a media organization, digital publishing company, non-profit, or subscription/membership-driven enterprise.
  • Practical experience implementing AI-enabled automation or algorithmic segmentation within marketing workflows.
  • Familiarity with user privacy regulations, consent frameworks, and modern consumer data compliance standards.

Required Skills/Competencies

  • Systems Thinking: Ability to synthesize inputs from across a federated matrix of stakeholders into a coherent product architecture and execution plan.
  • Internal Tool & Platform Enablement: Deep empathy for internal users, balancing self-service flexibility with structured organizational guardrails.
  • Data Literacy & Attribution: Fluency in customer segmentation logic, data pipelines, retention funnels, and performance reporting.
  • Cross-Functional Influence: Superior written and oral presentation skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical partners.
  • Iterative Problem Solving: Ability to prioritize high-leverage product enhancements and maintain roadmaps through periods of organizational or technical evolution.

Education Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Administration, Marketing, or related field, OR equivalent practical work experience demonstrating equivalent technical and product management capability.

Work Location & Requirements

  • NPR Remote-Permitted: This is a remote-permitted role. This role is based out of our Washington, D.C. office, but the employee may choose to work on a remote basis from a location that NPR approves. You will have the option of working (a) remotely from a location of your choosing within the United States that is supported by NPR; (b) on-site at an NPR facility, based on the availability of desks and approval from NPR; or (c) a combination of both. Regardless of where you choose to work from, you may be expected to travel to other locations from time to time to perform the duties of your position.

Job Type

  • This is a full-time, exempt position.

Compensation

Salary Range: The U.S.-based anticipated salary range for this opportunity is $132,915.86  - $151,852.82 plus benefits. The range displayed reflects the minimum and maximum salaries NPR expects to provide for new hires for the position across all US locations.

NPR Benefits: NPR provides comprehensive benefits for employees and dependents. Regular, full-time employees scheduled to work 30 hours or more per week are eligible to enroll in NPR’s benefits options. Benefits include access to health and wellness, paid time off, and financial well-being. Plan options include medical, dental, vision, life/ accidental death and dismemberment, long-term disability, short-term disability, and voluntary retirement savings to all eligible NPR employees.

  • Actively participate in campaign planning activities, including but not limited to defining the marketing objectives for each campaign, creating and managing project plans with clearly defined deliverables and resources, defining success criteria and KPIs and providing insights to inform campaign activities.

Experience in marketing operations, program coordination, business operations, executive support, PMO, who enjoy bringing structure, organization and executional excellence to complex regional teams

job.title: Fact Checker, Shows
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times Shows department is hiring a staff editor to fact check episodes of Hard Fork, both in video and audio formats.

You will work with producers and editors to check facts and assertions, with extra attention to the tone and context in which they're delivered.

You are comfortable working in print, audio and video mediums in a fast-paced news environment. We're looking for exceptional news judgment, an investigator's mind and the ability to dive into unfamiliar material on deadline. And while we value deliberate, careful checking, speed is also important. The fact checker will be part of a small group of producers and editors, so collegiality, diplomacy and a collaborative spirit are a must.

This is a part-time role for 20 hours a week to start. It could scale up over time. You will report to the Executive Producer of Hard Fork.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Check factual assertions in podcast and video episodes to determine veracity and correctness on deadline
  • Check prep documents and listen during live recordings to track facts and assertions to be verified
  • Listen to drafts, checking all facts, noting attribution, and providing guidance on editing or adjusting material as needed
  • Conduct quick and accurate research to gather and verify facts in collaboration with producers, editors and hosts
  • Work to ensure fairness and accuracy; correct contradictions and omissions in consultation with producers, editors and hosts; correct spelling and grammar
  • Check episode descriptions and other copy for video and audio assets. Adjust show print excerpts, transcripts and captions for factual accuracy
  • Check video episode's visuals for factual accuracy and context
  • Exercise news judgment
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3 or more years of fact-checking experience
  • Available to work evenings as needed

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Exercise news judgment
  • Quickly identify facts to be checked in a podcast episode transcript
  • Communicate notes & feedback clearly
  • Superb research skills
  • Use data to inform decisions
  • Manage deadlines simultaneously
  • Well-developed and adaptive cultural competence and emotional intelligence
  • Experience in a deadline-driven environment
  • Experience fact checking audio or video products

job.title: Customer Support Specialist
job.description:
We are UMG, the Universal Music Group. We are the world’s leading music company. In everything we do, we are committed to artistry, innovation and entrepreneurship. We own and operate a broad array of businesses engaged in recorded music, music publishing, merchandising, and audiovisual content in more than 60 countries. We identify and develop recording artists and songwriters, and we produce, distribute and promote the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful music to delight and entertain fans around the world.
 

CD Baby is the world’s largest digital distribution platform for independent artists. For more than 20 years, we’ve empowered creators to release their music to Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, Amazon Music, Instagram, TikTok, and 150+ other platforms worldwide—paying out nearly $1 billion in earnings directly to independent artists.


Built by artists, for artists, we’re a mission-driven, artist-first company, and we’re expanding our Support team with experienced, detail-oriented problem-solvers who care deeply about helping creators succeed.


How we LEAD:

As a Customer Support Specialist, you’ll handle our most complex support inquiries, serving as an escalation point for high-impact issues involving royalties, metadata, distribution workflows, rights management, account configuration, and platform compliance.


You’ll be an expert in the independent music ecosystem and CD Baby’s product suite, capable of diagnosing nuanced, multi-layered problems and communicating solutions clearly and empathetically.


You’ll report to our Customer Support Manager, and work closely with the rest of the Customer Support team and cross-functional partners to improve workflows, provide insights, and elevate the overall quality and consistency of the CD Baby artist experience.


How You’ll CREATE:

Expert Support & Escalation Handling

  • Manage complex customer cases, including advanced revenue issues, delivery failures, content policy blocks, and technical issues.
  • Troubleshoot multi-product, multi-stakeholder issues requiring deep system knowledge and cross-team coordination.
  • Provide accurate, timely, empathetic email support that upholds CD Baby’s artist-first values.
  • Maintain expert-level knowledge of CD Baby’s products, distribution pipelines, publishing, copyright, monetization, and related industry topics.
  • Communicate with professionalism, clarity, and empathy in every interaction.

Operational & Process Improvement

  • Identify recurring issues, workflow gaps, and opportunities for automation or simplification.
  • Surface actionable insights to the Customer Support Manager, CX Operations Manager, and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Contribute to improving policies, SOPs, and troubleshooting frameworks.

Knowledge & Documentation

  • Maintain expert-level knowledge of CD Baby’s distribution pipelines, monetization, and digital service provider (DSP) requirements.
  • Collaborate on updates to macros, internal SOPs, and customer-facing documentation to ensure clarity and accuracy.
  • Contribute to support documentation and internal resources (macros, SOPs, training guides).

Cross-functional Collaboration

  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Digital Operations, and Marketing to resolve escalations that involve system bugs, content policy questions, or distribution exceptions.
  • Participate in case reviews and knowledge-sharing sessions to strengthen Support team expertise.
  • Provide insight into recurring customer pain points, workflow gaps, product issues, and documentation needs.

Customer Experience Leadership

  • Model best-in-class communication standards across empathy, clarity, tone, and personalization.
  • Mentor associates through shadowing, pairing, and informal guidance as needed.
  • Help uphold a culture of continuous learning, artist advocacy, and operational excellence.
  • Collaborate with the Customer Support Manager on quality assurance, training opportunities, and improvements to customer experience.

Bring your VIBE:

  • 2–4 years experience in customer support, operations, or technical troubleshooting—preferably in music, tech, SaaS, or digital media.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to break down complex issues into clear next steps.
  • Exceptional written communication—concise, empathetic, and tailored to artist needs.
  • Familiarity with digital music distribution, publishing, copyright, royalties, or DSP ecosystems (a strong plus).
  • Comfort working in ticketing systems and internal tooling (e.g., Zendesk, Jira, CRM platforms).
  • Detail-oriented, organized, and able to thrive in a fast-paced, high-volume environment.
  • A passion for helping independent artists succeed and a deep respect for the artist community.

Join an entrepreneurial, global organization where authenticity, boldness, creativity, connection, drive, and insight aren’t just values—they’re how we work every day. Here are some of the ways we support you along the way (and just a few of the benefits we offer):

  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage

  • Including 100% coverage for out-patient in-network mental health services

job.title: Senior Customer Service Agent, NYT Wirecutter (Temporary)
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

Wirecutter, a New York Times company, is the premier product recommendation service dedicated to rigorously testing and reviewing products to help readers make the best decisions for their lives. Building on our mission of trust and utility, the Wirecutter Store (wirecutterstore.nytimes.com) is our dedicated e-commerce destination, offering our audience for purchase a highly-curated selection of the exceptional products we recommend.

 

As we approach our busiest time of the year (Q4/Holiday Season), we are looking for two experienced Senior Temporary Customer Service Agents to join our team. You will be the customer-facing voice of the Wirecutter Store. You will ensure that our customers receive the same level of care, clarity, and reliability that they expect from Wirecutter's editorial recommendations.

 

You will report directly to the Ecommerce Operations Director. You will work with our Customer Experience Manager to resolve inquiries, refine support processes, and improve our helpdesk operations during the peak holiday shopping rush.

 

Schedule and Hours:

  • Base Hours: Up to 20 hours per business week.

  • Peak Season: An additional 10 hours on weekends during peak periods.

  • Available Shifts (subject to change):

    • Shift A: 9:00 AM – 1:00 PM

    • Shift B: 1:00 PM – 5:00 PM

 

Responsibilities:

  • You will provide customer support across our primary communication channels: email and chat.

  • You will manage inquiries coming through our email and AI chat systems, providing rapid, real-time responses to customers and take over complex issues that require a human touch.

  • You will resolve inquiries regarding order status, product information, shipping, and returns.

  • You will process returns using Loop Returns, ensuring accurate refunds and inventory tracking.

  • You will guide communication between the store and our external supply partners, investigating and escalating complex fulfillment, shipping, or product inquiries to ensure rapid resolution for the customer.

  • You will navigate and use our ecommerce tech platforms at an expert level, specifically Shopify, Gorgias (including live chat and AI automation features), and Loop Returns.

  • You will collaborate with the Customer Experience Manager to identify trending customer issues and suggest operational improvements.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

 

Basic Qualifications:

  • At least 5 years, as a senior or lead customer service representative.

  • Communication & Speed: at least 5 years of experience interpreting and responding to customer requests with impeccable grammar and empathy. Must respond quickly to live chat inquiries without sacrificing quality.

  • Technical Expertise: at least 2 years of experience with Shopify, Gorgias, and Loop Returns.

  • AI Chat & System Optimization: at least 1 year of experience working with AI chat tools, managing live chat queues, creating macros, configuring auto-responses, and performing advanced administrative tasks within Gorgias.

  • Work Environment: at least 3 years of experience in a high-volume retail environment, meeting strict response time expectations during peak season.

  • Location Flexibility: You will work in-office during the Monday–Friday business week, with the flexibility to work from home on weekends during peak volume weeks.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 3 years of experience working with drop-ship retailers.

job.title: Programming Coordinator
job.description:
At Corus Entertainment, we’re shaping the future of media in Canada—home to the country’s biggest hits, most trusted news, and greatest value. Our mission is simple: to create engaging content, connect with audiences wherever they are, and drive meaningful growth.

Guided by our values—Think Boldly, Make a Positive Impact, Win as a Team, and Own the Outcome—we bring creativity and collaboration to everything we do.

If you’re ready to make an impact, there’s a place for you at Corus.

Division: Programming & Multiplatform

Work Status: Full-Time

Location: Toronto, Ontario (Hybrid)

About the Role

Reporting to the Manager, Programming, the Programming Coordinator provides operational and administrative support across content scheduling, planning, inventory management, regulatory reporting, and content operations.

This role plays an important part in supporting the day-to-day execution of programming activities across Corus' portfolio of channels and digital platforms. The successful candidate will work closely with Programming Managers, Program Schedulers, Acquisitions, Sales and other internal stakeholders to ensure programming information, schedules, inventories, and reports are maintained accurately and efficiently.

You will contribute by:

• Support the planning and scheduling activities across a portfolio of channels.

• Assist with monthly movie planning, scheduling preparation, and inventory management.

• Prepare and process program transfer forms and schedule adjustment requests.

• Support Program Schedulers with weekly listings, PROL updates, and other scheduling activities as required.

• Assist with special scheduling initiatives, stunts, marathons, and seasonal programming events.

• Maintain programming inventories and monitor content availability.

• Track content commitments and output deals in partnership with the Manager.

• Circulate output deal information and programming updates to internal stakeholders.

• Conduct inventory analysis and reporting to support programming decisions.

• Assist with on-demand content tracking and availability management.

• Coordinate monthly CRTC reporting requirements.

• Prepare and distribute ratings reports and audience performance packages.

• Maintain programming documentation, records, and internal reporting materials.

• Maintain the master viewer advisory list.

• Coordinate updates with Programming, Traffic, and Scheduling teams to ensure advisories remain accurate and current.

• Prepare presentations, reports, and planning materials as required.

• Support special projects and departmental initiatives.

• Assist the Programming team with ad hoc operational tasks as required.

Skills and experience you will bring:

• Post-secondary education in Broadcasting, Communications, Media Studies, Business Administration, or a related field.

• 1-3 years of experience in broadcasting, media, content operations, scheduling, or a related environment.

• Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.

• Experience working with scheduling, broadcast, or content management systems is an asset.

• Familiarity with television scheduling, programming operations, or digital media environments is preferred.

• Knowledge of CRTC regulations and reporting requirements is considered an asset.

• Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy.

• Strong organizational and time management skills.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.

• Effective written and verbal communication skills.

Application deadline: October 23, 2026
