Senior Software Engineer, Smart TV/CTV 

 

Location: New York / Los Angeles / San Francisco / Ft. Lauderdale


Overview


You’ll build and ship Paramount’s Smart TV applications across Samsung Tizen, LG webOS, and other CTV
platforms. These apps run on web-based runtimes with tight memory budgets, limited CPU, and hardware that
varies by model year and price point. You’ll write React and TypeScript that performs within those constraints.
You’ll own features from concept through certification. You’ll work with central video engineering, external
platform partners, and Product/Design to deliver what millions of viewers see on the biggest screen in the
house.


Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and maintain application components for Paramount’s Smart TV apps using React and
    TypeScript
  • Optimize application performance on resource-constrained CTV devices. Profile rendering, measure
    memory, fix what’s slow
  • Collaborate with central video engineering teams to integrate and optimize video players across platforms
  • Work with external platform partners (Samsung, LG, and others) to develop, debug, and certify
    applications
  • Manage application state with Redux and RTK. Keep the store clean and selectors fast as the app grows
  • Write clean, tested code and participate in code reviews. Hold your teammates to the same standard
  • Coordinate with Product, Design, and Backend Engineering to turn requirements into working features
  • Work across multiple agile teams and contribute to all phases of the development cycle
  • Improve CI/CD pipelines and testing infrastructure for multi-platform Smart TV deployments
  • Document components, platform-specific patterns, and technical decisions
  • Use AI development tools to move faster and share what works with the team

 

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years writing software
  • 2+ years building Smart TV or CTV applications on web-based platforms (Tizen, webOS, or similar)
  • BS in Computer Science, a related field, or equivalent work experience
  • React and TypeScript. You build components, not just consume them
  • State management with Redux and RTK. You understand store shape, middleware, and when selectors
    cause unnecessary re-renders
  • Client-side routing patterns (React Router or equivalent)
  • Front-end fundamentals: HTML, CSS, modern JavaScript. You can debug layout and rendering issues on
    a TV runtime
  • You’ve taken features from concept through delivery on CTV platforms, including certification
  • CI/CD environments with DevOps and SRE principles
  • RESTful API integration and data handling
  • You communicate technical decisions in writing and in conversation. People act on what you say because
    it’s clear
  • You use AI tools (Copilot, Claude, Cursor, or similar) to write and ship code faster

 

Desired Qualifications

  • Experience with multiple CTV platforms (Tizen, webOS, Vizio, Xbox, PlayStation, or others)
  • Performance optimization on TV devices: profiling, memory measurement, rendering analysis. You know
    how to find the bottleneck, not just guess
  • Browser internals knowledge: rendering pipelines, compositing, layout thrashing, and how these behave
    on TV runtimes vs. desktop browsers
  • Video player integration experience (Shaka, hls.js, or native platform players)
  • Observability tools: Conviva, New Relic, Datadog, Sentry, or similar
  • Experience working in Agile frameworks across distributed teams and time zones
  • Rapid proof-of-concept experience. You’ve built throwaway prototypes to answer hard questions fast
  • Enthusiasm for sharing AI tools and workflows that save the team time
  • You care about UX on the 10-foot screen and you’ll push back when something isn’t right
  • You say “I don’t know” when you don’t know

 

What Good Looks Like

  • You open a Smart TV codebase you’ve never seen, connect a Tizen emulator, and start diagnosing a
    rendering issue the same afternoon
  • Other engineers read your code and understand it without a walkthrough
  • You spot a memory leak on a 2020-era LG TV before QA files a ticket. You fix it and write up what
    happened
  • When a certification submission fails, you read the rejection, fix the issue, and flag what the team should
    check next time
  • You own your features end to end. From scoping through deployment, you don’t wait for someone to tell
    you what’s next
  • You know which React patterns cause jank on low-end CTV hardware. You avoid them and explain why to
    teammates who ask
  • You push back when a plan has gaps. You suggest a better approach
  • You treat the build pipeline, test coverage, and error monitoring like product features
  • You help your teammates get better. Through code reviews, pairing, or writing things down so the next
    person doesn’t hit the same wall

Paramount+, a direct-to-consumer digital subscription video on-demand and live streaming service from Paramount Global, combines live sports, breaking news, and a mountain of entertainment. The premium streaming service features an expansive library of original series, hit shows and popular movies across every genre from world-renowned brands and production studios, including BET, CBS, Comedy Central, MTV, Nickelodeon, Paramount Pictures and the Smithsonian Channel. The service is also the streaming home to unmatched sports programming, including every CBS Sports event, from golf to football to basketball and more, plus exclusive streaming rights for major sports properties, including some of the world’s biggest and most popular soccer leagues. Paramount+ also enables subscribers to stream local CBS stations live across the U.S. in addition to the ability to stream Paramount Streaming’s other live channels: CBSN for 24/7 news, CBS Sports HQ for sports news and analysis, and ET Live for entertainment coverage.

job.description:
Storytelling is, and will always be, the heart of what we do at Skydance.
Our vision is to build a thriving entertainment ecosystem where stories and worlds are imagined, brought to life and experienced. We create for every age and audience, anchored by the strength of our content and experiences and the depth of our connection with fans. We are creator-first, audience-focused, tech-forward, globally scaled.

 

Here, you’ll work with talented teams that move fast, think boldly and collaborate with purpose to deliver results. We aim high, champion the best ideas and win together, earning the trust of our employees, creators, partners and audiences every day.

 

If you’re energized by the opportunity to help build the next-generation global media and entertainment company powered by creativity and technology, we’d be thrilled to welcome you aboard. LET’S GO!

 

SENIOR SOFTWARE ENGINEER — ROKU

 

Location: On-Site - New York / Los Angeles / San Francisco / Ft. Lauderdale

 

ABOUT THE ROLE

 

You'll build and ship the Paramount+ Roku application used by millions of viewers. The Roku platform has constraints other platforms don't: tight memory budgets, a single-threaded render loop, device hardware that ranges from flagship to five years old. You'll solve problems inside those constraints.

 

We write software that's simple to read, cheap to maintain, and built to last. You'll own features from design through deployment, work across agile teams, and help other engineers get better at this work.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 

• Design, build, and maintain core Roku framework components and application features for Paramount+

• Architect around Roku's constraints: memory limits, render-thread/task-thread boundaries, device performance tiers, and certification requirements

• Use RSG 1.3 data transfer APIs, BrightScript Memory Monitor, and Perfetto tracing to find and fix performance problems before users hit them

• Build real-time personalization and engagement features — personalized recommendations, dynamic artwork, ad engagement — within Roku's memory and performance budgets

• Write clear documentation for components, architecture decisions, and platform-specific patterns

• Measure and improve application performance and stability through instrumentation and observability

• Work across agile teams and coordinate with backend engineering and DevOps/SRE on service builds and deploys

• Review code, pair with teammates, and raise the quality bar across the team

• Maintain and improve CI/CD pipelines and testing infrastructure

• Design and run A/B tests, then act on what the data says

• Use AI development tools to move faster and share what works with the team

 

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 

• 6+ years writing software

• 3+ years building Roku applications

• BS in Computer Science, a related field, or equivalent work experience

• You know OOP, data structures, and algorithms well enough to design systems, not just pass interviews

• BrightScript and SceneGraph SDK, including RSG 1.3

• You can explain Roku's memory model, the render-thread/task-thread split, device tiers, and what certification requires

• RESTful API design and data serialization

• Roku frameworks and services: RAF, RMF, RokuPay

• Unit and integration testing on Roku

• HTTP protocol and caching behavior

• Git and GitHub

• You write and speak about technical decisions in a way that helps people act on them

• You use AI tools (Copilot, Claude, Cursor, or similar) to write and ship code faster

 

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 

• BrighterScript and Roku community tooling (ropm, bslint, roku-debug)

• Other OTT platforms: Fire TV, Android TV, Apple TV, Samsung TV, LG webOS

• Observability tools: Conviva, New Relic, Datadog, Sentry

• Microservices and backend-for-frontend patterns

• You've worked with personalization or recommendation APIs on resource-constrained devices

• E2E testing for connected-device applications

• Docker and CI/CD tooling (Jenkins or similar)

• GraphQL

• You share AI tools and workflows that save the team time

• You care about UX enough to push back on Product and Design when something isn't right

• You say "I don't know" when you don't know

• You've worked across time zones without waiting for meetings to unblock you

 

WHAT GOOD LOOKS LIKE

 

• You open a 200-file BrightScript repo you've never seen and start making changes the same day

• Other engineers read your code and understand it without a walkthrough

• You notice a memory spike on a Roku Express before QA files a ticket. You fix it and write up what happened

• You track Roku OS releases and adopt new APIs when they solve a real problem, not because they're new

• You write architecture docs, component guides, and Slack explanations that save ten people from asking the same question

• You push back when a plan has gaps. You suggest a better one

• You treat the build pipeline, test coverage, and error monitoring like product features

• You make the people around you better at their jobs

job.title: Visual Journalist
job.description:
Bring stories to life in a fast-moving, digital-first newsroom. As a visual journalist at McClatchy, you’ll shape how our diverse and growing community sees itself—capturing moments, people and issues with photography and video that matter to our readers. You’ll work across formats, from original assignments to short-form verticals and multi-format versions of existing reporting, using company-provided tools that streamline production and let you focus on what counts: impactful storytelling.

You’ll pitch and develop your own visual story ideas, respond to breaking news and deliver timely, accurate and ethically captured photo and video content. Our visual journalists are audience-first, using analytics and feedback to inform coverage and drive growth. You’ll work with Nikon gear and the Adobe suite, and you’ll be expected to write clean, compelling captions and headlines that help your work get discovered and shared. job.title: Senior Analyst, Newsroom Data
job.description:
Job Description:


WSJ Newsroom | Senior Data Analyst (September 2026)

The Wall Street Journal is seeking a Senior Data Analyst to join our newsroom data team, reporting to the Senior Manager, Newsroom Analytics. You will work directly with editorial, audience, and product teams on the decisions that shape how our journalism is reported, prioritized, and delivered to readers.

This is a hands-on, high-autonomy role that blends strong analytical craft with sharp newsroom judgment. You will own the analyses, dashboards, and measurement frameworks the newsroom depends on, and see your work through from question to adopted decision. You will also help set the technical bar for the data team, mentoring more junior colleagues and strengthening our shared practices.

This position will be based in our New York office.

You will:

  • Serve as a trusted analytics partner to newsroom editorial and strategy leaders, driving audience growth, engagement and retention. Frame the right questions, answer them with rigorous analysis, and translate findings for non-technical stakeholders.

  • Develop and maintain centralized dashboards and automated reports that expand self-serve access to newsroom data.

  • Run deep-dive analyses on areas of opportunity, major news events, high-priority moments, and unexplained shifts in performance.

  • Push measurement forward by developing novel metrics and analytical frameworks that inform newsroom strategy, and drive adoption across editorial, product, and business teams.

  • Own and maintain the reporting stack, partnering with data engineering and product to keep our data accurate, fresh, and high-quality, and to strengthen the taxonomies, instrumentation, and foundational datasets the newsroom relies on. Respond to and prevent pipeline incidents so daily reporting stays reliable.

  • Design and run A/B tests and experiments in partnership with strategy, product, and tech teams, applying statistical measurement to interpret results and translate them into decisions about editorial and audience strategy.

  • Mentor junior analysts, set shared standards for technical and non-technical outputs, and contribute to a shared library of methods and lessons the team can pull from.

You have:

  • 3+ years in data analytics, data science, or a related field, preferably in media, publishing, or content.

  • Track record of owning recurring reporting end-to-end and delivering analyses whose findings have shaped business decisions.

  • Strong SQL skills, with experience working in large-scale data warehouses like BigQuery or Snowflake, and analytics-engineering frameworks like dbt.

  • Experience designing and running A/B tests, and applying statistical methods to interpret results

  • Proficiency in Python for analysis, data wrangling, and automating analytical workflows, with experience  maintaining code in Git.

  • Strong communication skills, with a track record of driving alignment and consensus across cross-functional groups.

Standout candidates will have strengths in one or more of the following:

  • A background in content performance analysis, audience segmentation, cohort analysis, or editorial research.

  • Working knowledge of off-platform attribution, connecting distributed content and platform referrals to downstream engagement.

  • Comfort using AI/LLM tooling to speed up analytical workflows or make data more accessible to non-technical partners.

  • Prior newsroom experience with an interest in driving journalistic outcomes.

job.title: Global Member Services Representative
job.description:
About ASCAP

The American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers (ASCAP) is a membership association of more than one million songwriters, composers and music publishers, and represents some of the world’s most talented music creators. Founded and governed by songwriters, composers and publishers, it is the only performing rights organization in the U.S. that operates on a not-for-profit basis. ASCAP licenses a repertory of over 20 million musical works to hundreds of thousands of businesses that use music, including streaming services, cable television, radio and satellite radio and brick and mortar businesses such as retail stores, hotels, clubs, restaurants and bars. ASCAP collects the licensing fees; identifies, matches and processes trillions of performances every year; and returns nearly 90 cents of every dollar back to its members as royalties. The ASCAP blanket license offers an efficient solution for businesses to legally perform ASCAP music while respecting the right of songwriters and composers to be paid fairly. ASCAP puts music creators first, advocating for their rights and the value of music on Capitol Hill, driving innovation that moves the industry forward, building community and providing the resources and support that creators need to succeed in their careers. Learn more and stay in touch at www.ascap.com, on X and Instagram @ASCAP and on Facebook.

# # #

This is a hybrid position with currently a minimum 3 day per week in-office requirement, based out of the ASCAP New York Office.

      • Performance crediting

    • Use sound judgment to determine if claims need to be escalated

    • Liaise with other departments to seamlessly resolve Member issues

  • Excellent administrative, written, and verbal communication skills

job.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer
job.description:
Who We Are:

SiriusXM and its brands (Pandora, SiriusXM Media, AdsWizz, Simplecast, and SiriusXM Connect) are leading a new era of audio entertainment and services by delivering the most compelling subscription and ad-supported audio entertainment experience for listeners -- in the car, at home, and anywhere on the go with connected devices. Our vision is to shape the future of audio, where everyone can be effortlessly connected to the voices, stories and music they love wherever they are.

This is the place where a diverse group of emerging talent and legends alike come to share authentic and purposeful songs, stories, sounds and insights through some of the best programming and technology in the world. Our critically-acclaimed, industry-leading audio entertainment encompasses music, sports, comedy, news, talk, live events, and podcasting. No matter their individual role, each of our employees plays a vital part in bringing SiriusXM’s vision to life every day.

SiriusXM is the leading audio entertainment company in North America, and the premier programmer and platform for subscription and digital advertising-supported audio products. SiriusXM’s platforms collectively reach approximately 150 million listeners, the largest digital audio audience across paid and free tiers in North America, and deliver music, sports, talk, news, comedy, entertainment and podcasts. Pandora, a subsidiary of SiriusXM, is the largest ad-supported audio entertainment streaming service in the U.S. SiriusXM's subsidiaries Simplecast and AdsWizz make it a leader in podcast hosting, production, distribution, analytics and monetization. The Company’s advertising sales organization, which operates as SiriusXM Media, leverages its scale, cross-platform sales organization and ad tech capabilities to deliver results for audio creators and advertisers. SiriusXM, through SiriusXM Canada Holdings, Inc., also offers satellite radio and audio entertainment in Canada. In addition to its audio entertainment businesses, SiriusXM offers connected vehicle services to automakers.

How you'll make an impact:

As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer at SiriusXM, you will bring machine learning models from development and experimentation to reliable, scalable production systems. You will work closely with Data Scientists, Data Engineers, Platform Engineers, and Services teams to productionize models, build robust feature pipelines, and ensure models operate reliably in live environments. This is a hands-on engineering role with ownership across deployment, serving, monitoring, and lifecycle management of ML systems.

What you'll do:

Model Productionization and Deployment

  • Lead the deployment of ML models into production using Databricks and MLFlow, ensuring high performance and integration with existing systems.

  • Implement scalable and reliable model serving solutions (both batch and real-time).

  • Design and maintain CI/CD pipelines for automated build, test, validation, and deployment of ML artifacts.

  • Support safe rollout and rollback strategies across environments.

Feature Engineering and Serving

  • Translate feature definitions from data scientists into production-grade pipelines.

  • Build and maintain reliable feature serving systems to ensure consistency between training and inference environments.

  • Optimize feature pipelines for performance, maintainability, and scalability.

Model Lifecycle Management

  • Support model registration, versioning, publishing, and promotion.

  • Implement retraining pipelines and redeploy improved models as data and algorithms evolve.

  • Participate in the decommissioning and retirement of models.

Reliability, Observability, and Performance

  • Ensure production models meet latency, throughput, and reliability requirements.

  • Implement logging, monitoring, and alerting of ML systems.

  • Investigate and resolve issues related to model performance, deployments, and infrastructure.

  • Contribute to operational runbooks and documentation.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with data scientists, engineers, and other stakeholders, providing ML engineering and operations expertise and support.

Best Practices Implementation

  • Spearhead the adoption of industry best practices in ML engineering and operations, focusing on areas like version control, data governance, and resource optimization.

Problem Resolution

  • Identify and resolve complex issues in ML model performance, deployment, and operational workflows.

What you'll need:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.

  • 5+ years of experience in ML Engineering, MLOps, data engineering, or a similar role.

  • Working knowledge of ML models and algorithms.

  • 2+ years of experience with Databricks, MLFlow, and other relevant ML tools and frameworks.

  • Proficiency in programming languages such as Python, Scala, or Java.

  • Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, etc.) and containerization technologies (Docker, Kubernetes).

  • Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code tooling and practices, e.g., CDK, Terraform

  • Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills

Our goal at SiriusXM is to provide and maintain a work environment that fosters mutual respect, professionalism and cooperation. job.title: Assistant Editor, Visuals
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

We’re looking for a senior editor to lead our visual journalism across Asia, driving the execution of new forms of storytelling and overseeing a team of graphics and multimedia journalists. This role is based in the Times’ Seoul newsroom. 

Visual journalists at The Times have investigated how China built a great wall of villages along its frontier and strong-armed its way into dominating the South China Sea, documented the Myanmar military’s campaign of terror against its own people and Taliban rule in Afghanistan, and reconstructed South Korean president’s botched martial law bid. They have revealed how drones have transformed the war in Ukraine. They have also devised ambitious multimedia approaches to explain the far-reaching impact of the Iran war, air pollution in India and American households’ reliance on Chinese goods.

We want to do more of these kinds of stories. And we want to continue to transform how we work to bring visual reporting and editing into the core of how we show readers the world and hold power accountable. We will do this through compelling graphical explanations; urgent, immersive field reporting in photography and video; sharp visual news coverage; and investigations driven by deep reporting on imagery and data.

This role reports to the assistant international editor for visuals in New York and collaborates with the Asia editor to help drive coverage of Asia. You will work closely with the lead video producer and photo editor in Seoul, the senior editor for visuals in London, and counterparts in photo, video, graphics and news design.

This is an in-office position based in Seoul,  and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Main responsibilities:

  • Collaborate with international editors to drive visual coverage of Asia. 
  • Coordinate, lead and edit the work of correspondents and visual journalists on visual stories.
  • Serve as the leader of a small group of graphics/multimedia reporters focused on Asia, helping to create, design and edit multimedia coverage. 
  • In collaboration with the deputy International editor for visuals, plan and execute stories that use data analysis and visualization, photography, imagery analysis, open source investigation and other reporting techniques.
  • Work with desk leaders to shape and execute our broader editorial strategy for visual journalism, including how we should work with partners in photo, video, graphics and news design.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the assistant international editor for visuals.

Basic qualifications:

  • Strong news judgment.
  • Ability to identify and conceive ambitious stories, spot visual opportunities in reporting and develop them into a range of compelling visual forms.
  • Skill pulling multiple visual disciplines together into multimedia projects, with an emphasis on visualization, explanatory visuals, digital design, use of video and other visual forms. 
  • A record of clear communication and strong collaboration with colleagues.
  • The ability to write clearly, work on tight deadlines and edit to sharpen the relationship between visuals and copy.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience leading multidisciplinary teams to create ambitious multimedia news stories, including interactive visuals, and help them develop as journalists. . 
  • Strong portfolio in one or more of these areas: data visualization, mapping, explanatory writing, news illustration, digital design, interactive development and explanatory multimedia or video.

In order to be considered for this role, please submit the link to your portfolio/clips.

job.title: Senior Podcast Producer (LA Times Studios)
job.description:
The L.A. Times Studios LLC vision is to be the premier studio for groundbreaking and impactful storytelling, setting high standards for excellence in content creation and production. We push the boundaries of traditional media, exploring new formats and platforms to reach diverse and global audiences. By championing innovative ideas and diverse voices, we aspire to create a more connected world through storytelling and events supported by robust revenue streams from advertising sales, branded content, event production, products and business development.

Join a team of creative, collaborative and innovative professionals, apply today using the link below.

The Senior Podcast Producer leads the planning, development, and execution of complex or high-priority content and production projects from concept through delivery. This role combines sound content judgment, creative direction, and production expertise to deliver accurate, engaging, high-quality content aligned with company objectives and audience needs. The Senior Producer is accountable for the content quality, production execution, and timely delivery of assigned projects and serves as the primary production decision-maker within established guidelines. This position manages production priorities, coordinates cross-functional resources, and resolves complex content and production issues independently, escalating matters that require leadership approval. The Senior Producer supervises assigned production staff, providing direction, coaching, and performance oversight to strengthen team capabilities and results.

Responsibilties:

• Lead complex or high-priority productions from concept through delivery, with accountability for content quality, execution, timelines, and effective use of approved resources and budgets.

• Develop and evaluate story ideas, formats, and creative approaches that align with company priorities and engage intended audiences; translate programming or business objectives into actionable production plans.

• Oversee research, scripts, outlines, and other production materials, providing final production-level review within delegated authority to ensure content is accurate, clear, compelling, and consistent with company standards.

• Direct production workflows and coordinate staff, talent, technical resources, and cross-functional partners; establish priorities, allocate approved resources, and resolve competing demands across concurrent projects.

• Serve as the primary production decision-maker for assigned projects, exercising independent judgment to resolve complex content and production challenges, adjust priorities, and escalate sensitive or high-impact issues that exceed delegated authority.

• Supervise assigned production staff, establishing performance and quality expectations, delegating work, coaching employees, and evaluating performance; participate in hiring and disciplinary actions in partnership with management and HR.

• Collaborate with distribution, marketing, and audience teams to adapt content across relevant platforms; evaluate performance against established objectives and implement improvements based on audience insights, content performance, and production results.

• Partner with leadership to develop future programming and production initiatives; recommend new formats, resource needs, and workflow improvements that increase production capacity, efficiency, and content quality.

• Other duties as assigned.

Requirements:

• 9+ years of progressively responsible experience in content production, media production, or a related field.

• 3+ years experience supervising production staff, including delegating assignments, coaching employees, evaluating performance, and addressing performance concerns.

• Demonstrated experience leading complex productions or multiple concurrent projects from concept through delivery, with accountability for quality, timelines, and production outcomes.

• Strong content judgment and demonstrated ability to make independent decisions involving sensitive subject matter, production risks, and competing priorities.

• Strong writing, storytelling, verbal communication, and creative direction skills.

• Experience coordinating talent, production staff, technical resources, and cross-functional partners, including setting priorities and resolving resource or workflow conflicts.

• Working knowledge of production workflows and tools relevant to the assigned content format.

• Knowledge of applicable content standards, editorial integrity, and quality-control practices.

• Ability to manage competing deadlines, resolve production issues, and adapt to changing priorities.

• Ability to work flexible schedules based on production requirements.

Preferred Qualifcations:

• Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Journalism, Media Studies, Film/Television Production, or a related field.

• Experience producing content across multiple formats or distribution platforms.

• Experience developing new content formats or programming initiatives.

• Experience managing production budgets and allocating resources.

• Experience using audience insights and performance metrics to improve content.

• Experience improving production workflows and developing production teams.

Additional Responsibilities

• Shape podcast episode formats, narrative arcs, interview approaches, and scripts in partnership with hosts, reporters, and editors.

• Direct studio, remote, and on-location podcast recordings, guiding host and guest performance and coordinating audio and video needs.

• Oversee podcast post-production, including audio editing, mixing, sound design, scoring, and coordination of video edits.

• Oversee episode publishing, including titles, descriptions, show notes, metadata, and release scheduling across podcast and video platforms.

Additional Requirements

• Demonstrated experience producing professional audio and video podcasts, including weekly, seasonal, or narrative series.

• Strong skills in podcast storytelling, interview development, host preparation, and script editing.

• Proficiency with Adobe Audition, Premiere Pro, Riverside, or comparable audio, video, and remote recording tools.

• Working knowledge of audio editing, mixing, sound design, and podcast delivery standards.

• Familiarity with podcast hosting, RSS feeds, and distribution through Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and YouTube.

• Knowledge of journalistic sourcing, fact-checking, and editorial review practices for news and investigative programming.

Additional Preferred Qualifications

• Experience developing and launching original podcast series.

• Experience producing investigative, documentary, or serialized narrative podcasts.

• Experience integrating sponsorships or branded segments while maintaining editorial standards and applicable disclosures.

• Familiarity with music and archival content permissions and podcast accessibility practices, including transcripts and captions.

job.title: Video Editor and Motion Designer, Temporary
job.description:
ProPublica is an independent, nonprofit newsroom that produces investigative journalism in the public interest. 

Applications will close on Monday, November 9, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET.

In 2024, ProPublica launched a short-form vertical video team to adapt our long-form investigative journalism for audiences on Instagram, TikTok and YouTube Shorts. Since then, the team has amassed nearly 65 million views. Now we’re building out the second phase of our social video strategy and have launched a new YouTube team dedicated to producing midlength adaptations for the platform.

We are looking for a video editor and motion designer who has a passion for accountability journalism and is excited by the opportunity to bring our reporting to an increasing number of viewers who treat YouTube as a platform to learn about the world around them.

In this role, you will work alongside video producers on the YouTube team and will own the creative and technical postproduction for several assigned videos a month. As this is a new team, you will also be a key part of building the workflows and best practices that make our YouTube video pipeline sustainable as well as creating the visual identity that helps to answer: What should ProPublica look and sound like on YouTube? 

The videos you help create for YouTube are meant to serve as standalone editorial products, and we’re looking for your platform-native expertise to drive experimentation that helps us learn quickly, adapt and deliver the most compelling storytelling formats while adhering to our rigorous editorial standards and practices. You should be comfortable working with reporters and editors across the newsroom as well as freelancers we’ll bring on to help with projects.

This is a temporary two-year role that will report to our director of multiplatform audience strategy. The YouTube team sits within the larger ProPublica audience team.

Essential responsibilities 

  • Collaborate with producers to create videos — and related promo cuts — that are grounded in ethical journalistic principles, standards and practices.
  • Use editorial judgment to translate investigations and video scripts with the sensitivity, care and appropriate tone they require.
  • Own the creative and technical postproduction for videos — editing, motion graphic design and animation, color grading and sound design — ensuring projects are shaped and paced for a YouTube-first audience.
  • Own end-to-end motion design workflows, including creating storyboards, animatics and the polished final products for videos.
  • Establish and maintain a central motion design library of MOGRTs, templates, toolkits and other reusable visual assets for teamwide use.
  • Maintain ProPublica’s brand standards and overall design system, collaborating with the design and graphics teams, among others, to ensure visual cohesiveness in videos.
  • Communicate proactively with the team regarding project status and timelines and directly collaborate with producers on scoping and delivering videos on schedule. 
  • Manage multiple projects in various stages of production, sometimes meeting tight deadlines.

About you

We are looking for candidates who have proven that they can use video editing and design skills for journalistic ends.

The ideal candidate will have these skills and attributes:

  • Four or more years of professional video editing and motion design experience in a newsroom, media organization or production studio. 
  • High proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite, with expert proficiency in both Adobe After Effects and Premiere Pro.
  • A portfolio that highlights videos you have edited specifically for YouTube, including hosted, vlog-style and/or explainer formats.
  • Experience building tension in hooks, controlling pacing and navigating tonal shifts in video storytelling. 
  • You are energized by the opportunity of being part of a founding team and creating something from scratch — establishing formats, defining visual languages and building efficient workflows. 
  • You thrive while collaborating, seeking input from others and iterating your work based on feedback. 

And many of these: 

  • Experience being part of a founding YouTube team or launching a new project initiative. 
  • Experience in on-site production, including shooting on professional camera equipment and knowledge of lighting and audio setups.
  • Experience with digital asset management and video archival workflows. 
  • Proficiency in Figma and Google Workspace.

This job is full time and includes benefits. ProPublica is based in New York, but we’re open to remote candidates. We have offices in New York City; Washington, D.C.; Atlanta; Chicago; Phoenix; and Berkeley, California. Applicants must be eligible to work in the U.S. and have the ability to travel, as necessary, for team meetings, training and video-related duties.

This role is subject to an in-office work requirement of two days per week in the New York City office. That requirement may be extended to other offices with 60 days’ notice. 

This job is covered under the terms of a collective bargaining agreement with The NewsGuild of New York, Local 31003, CWA, AFL-CIO.

The expected salary range for this position is $90,000 to $115,000.

This is a good-faith estimate of what we expect to pay for this position. The final salary figure will take into account a person’s experience, accomplishment and location. ProPublica is committed to paying its staff equitably, and these ranges should not be considered career salary limits or caps.

We will begin reviewing applications as we receive them, but we will continue to consider candidates as long as the posting remains live on our site.

Questions? Send an email to talent@propublica.org. 

No phone calls, please.

job.title: Machine Learning Engineer
job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking a Machine Learning Engineer to help build the next generation of AI-powered newsroom and product capabilities. As we expand into new sector products, new professional audiences and new geographies, POLITICO is investing in machine learning systems that go beyond simply integrating foundation models. This role will work alongside software engineers, product managers, journalists and editorial leadership to develop models, evaluation frameworks and data pipelines that apply POLITICO's editorial expertise across AI-powered tools and improve newsroom and product workflows.


The ideal candidate is excited about applying machine learning in support of journalism. You'll work closely with software engineers, journalists and product teams to develop AI-powered tools and data products that strengthen reporting, improve newsroom workflows and help bring POLITICO's editorial expertise to a broader audience.


What You'll Do:

  • Design, build and deploy production machine learning systems that support newsroom, editorial and new-audience initiatives.
  • Develop classification, prediction and ranking models using proprietary newsroom data and editorial expertise — a modeling foundation that extends across new products rather than requiring a bespoke build per vertical.
  • Build datasets, feature engineering pipelines and evaluation frameworks to improve AI system performance.
  • Experiment with prompting, retrieval, fine-tuning and other model adaptation techniques to solve journalism-specific problems.
  • Partner closely with journalists and editors to translate editorial knowledge into machine learning features, labels and evaluation criteria.
  • Collaborate with software engineers to integrate machine learning capabilities into production applications.
  • Measure and improve model quality using rigorous evaluation methodologies that balance accuracy, editorial standards and operational performance.
  • Evaluate new AI technologies while considering performance, cost, maintainability and long-term flexibility.

Example Projects:

You may work on initiatives such as:

  • Building systems that classify the newsworthiness of stories using editorial judgment.
  • Developing prediction models that combine public information with POLITICO's proprietary reporting expertise.
  • Improving AI-assisted editing by helping models better understand and apply POLITICO's editorial style guide.
  • Creating proprietary classifiers that enrich public datasets with editorial intelligence, extendable to new sector products as they launch.
  • Designing evaluation frameworks to measure AI quality before newsroom deployment.
  • Optimizing AI workflows to improve performance while reducing inference costs.
  • Supporting investigative and enterprise reporting through machine-learning-assisted analysis of complex datasets.

What You'll Need:

Required

  • 5+ years of professional experience building or deploying machine learning systems.
  • Strong software engineering skills, preferably in Python.
  • Experience with machine learning fundamentals including supervised learning, feature engineering, model evaluation and experimentation.
  • Experience with modern machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.
  • Familiarity with large language models, embeddings or natural language processing techniques.
  • Experience working with structured and unstructured data.
  • Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to collaborate with engineers, product managers and non-technical stakeholders.

Preferred

  • Experience adapting or fine-tuning foundation models.
  • Experience building NLP, information retrieval, classification or ranking systems.
  • Familiarity with model evaluation frameworks, experiment tracking or MLOps practices.
  • Experience deploying machine learning models to cloud infrastructure.
  • Interest in journalism, media, public policy or knowledge-intensive domains.

What Success Looks Like in the First Year:

  • Improve the accuracy and reliability of AI systems used by POLITICO's newsroom.
  • Build evaluation frameworks that help teams confidently assess AI quality and editorial alignment.
  • Contribute to proprietary classifiers, prediction systems and editorial intelligence capabilities that differentiate a named initiative.
  • Partner effectively with software engineers, product teams and newsroom stakeholders to bring machine learning solutions into production.
  • Help establish a strong technical foundation for future AI initiatives across the newsroom and our new lines of business.

COMPENSATION: $175,000 - $225,000 Annual Base. The final salary offered will be based on factors including relevant experience, skills, and qualifications.


We value our people. Click here for more on what we offer and what it’s like to work for POLITICO.

Let’s keep in touch. You can view our list of open positions here. We hope to see your application soon!


About Us. 

POLITICO illuminates the forces shaping global power. Since 2007, we have delivered intelligence that anticipates tomorrow's headlines, not reports on yesterday's news. As politics has increasingly become the defining force of our era, our work has never been more vital. 


Cabinet secretaries and Ministers start their mornings with our analysis. CEOs shape strategy around our reporting. Advocacy leaders rely on our insights to move policy. We deliver the straightforward facts and clear-eyed analysis they need to navigate the most complex political landscape of our lifetimes. 


Our 1,100+ publishing professionals across the world's key democratic capitals—Washington, Brussels, London, Paris, Berlin, Sacramento, and New York—form the world's premier politics and policy newsroom. We tell the story of how power really works by explaining who wields it and how they plan to exercise it, connecting dots others miss and delivering scoops from sources others don't even know exist. 


Innovation has always been a core tenet of our story. At launch, we bet that depth would trump scale, that talent would trump traffic, and that politics would become central to modern life. In 2011, we made another bet and launched POLITICO Pro to help decision-makers understand the business of government, transforming both how they shape government action and the business of journalism itself. 


These bets have made POLITICO the most successful digital news startup of its generation and the indispensable resource for leaders who shape the future. Today, we are a rarity in media: a growing, profitable, and sustainable news organization. 


POLITICO is a subsidiary of Axel Springer SE, a family-owned transatlantic media company headquartered in Berlin and New York. Axel Springer is dedicated to shaping the future of journalism in the free world, believing that a free and informed society is essential to democracy. The company’s guiding principles - first articulated as  The Essentials by founder Axel Springer in the aftermath of World War II - remain a cornerstone of the company’s foundation today. Learn more about Axel Springer.

Based at our Arlington, Virginia headquarters and reporting to the CFO, you will lead our Global Accounting Team (US and European). This highly visible role will be responsible for ensuring the integrity, accuracy, and scalability of POLITICO’s financial operations across our growing global organization. The ideal candidate brings deep technical accounting expertise combined with strong business judgment and a modern, forward-looking approach to finance—someone who can strengthen controls and processes, develop a high-performing global team, and build the financial infrastructure needed to support POLITICO’s continued growth and evolving business.


Who You Are:

  • A strategic finance leader and trusted advisor who can translate complex accounting and financial matters into clear insights, recommendations, and decisions for senior leadership.
  • A strong technical accounting expert with deep knowledge of financial reporting, controls, audit, compliance, and accounting policy across a complex, multi-entity organization.
  • A hands-on operator and transformation leader who can balance day-to-day execution with opportunities to simplify, automate, and scale global finance processes.
  • A collaborative global leader who builds strong partnerships across Finance and the broader business and can effectively navigate different entities, markets, and regulatory environments.
  • A developer of high-performing teams who establishes clear accountability, develops talent, and creates a culture of accuracy, partnership, and continuous improvement.

What You’ll Do:

  • Lead the global close and IFRS consolidation for group reporting, with operational accounting delivered through our regional Controllers.
  • Set accounting policy and be the final voice on complex judgments, including subscription revenue recognition.
  • Lead statutory reporting and filings in every jurisdiction in which POLITICO operates, in partnership with our external accountants.
  • Own the financial governance and control framework (ICFR), and serve as the main contact for external auditors and Internal Audit.
  • Oversee tax accounting, transfer pricing and indirect tax compliance with external tax advisers.
  • Partner with tax and legal on international structure, entity set-up, and the financial unwinding, liquidation or roll-up of legacy and redundant entities.
  • Support acquisitions end to end, from financial due diligence and quality of earnings through to post-deal integration.
  • Lead purchase accounting, including purchase price allocation, valuation of identifiable intangibles and annual goodwill impairment testing.
  • Lead the accounting for disposals and restructurings, including carve-out financials and discontinued operations.
  • Drive automation of finance processes in Workday and the order-to-cash flow from Salesforce through to the ledger.
  • Build and develop the global accounting team, set clear accountabilities, and define how we measure the function’s success.

What You’ll Need:

Required

  • 15+ years of progressive accounting experience at an international group, including several years as a regional or global Controller.
  • A professional accounting qualification (CPA, ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent) and a degree in accounting, finance or a related field.
  • Strong understanding of the accounting principles under both IFRS and US GAAP.
  • Experience consolidating a multi-entity, multi-currency group into a large corporate parent, whether in industry or in an audit practice.
  • Proven ownership of an internal control framework over financial reporting and of external audits.
  • Strong revenue recognition experience (IFRS 15 and ASC 606), ideally with subscription, advertising or events revenue.
  • Working knowledge of transfer pricing and international tax, enough to shape structure and challenge advisers. You do not need to be a tax specialist.
  • Experience leading finance teams across countries and time zones, including a regular early-morning overlap with our Brussels hub.

Preferred

  • Hands-on experience with acquisitions, disposals or carve-outs, including purchase accounting and discontinued operations.
  • Workday Financials and Salesforce experience, and a record of automating close and reporting.
  • Familiarity with Belgian GAAP, and additional European languages.

Compensation: $250,000 - $275,000 annual salary. The final salary offered will be based on factors including relevant experience, skills, and qualifications.

job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO Live is seeking an Editorial Producer to help shape the editorial programming for our summits, policy briefings and other events across North America. 


The Live Events Producer will help identify the issues, debates and developments that deserve to be on stage, determine the newsmakers and experts who can bring those conversations to life, and work with a team of journalists, producers and bookers to develop compelling programs for POLITICO audiences.


The ideal candidate is an experienced reporter or producer with strong editorial judgment, a deep interest in politics and policy, and an instinct for what makes a story timely, consequential and engaging. This person should be equally comfortable digging into a complicated policy issue, identifying the right person to interview about it, developing sharp questions and writing compelling copy that makes an audience want to pay attention.


Who You Are:

  • You have strong news judgment and know what stories, issues and people deserve attention
  • You thrive in a fast-moving news environment and make smart editorial decisions under pressure
  • You can turn complex policy and political issues into compelling, timely and accessible live conversations
  • You are a sharp researcher and interviewer who knows how to develop questions that get beyond talking points
  • You are a strong writer who can make news engaging and urgent across formats
  • You are curious, resourceful and quick to get up to speed on unfamiliar topics
  • You are organized, driven and able to manage multiple projects and deadlines 

​What You’ll Do:

  • Help shape the editorial vision for POLITICO Live events, identifying the most important and timely issues, debates and stories that should be explored on stage
  • Develop compelling programming ideas from breaking news, POLITICO reporting, emerging policy debates and broader trends in politics, business and global affairs
  • Identify and research newsmakers, policymakers, industry executives, experts and other influential voices who can provide meaningful perspectives and insights
  • Write compelling editorial and promotional copy that makes complex issues accessible, engaging and urgent for audiences, including program descriptions, event copy, social media content, news stories, interview questions and other editorial materials
  • Work across teams to ensure editorial goals are aligned with the practical realities of event production, including timing, format, speaker availability and audience needs
  • Support live events from development through execution, including preparation of moderators and speakers and making adjustments as news and circumstances evolve
  • Contribute to digital, video and social storytelling around events, with an emphasis on creating content that extends the reach and impact of live programming

​What You'll Need:

  • 5-10 years of experience as a reporter, editor, producer or journalist, with a strong understanding of how to tell compelling and balanced news stories
  • Experience with research and reporting, interviewing and/or producing interviews for live events, podcasts, television or other editorial platforms
  • Exceptional editorial judgment, with the ability to identify the stories, issues and personalities that matter most to an audience
  • A strong understanding of politics and policy, with demonstrated interest in U.S. politics, global affairs and business
  • Strong writing skills and a talent for making news engaging, accessible and urgent
  • Strong research skills, including the ability to quickly become knowledgeable about unfamiliar subjects and identify credible sources and relevant perspectives
  • Critical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to make sound editorial decisions under pressure
  • Strong guest identification instincts and an ability to recognize which newsmakers, experts and voices can add the most value to a conversation
  • A collaborative approach to work and a willingness to contribute across a team of producers, editors and bookers who build events together
  • Strong verbal communication and presentation skills, including the ability to pitch ideas, explain editorial decisions and work effectively with colleagues and potential speakers
  • Experience with video editing for social media is a plus

COMPENSATION:

$90,000- 100,000 Annual Base.

The final salary offered will be based on factors including relevant experience, skills, and qualifications.

Job Description:

POLITICO is looking for an experienced editor of impeccable judgment for a 12-month, 4 days per week assignment to join our growing global standards and ethics team to ensure the integrity of our journalism across all platforms and deepen our bonds of trust with readers.

 

This role comes with a mandate to uphold POLITICO’s editorial values and commitment to authoritative, nonpartisan and tough-mindedly fair journalism; to provide an essential quality check on all the work we do; and to set guidelines but more importantly in real time help journalists resolve knotty ethical questions as they arise.

 

This editor will serve as a hands-on collaborator with other editors on pre-publication reporting and reviews of our most sensitive content as well as the countless issues that come up in the course of producing ambitious and innovative journalism.

 

This editor will take a lead role in writing and updating newsroom policies and stylebook entries to offer clear direction to the staff across the globe and work alongside others to assist on training and development programs for our journalists. 

 

This 32-hours-a-week position can be based in Arlington, VA, New York, NY or Sacramento, CA with the strong preference to work in the afternoon and evening (Eastern Standard Time).


What You’ll Do:

  • Serve as a hands-on editor who can offer pre-publication guidance on stories
  • Address and resolve issues related to our journalism after it is published
  • Help research and write newsroom policies on ethics and professional behavior and stylebook entries 
  • Assist in designing training and development programs for POLITICO journalists

 

 What You’ll Need:

  • A rigorous commitment to fair-minded, nonpartisan journalism 
  • Ability to juggle multiple tasks at once at a demanding pace  
  • Desire to collaborate with journalists across the newsroom, helping broker solutions to challenging situations
  • Demonstrated commitment to excellence and the highest standards of professional integrity.

Compensation:

  • $100,000–$120,000 annual salary, based on a four-day-per-week (80% FTE) schedule

POLITICO is seeking a Newsroom Engineering intern for Summer 2027. The intern will help reporters and editors solve real workflow problems with practical, responsible technology, with the goal to help shape the future of newsroom tools and workflows. This opportunity sits at the intersection of journalism, product thinking, and technology, supporting experiments and internal tools that help reporters and editors work more effectively. You’ll help research newsroom needs, code real tools, and evaluate AI-assisted workflows in newsroom contexts.


You don't need necessarily need to come from a Computer Science background. If you ever written a script to scrape data for a story, built a personal site or taught yourself to code out of curiosity – that counts.

  • You have both journalistic instincts and a technical aptitude 
  • You like understanding how reporters and editors work, where workflows break down, and how tools can help. 
  • You’re thoughtful about emerging technologies, including AI, and interested in how they can support journalism 
  • You’re comfortable collaborating across multiple stakeholders, especially with reporters, editors, product managers and engineers 

 

What You’ll Do:

  • Contribute to other Newsroom Engineering projects by writing code, building prototypes, testing features and documenting technical decisions 
  • Research and document workflow challenges facing reporters and editors  
  • Help identify opportunities to improve newsroom processes and internal tools. 
  • Test prototypes and internal tools with realistic reporting and editing scenarios. 
  • Help evaluate AI-assisted workflows for accuracy, usefulness, risk and editorial fit. 
  • Participate in conversations about responsible technology usage in newsroom products and workflows 

 

What You’ll Need:

  • Ability to work quickly and efficiently under deadlines 
  • Entrepreneurial mindset 
  • Proven experience in a newsroom. At least one professional news media internship or job preferred

Why Intern at POLITICO?

POLITICO is seeking exceptional college students and recent graduates for its Spring 2027 reporting in Tallahassee. 


Who You Are:
You’re an enterprising and creative journalist eager to report and write for an audience of political and policy junkies. You’re excited to report from the Capitol in Tallahassee, covering the state legislative session and the newly elected governor of Florida.


What You’ll Do:

  • Cover legislation, lawmakers, the governor, state agencies and Florida politics
  • Play a critical role in story creation and production, including research, reporting, writing and aggregating, including for newsletters
  • Contribute to the reporting of a dynamic team covering policy and politics for both in-state and national audiences


What You’ll Need:

  • A passion for politics/policy and a thirst to learn about Florida politics and government
  • Strong foundational reporting and writing skills
  • Excellent news judgment
  • Ability to work quickly and efficiently under deadlines
  • Entrepreneurial mindset
  • Proven experience in a newsroom. At least one professional news media internship or job preferred

Why Intern at POLITICO?

  • Cover the biggest stories in Florida as they unfold, with a behind-the-scenes view of how news gets made
  • Be a full-time reporter. Work independently (and with your team) on breaking news, enterprise, newsletters and more
  • Report in the field as needed
  • Build your skills through biweekly intern-specific trainings, newsroom sessions and direct feedback


Internship Details:

  • Dates: January-May 2027
  • Pay: $23/hr
  • Schedule: Hybrid, full-time 40 hours/week
  • Location: Tallahassee, FL
  • Application deadline: Monday, October 26, 2026, 11:59pm EST

Submission Materials:

  • Resume
  • Cover Letter
  • 3-5 original clips to showcase your experience. Please attach as PDFs or links that are publicly accessible. Do not submit clips behind a paywall.

Please follow instructions carefully. All of the above materials must be uploaded to the Resume/CV section of the application to be considered for the position. Incomplete applications will not be accepted.


We value our people. Click here for more on what we offer and what it’s like to work for POLITICO.

Let’s keep in touch. You can view our list of open positions here and email us careers@politico.com. We hope to see your application soon!


About Us. 

POLITICO illuminates the forces shaping global power. Since 2007, we have delivered intelligence that anticipates tomorrow's headlines, not reports on yesterday's news. As politics has increasingly become the defining force of our era, our work has never been more vital. 


Cabinet secretaries and Ministers start their mornings with our analysis. CEOs shape strategy around our reporting. Advocacy leaders rely on our insights to move policy. We deliver the straightforward facts and clear-eyed analysis they need to navigate the most complex political landscape of our lifetimes. 

Our 1,100+ publishing professionals across the world's key democratic capitals—Washington, Brussels, London, Paris, Berlin, Sacramento, and New York—form the world's premier politics and policy newsroom. We tell the story of how power really works by explaining who wields it and how they plan to exercise it, connecting dots others miss and delivering scoops from sources others don't even know exist. 


Innovation has always been a core tenet of our story. At launch, we bet that depth would trump scale, that talent would trump traffic, and that politics would become central to modern life. In 2011, we made another bet and launched POLITICO Pro to help decision-makers understand the business of government, transforming both how they shape government action and the business of journalism itself. 


These bets have made POLITICO the most successful digital news startup of its generation and the indispensable resource for leaders who shape the future. Today, we are a rarity in media: a growing, profitable, and sustainable news organization. 


POLITICO is a subsidiary of Axel Springer SE, a family-owned transatlantic media company headquartered in Berlin and New York. Axel Springer is dedicated to shaping the future of journalism in the free world, believing that a free and informed society is essential to democracy. The company’s guiding principles - first articulated as  The Essentials by founder Axel Springer in the aftermath of World War II - remain a cornerstone of the company’s foundation today. Learn more about Axel Springer.

job.title: Senior Android Engineer
job.description:
Join our team at the Guardian and be a part of a diverse and inclusive global organisation that delivers fearless, investigative journalism and holds power to account. Our team of award-winning journalists, cutting-edge commercial professionals and industry-leading digital experts are committed to making a difference and represent a wide range of backgrounds and perspectives. We offer a challenging and exciting environment for career development, with a focus on training, growth and fostering an inclusive culture.

 

We are now looking for a Senior Android Developer to join our Apps Experience team. Development of digital products is central to the Guardian. We create our award-winning Android app primarily in Kotlin and Java using Android Studio. We're focussed on providing a fast and stable experience to our users, and our Play Store rating of 4.7 stars is testament to that.

 

You'll work on major new features, as well as improving and maintaining existing functionality for The Guardian’s Android app. As a Senior Developer you’ll take the lead on projects and offer encouragement and guidance to help others to grow. 

 

About the role

 

  • Building and testing major new features, as well as improving and maintaining existing functionality for the app.
  • Working  90%+ in Kotlin, but you may be required to work with Java too.
  • You won't be coding in isolation - our culture is strongly collaborative, whether pair programming with other developers or working closely with other stakeholders. 
  • You can expect to work closely with iOS, server-side, and web engineers, and designers, product managers, editorial and commercial colleagues.
  • You'll take on a leadership role in some of the teams projects
  • You’ll be encouraged to help others grow - you will pass on your expertise to other developers, whilst continuing to grow yourself.
  • Sometimes deciding what code to write is as hard as writing the code itself. As an engineer you'll be involved in product decisions as well as technical ones.
  • You'll strive to be innovative on a daily basis, as well as at our regular hack days.

 

About you

 

  • You have demonstrated expertise in Android development and you have a strong interest in growing your skills.
  • You have strong competence in one or more of modern Android development tools, including Jetpack Compose, Coroutines/Flow, MVVM, Webviews, other Jetpack libraries, and modular app architectures.
  • You test your code and promote a culture of testing. Demonstrate experience with some of JVM unit testing, instrumented testing, and UI regression testing
  • You are comfortable working with both cutting edge technologies as well as legacy code
  • You have experience of, or are willing to take on a leadership role in some team projects
  • You have a rough idea of how iOS development works and you'd like to know more, perhaps even try it yourself.
  • Familiarity with Swift and ObjectiveC for iOS, or Scala and Typescript for server side development is useful. 

 

We actively encourage applications from groups traditionally underrepresented in the UK media

 

Our developers operate in a hybrid environment working 1 day a week from our offices in Kings Cross and 4 days remotely. If you’d like to come in more than that, that’s great too. 

 

We strive for transparency in remuneration where possible. The salary for new Senior Android Developers at the Guardian is £82,000 per year. 

 

We value and respect all differences (seen and unseen) in all people. We aspire to have inclusive working experiences and an environment that reflects the audience we serve, where our people have equal access to career development opportunities, their voices are heard and can contribute to our future. We actively encourage applications from people of all backgrounds. Many of our staff work flexibly and we will consider all requests for flexible working arrangements.

 

How to apply

 

To apply, please upload your latest CV. We don’t require a cover letter but we’ll ask you a question about our android app as part of the application questionnaire. This question should take no longer than 5 minutes to answer, so please factor in the extra time when applying. 

 

We appreciate the time taken to prepare each application we receive. We do not use AI-assisted technology to review applications; every application is reviewed by a member of our recruitment team. Thank you for bearing with us during the screening process. 

 

The closing date for applications is Monday 26th October 2026.

 

All roles at the Guardian are open for everybody to apply. It is important to us that you feel supported and comfortable throughout your recruitment process, in order to perform your best. Please let us know if there are any changes we could make to help your application, this includes providing documents in accessible formats or personalising the process to better support your needs. Please contact Anna Vipers on anna.vipers@theguardian.com to discuss further so we can work with you to support you through your application.

 

Benefits at the Guardian

You'll have 30 days of annual leave per year (plus bank holidays) with the option to purchase an additional 5 days. Our pension scheme is generous; if you contribute 5% then we will contribute 8-12% (depending on your age). We believe in giving back, which is why employees are given 2 volunteering days annually and the option of payroll giving. Season ticket loans are also available.

 

You are entitled to private healthcare, life cover, income protection, and eye tests. You can also opt in to dental insurance.

 

We have enhanced maternity, paternity, adoption and shared parental leave policies in place. We also support our employees by offering an IVF, menopause, baby loss, and trans equality policy.

 

Culture and wellbeing

We want everyone to feel like they belong at the Guardian and we champion diversity of thought. Our various employee forums provide a platform to use their voice to foster an inclusive workplace. We became the first major media organisation to achieve B Corp status.

 

We offer tools to help you prioritise your wellbeing including access to our employee benefits platform which provides tailored support for health and wellbeing. In addition, we also offer free yoga and pilates classes. These run alongside our corporate gym membership and cycle to work scheme.

 

Our canteen has views overlooking the Regents Canal and caters for breakfast, lunch and dinner.

 

Learning and development

We encourage personal and professional growth. Employees have access to a broad range of tools and solutions, and we are happy to support the pursuit of professional qualifications through vocational courses and apprenticeships.
