job.title: US Data Journalist
job.description:
About us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

 

The role

The FT’s visual and data journalism team is looking for an experienced data journalist to cover US politics, economics and financial news. This is a full-time staff position.

The successful applicant will collaborate with US-based news editors and correspondents across North America as well as colleagues in London, Hong Kong and beyond. You’ll help us deliver compelling journalism on our core coverage areas of trade, economics and financial markets, as well as US electoral politics and campaign finance. 

You will have a record of working self-sufficiently, from story pitch to final product, and an interest in providing a global perspective for both US and overseas readers. You will also collaborate with the wider Visual & Data Journalism team, and reporters and editors from across the FT’s network who need support applying data-driven methods to their work. 

We are happy to consider candidates wishing to be based in Washington DC or New York City. External applicants must be eligible to work in the US.

Occasional weekend/flexible working may be required as part of covering fast-moving news.

 

Essential skills

You will have a strong portfolio of work in data journalism, ideally focused on business, finance, economics or politics in North America. In addition, we are looking for:

  • Experience using data journalism or data science techniques to find and tell news stories
  • Confidence using R or Python for data sourcing (including web scraping, APIs and large databases), cleaning and analysis
  • Excellent communication skills, particularly the ability to explain your quantitative analysis work simply to non-specialist audiences
  • A passion for continuously learning in order to keep your skills at the forefront of current practice
  • The ability to pitch, write and deliver original data driven stories

 

Desirable Skills

While this is not a graphics-production role, experience of using data visualisation effectively in reporting would be a distinct advantage. 

In addition, while we don’t expect you to have all of these skills, any of the following would be beneficial, so please mention them in your cover letter and résumé:

  • Training in statistics, data science or quantitative social science methods
  • Experience building, maintaining or working with pipelines for continuously acquiring and processing data
  • Experience applying data analysis in financial or business journalism
  • Knowledge of working collaboratively with others on coding projects using version control systems such as Git
  • Familiarity with Adobe Illustrator 

 

Please submit your application by the end of the day, Friday 6th November 2026. 

 

Salary range

A reasonable estimate of the salary range for this role is $85,000 to $115,000. To ensure pay fairness, the successful candidate will be offered a salary within the estimated salary range based on a number of considerations including but not limited to: skill set; experience and training; certifications; and other business and organisational needs. This position is represented by the News Guild.

 

The use of AI

Original reporting, great writing and intelligent commentary lie at the heart of FT journalism. Our readers trust us to produce quality journalism that is accurate, fair and insightful. This is why FT editorial staff do not by default use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to write articles or create other reader-facing content. For specific and pre-approved cases, AI can be harnessed for certain tasks, such as assisting data research for investigations.  

We expect applicants to the FT newsroom to refrain from using AI in their test submissions, and any written materials should be a genuine reflection of their own knowledge, skills and experiences. We encourage candidates only to employ AI as a tool to help with research and interview readiness for a role. 

Candidates should be aware that the use of AI throughout the application process is monitored to ensure a fair and transparent hiring process for all.

 

Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion 

We believe in the power of unique perspectives and want all voices in our organisation to be heard, respected and valued. A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.

 

What’s in it for you? Our benefits

Our benefits vary by location but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. job.title: US Summer Newsroom Intern
job.description:
About us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading business news organisations, recognised internationally for its authority, integrity, and accuracy.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing. 

The FT has a record paying readership of 1.6 million, more than 1.4 million of which are digital subscriptions. It is part of Nikkei Inc., which provides a broad range of information, news, and services for the global business community. We have offices in more than 35 countries, including London, New York, Hong Kong, Beijing, Manila, Sofia, San Francisco, and Tokyo.

Our Internships

We are looking for passionate and motivated students who are interested in pursuing a career in media to join our team! We expect our interns to be in the office a minimum of three days a week. 

This program offers the opportunity to connect and collaborate across the FT — in the US and globally. You’ll develop ideas that help drive our growth, present your work to US leadership, and gain valuable insights from across the business. Plus, you’ll be paired with a dedicated Buddy to provide mentorship and support throughout your experience.

This internship pays $22 per hour for 40 hours per week and runs from June 7, 2027 - Aug 13, 2027. Before applying, please ensure you will be available on these dates.

Applicants must be authorised to work in the US.

Role Overview

The FT’s US newsroom internship offers aspiring journalists a front-row seat to the fast-paced world of global news. This is your chance to learn from and contribute to a dynamic multimedia newsroom that values curiosity, creativity, and sharp storytelling.

No two days are the same. From breaking stories and in-depth research to innovative digital projects, you’ll work alongside editors and reporters to bring ambitious journalism to life. We’re looking for versatile, driven interns who are eager to dig into stories that matter and help shape how the world understands the news.

Key responsibilities

  • Pitching, reporting, and writing original news stories
  • Conducting interviews and developing sources
  • Assisting senior correspondents with research, document analysis and reporting
  • Curating newsletters and contributing to digital projects
  • Collaborating with staffers on special projects

Required skills / experience

  • Proven interest in journalism
  • Some experience or knowledge of financial journalism, business, economics, or related areas
  • Curiosity about global markets, companies, and economies
  • Initiative to pitch and complete story ideas
  • Ability to work independently and meet deadlines
  • Excellent research and analytical skills
  • Strong communication and writing skills across platforms
  • Sound news judgment and high ethical standards

Please submit your application by November 2nd by 5pm Eastern Time and be sure to include the following documents in your application:

  • Resume
  • A cover letter explaining why you would be a good fit, and explaining your interest in joining our team
  • Three writing samples or published clips

Any application submitted after the deadline will not be considered.

The use of AI

Original reporting, great writing and intelligent commentary lie at the heart of FT journalism. Our readers trust us to produce quality journalism that is accurate, fair and insightful. For this reason, FT editorial staff do not use AI tools to write articles or create reader-facing content.

AI may be used in specific, pre-approved cases to assist with research, such as in data investigations. We expect internship applicants to refrain from using AI in writing tests or written materials submitted during the application process. All submissions must reflect your own knowledge, skills, and experiences.

Candidates may use AI to assist with research and interview preparation. However, the use of AI throughout the application process is monitored to ensure fairness and transparency for all applicants.

Our commitment to a fair and inclusive workplace

At the FT, we are committed to creating a fair and inclusive workplace where everyone has equal opportunity to succeed. We welcome and value different perspectives and strive to ensure all employees are heard and supported. We believe people do their best work when they can be themselves and have the flexibility they need to balance their work and personal lives. We are an equal opportunity employer and align with all applicable laws prohibiting discrimination.

Accessibility

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments/personalisation as part of the application process or to enable you to attend an interview. If you would like to discuss your requirements or have any questions, email talent@ft.com and a member of our team will be happy to help.

job.title: Beauty & Wellness Intern
job.description:
The Daily Beast delivers award-winning original reporting and sharp opinions from big personalities in the arenas of politics, pop culture, world news, and more. Fiercely independent and armed with irreverent intelligence, The Daily Beast now reaches more than 20 million readers per month.

Job Description

The Daily Beast is seeking talented, motivated, and curious editorial interns with interests in beauty and wellness to join our award-winning newsroom on-site in New York, where they will write for The Looker. Open to undergraduate juniors and seniors, graduate students, and post-grads, this internship is a unique opportunity for emerging journalists to gain hands-on experience writing and reporting on the fast-evolving landscapes of aesthetics, style, and culture—from celebrity beauty news and product reviews to plastic surgery explainers and personal essays.

The role is full-time (37.5 hours/week) for a three-month period, and may include some evening or weekend shifts.

Ideal candidates will have a deep interest in health and wellness journalism, an eye for beauty and lifestyle trends, and a desire to tell smart, creative, and engaging stories. The best applicants will be full of ideas, write cleanly, and be comfortable juggling news curation, evergreen features, and commerce-adjacent content.

Qualifications

  • Strong organizational skills and ability to meet tight deadlines.

  • Demonstrated interest in health, wellness, beauty, or lifestyle writing. Prior experience writing or interning for a publication, blog, or newsletter is preferred.

  • A strong news sense and deep curiosity about topics that impact how people live, feel, and look.

  • Excellent writing and reporting skills, with the ability to balance voice and authority.

  • An understanding of the role of visuals and video in health, wellness, and beauty storytelling.

  • Familiarity with digital publishing and content management systems is a plus.

  • Degree in a relevant discipline is preferred but not required.

To apply, please submit a resume and a brief cover letter that includes links to 4–6 writing samples or portfolio pieces.

Compensation

The salary for this role is $19.00 per hour.

Additional Information

Don’t meet every single requirement listed here? If you’re interested in joining the Beast but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with this job description, we encourage you to give it a shot all the same. It might turn out that you’re just the right candidate for this or other roles. See more about our commitment to diversity at https://www.thedailybeast.com/company/diversity

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

job.title: Senior Workday Financial Reporting Manager
job.description:
This is a remote US position that must be worked within Pacific Time core business hours.

 

 

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 

The Senior Workday Financial Reporting Manager is responsible for overseeing the preparation and distribution of financial statements in compliance with regulatory requirements and company policies. You will ensure the accuracy and integrity of financial reporting, assist with external audits, and implement best practices in financial disclosure. You have a strong background in GAAP/IFRS, SEC reporting (if applicable), and financial analysis.

 

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 

  • Report Development: Design, build, test, and maintain custom Advanced, Matrix, Composite, and standard Workday reports using calculated fields and Business Objects.
  • System Maintenance & Upgrades: Test, review, and update existing reports during Workday's bi-annual releases to maintain functionality.
  • Dashboard Creation: Design and manage operational dashboards, Discovery Boards, and Report-as-a-Service (RaaS) outputs, partnering with the Financial Analyst, to track key performance indicators (KPIs) for leadership.
  • Prepare and update financial statement templates.
  • Oversee internal financial reporting processes and implement controls to maintain accuracy and efficiency.
  • Manage the preparation of quarterly and annual reports.
  • Participate in monthly, quarterly, and year-end closing process.
  • Collaborate with internal teams to gather report parameters.
  • Lead process improvements in financial reporting systems and procedures.
  • Ensure compliance with internal policies.

 

 

SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

 

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, information systems, business, or a related field, providing the technical foundation for Workday reporting responsibilities. MBA or CPA is valued.
  • 3-5 years of experience in financial reporting, accounting, and/or auditing roles.
  • Demonstrated, hands-on experience building reports in Workday Report Writer including calculated fields and advanced, matrix, and composite reports.
  • Workday Report Writer Certification or be willing and able to successfully complete a Workday Report Writing proficiency assessment as part of the interview process.
  • Deep understanding of Workday Finance.
  • Workday Adaptive Planning experience including Adaptive Dashboards, HTML Reports, and OfficeConnect reporting packages highly preferred.
  • Experience with Workday Dashboards, Scorecards, and Workday Hubs preferred.
  • Experience gathering, documenting, and translating business requirements into reporting solutions, with working knowledge of data integration/ETL concepts and reporting governance practices.
  • Knowledge of GAAP.
  • Non-profit experience highly preferred.
  • Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and data analytics skills.
  • Proficiency in Excel.
  • Excellent problem-solving, communication, and leadership abilities.

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

ABOUT THE RECORDING ACADEMY AND ITS AFFILIATES

 

RECORDING ACADEMY

The Recording Academy represents the voices of performers, songwriters, producers, engineers, and all music professionals. Dedicated to ensuring the recording arts remain a thriving part of our shared cultural heritage, the Academy honors music's history while investing in its future through the Grammy Museum, advocates on behalf of music creators, supports music people in times of need through MusiCares, and celebrates artistic excellence through the Grammy Awards—music's only peer-recognized accolade and highest achievement. As the world's leading society of music professionals, we work year-round to foster a more inspiring world for creators.

 

LATIN RECORDING ACADEMY

The Latin Recording Academy is an international, membership-based organization comprised of Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking recording artists, musicians, songwriters, producers and other creative and technical recording professionals. The organization is dedicated to improving the quality of life and cultural condition for Latin music and its makers. In addition to producing the Latin Grammy Awards to honor excellence in the recorded arts and sciences, The Latin Recording Academy provides educational and outreach programs for the Latin music community either directly or through its Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation.

 

LATIN GRAMMY CULTURAL FOUNDATION

The Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation is a charitable organization established by the Latin Recording Academy in 2014. The organization is dedicated to creating opportunities for the next generation of Latin music creators through scholarships, educational programs, grants, and access to creators and industry executives.

 

MUSICARES

A friend and ally of the music community, MusiCares was established by the Recording Academy to safeguard the health and well-being of all music people. A four-star charity and safety net in times of need, MusiCares offers confidential preventative, recovery, and emergency programs to address financial, medical, and personal health issues. Through the generosity of our donors and volunteer professionals, our dedicated team works across the country to ensure the music community has the resources and support it needs.

 

GRAMMY MUSEUM

The Grammy Museum is a nonprofit organization dedicated to celebrating and exploring music from yesterday and today to inspire the music of tomorrow through music preservation, education, exhibitions, and public programming and aims to create a world in which shared love of music sparks curiosity, creativity, and community. Programs include Grammy in the Schools education programs that are offered year-round for students, teachers, and schools throughout the United States. 

 

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

The Recording Academy, its affiliates, and the music industry have a strong culture of inclusion and respect for everyone. The Recording Academy makes intentional, courageous, and principled decisions for stronger business outcomes and ensures that all creators and professionals live and work in a fair and safe environment. It is the Recording Academy's policy to provide equal employment opportunities for all applicants and employees. The Recording Academy does not discriminate on the basis of race (nor traits historically associated with race, including, but not limited to hair texture and protective hairstyles), color, religion (including religious dress and grooming), creed, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions), national origin, ancestry, age, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, family care status, military or veteran status, marital status, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by law. job.title: Audience Intelligence Analytics Intern
job.description:
Deadline to apply for KQED Internships is Friday, October 30, 2026. Please state which internship(s) you are applying for in your cover letter and apply to each internship individually.

This is a paid internship, working 16 hours per week from Tuesday, January 19, 2027, through Friday, June 25, 2027. The current hourly rate is $19.61 per hour.

Position Summary:

The Audience Intelligence team is charged with providing KQED with the data needed to make data informed decisions. The team serves as the central data hub for the organization and works with a variety of departments including news, science, arts, marketing, foundations and audience development. The Audience Intelligence intern will have many responsibilities including the mining of data sets for insights, automation, facilitating predictive analytics, and supporting research. The intern will also have the lead on a project allowing them to complete the internship with a deliverable that can be used in their future job search.

KQED envisions a public media organization with a culture that centers on human dignity, equity, and belonging. This will enable us to better serve and reflect the Bay Area through diverse and inclusive storytelling. 

We value the contributions of marginalized people in society — including Black, Indigenous, and all people of color,  people with disabilities, and LGBTQIA+ people — and we believe that these communities must be centered in the work we do, and we strongly encourage members of these communities to apply.

The mission that drives us:

KQED provide citizens of Northern California with a community-supported alternative to commercial media.   We provide citizens with the knowledge they need to make informed decisions; convene community dialogue; bring the arts to everyone and engage audiences to share their stories. We help students and teachers thrive in 21st-century classrooms, and take people of all ages on journeys of exploration- exposing them to new people, places and ideas.

This role requires working in KQED's newly renovated headquarters and working in the field. 

Essential Functions:
  • Help develop new insights and analyses that inform organizational decisions and help us continue to engage our audiences
  • Support research projects by aggregating and analyzing data
  • Execute quantitative analyses that translate data into actionable insights
  • Build visualizations that expose the health and performance of our products
  • Presentation building for a variety of stakeholders
  • Other Duties as assigned

Knowledge/Experience Required:

  • Intellectual curiosity for data-driven products
  • Experience with data analysis and/or visualization
  • Excellent writing, research, and communication skills
  • Strong attention to detail
  • Problem-solving acumen
  • Capacity to balance multiple responsibilities
  • Ability to work independently
  • At least some knowledge of SQL

Knowledge/Experience Desired:

  • Bonus points for knowledge of Python or another programming language, dashboarding tools (e.g., Looker, Tableau, etc.), ETL tools, or databases.

Growth & Development Opportunities:  

Audience Intelligence interns have a huge impact on what we do. They are a full-fledged member of our team and their life experience, opinions, and ideas bring fresh approaches to the work we do and are incredibly valuable. As part of the audience intelligence team, the intern will learn what it means to put our audiences first as we look to find the stories in their data that will allow us to grow a younger, more diverse audience base. This internship will help develop and hone analytical, and communication skills. If there is anything specific an intern wants to learn about audience intelligence, we are committed to making that happen.

job.description:
Title: Director of Membership Programs

Schedule Format - Location: Hybrid - San Francisco

Pay Information: Salary Range: $125,547 - $137,000

Position SummaryThe Director of Membership Programs leads the strategy and growth of KQED’s on-air, third-party, and emerging membership fundraising channels. This role manages a portfolio that includes on-air fundraising, matching gifts, vehicle and real estate donations, and other third-party programs, while identifying and testing new opportunities to grow membership revenue.This is a strategy and growth role with responsibility for evaluating the performance and potential of each fundraising channel, determining where KQED should invest, improve, scale, or shift resources, and building a disciplined pipeline of new tests and initiatives. The Director sets strategy, priorities, and revenue goals across both areas and is accountable for overall performance.

This role works closely with colleagues across Membership, Development, Product, Data and Analytics, Programming, Content and Donor Services to ensure fundraising channels work together to grow revenue, acquire new members and strengthen long-term donor relationships.

The ideal candidate is analytical and entrepreneurial, with experience growing or improving fundraising programs. This role requires strong editorial judgment, journalistic integrity, and the ability to work quickly and creatively in a newsroom environment. The Social Video Producer should be comfortable developing original story ideas, collaborating with reporters and editors, conducting interviews, producing one-person and small-crew shoots, directing talent, and creating production approaches that can be repeated and scaled across KQED’s social video portfolio.

The Social Video Producer will also work closely with Audience Development to understand audience behavior, platform trends, and performance data, applying those insights to story development, format development, and production decisions.

  • Work with Audience Development to identify audience opportunities, understand platform behavior, and use performance insights to inform story development and repeatable format strategies.

  • Demonstrated experience developing and producing original vertical video content for social and digital platforms.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop stories and video treatments specifically for mobile-first and social audiences.

job.description:
Deadline to apply for KQED Internships is Friday, October 30, 2026. Please state which internship(s) you are applying for in your cover letter and apply to each internship individually.

This is a paid internship, working 16 hours per week from Tuesday, January 19, 2027, through Friday, June 25, 2027. The current hourly rate is $19.61 per hour.

Listening to The California Report Magazine is like taking a road trip for your ears to meet the people and visit the places that make the Golden State unique. Every week, we bring you stories about real people and the sometimes extraordinary situations they find themselves in. We celebrate a range of experiences on our show, and encourage interns from all backgrounds to apply. We’re also looking for interns who are passionate about long-form audio storytelling, and amplifying the voices of people we don’t often hear from in the media. The 29-minute program airs throughout the weekend on stations across California, and is also available as a podcast.

 

KQED envisions a public media organization with a culture that centers on human dignity, equity, and belonging. This will enable us to better serve and reflect the Bay Area through diverse and inclusive storytelling. 

We value the contributions of marginalized people in society — including Black, Indigenous, and all people of color,  people with disabilities, and LGBTQIA+ people — and we believe that these communities must be centered in the work we do, and we strongly encourage members of these communities to apply.

The mission that drives us:

KQED provide citizens of Northern California with a community-supported alternative to commercial media.   We provide citizens with the knowledge they need to make informed decisions; convene community dialogue; bring the arts to everyone and engage audiences to share their stories. We help students and teachers thrive in 21st-century classrooms, and take people of all ages on journeys of exploration- exposing them to new people, places and ideas.

This role requires working in KQED's newly renovated headquarters and working in the field.

Essential Functions:

  • Research and develop potential stories, show themes and host interview segments.
  • Initiate discussions with TCR Magazine staff on your story pitches, and how you plan to report them.
  • Identify interview subjects, conduct pre-interviews, and book guests.
  • Conduct field interviews, record sound and provide producers with usable material.
  • Write accompanying digital story for every radio story you produce, and assist staff on additional digital stories.

Other Job Functions:

  • Assist the host, producers and editors with production needs as assigned.
  • Help promote stories through social media.

Knowledge/Experience Required:

  • Must have a background in long-form audio production and storytelling (and be able to share samples of audio work).
  • Must follow current California affairs, events, and trends through news outlets and other sources.

Knowledge/Experience Desired:

  • Skills and experience in writing news features are helpful, but not required.
  • Knowledge of California related-issues, geography, and communities.
  • Familiarity or experience with podcast production.
  • Fluency in languages other than English is a plus.
  • Some experience in digital audio editing (ProTools, Hindenburg, Audition, etc.). 
  • Social media skills.

Growth & Development Opportunities: 

  • Following the internship, some alums work in the newsroom in a range of positions – from filling in as a producer or reporting stories for The California Report Magazine, to being trained to work on other KQED News programs.

Duties include service support responsibilities and operations in the TV Engineering department, providing end-user, software & remote support for KQED staff across multiple departments.

job.description:
Title: Vertical Video Editor (News)

Schedule Format - Location: Hybrid - San Francisco

Pay Information: $79,828 - $99,785
Temporary: 1-Year Limited Term, Full Time



The Vertical Video Editor is an experienced video editor responsible for creating compelling, accurate, and platform-native vertical video content for KQED’s newsroom. Working closely with the Social Video Producer, reporters, editors, and other newsroom colleagues, this position will transform reporting, interviews, field footage, archival materials, graphics, and other source material into engaging short-form video for platforms including TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts.

The Vertical Video Editor will be a creative editorial partner to the Social Video Producer, collaborating from story development through final delivery to determine the most effective visual approach, story structure, pacing, graphics, sound, and platform-specific execution. The role will help develop repeatable vertical video formats and editing practices that allow KQED News to produce high-quality social video efficiently and consistently.

This position requires strong editorial judgment, excellent storytelling instincts, and advanced technical and creative editing skills. The ideal candidate understands how audiences consume video on mobile and social platforms and can translate journalistic reporting into concise, visually compelling stories without compromising accuracy, context, or KQED’s editorial standards.

The Vertical Video Editor will work within post-production workflows established by the Senior Video Editor and collaborate with Digital Video, Audience Development, and News leadership to improve vertical video storytelling based on audience behavior and performance data.
 

KQED envisions a public media organization with a culture that centers on human dignity, equity, and belonging. This will enable us to better serve and reflect the Bay Area through diverse and inclusive storytelling. 

We value the contributions of marginalized people in society — including Black, Indigenous, and all people of color,  people with disabilities, and LGBTQIA+ people — and we believe that these communities must be centered in the work we do, and we strongly encourage members of these communities to apply.

KQED Code of Ethics  https://www.kqed.org/about/code-ethics

The mission that drives us:

KQED provide citizens of Northern California with a community-supported alternative to commercial media.   We provide citizens with the knowledge they need to make informed decisions; convene community dialogue; bring the arts to everyone and engage audiences to share their stories. We help students and teachers thrive in 21st-century classrooms, and take people of all ages on journeys of exploration- exposing them to new people, places and ideas.

This role will work hybrid between working in KQED's newly renovated headquarters and working remotely. 

Essential Functions:
  • Edit high-quality vertical video content for KQED News across TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and other emerging vertical video platforms.
  • Edit video from a wide range of sources, including original field footage, interviews, reporter standups, user-generated content, archival footage, photographs, screen recordings, graphics, and third-party materials.
  • Shape edits for mobile-first viewing, using strong hooks, pacing, visual storytelling, captions, graphics, sound, and other techniques designed for vertical platforms.
  • Create captions, text treatments, lower thirds, graphics, and other visual elements appropriate for vertical video platforms.
  • Perform sound editing and mixing, color correction, basic motion graphics, and other post-production functions required to complete high-quality video.
  • Source and incorporate appropriate visual and audio assets, including archival and third-party materials, in coordination with producers and newsroom staff.
  • Create multiple versions, cutdowns, and platform-specific edits as needed.
  • Prepare final video files and associated assets for publishing and distribution.
  • Develop and maintain repeatable editing approaches, templates, workflows, and visual formats that improve the efficiency and consistency of KQED News vertical video production.
  • Manage project media and maintain organized edit projects in accordance with KQED post-production, media management, and archival workflows.
  • Meet tight publishing schedules and communicate proactively about potential production or post-production issues that could affect delivery.
  • Work with animators, illustrators, photographers, reporters, and other creative collaborators to incorporate additional visual elements as needed.
  • Work with the Senior Video Editor to develop, adopt and implement post-production standards, workflows, technical requirements, and best practices across News vertical video.
  • Help establish and maintain a distinctive visual language for KQED News vertical video while ensuring consistency with KQED’s broader brand and editorial standards.
  • Work quickly and efficiently on breaking and developing news while maintaining KQED’s standards for accuracy, fairness, attribution, context, and editorial integrity.
  • Work with reporters and editors to clarify or resolve editorial questions that arise during the editing process.Work closely with the Social Video Producer, reporters, editors, and newsroom stakeholders to translate reporting and story concepts into compelling visual narratives.
  • Collaborate with the News Social Video Producer from story development through final delivery, providing creative and editorial input on story structure, visual approach, pacing, graphics, sound, and platform execution.
  • Collaborate with Audience Development to understand audience behavior, performance data, and platform trends and apply those insights to future edits and storytelling approaches.
  • Participate in editorial and production meetings and contribute ideas for improving KQED’s vertical video strategy and storytelling.

Other Job Functions:
  • Perform other video and organizational duties as assigned.

Knowledge/Experience Required:
  • Minimum of three years of professional video editing experience, with demonstrated experience creating content for digital and social platforms.
  • Strong proficiency in Adobe Premiere Pro and familiarity with Adobe After Effects, Photoshop, Illustrator, and Media Encoder.
  • Demonstrated experience editing short-form, vertical video specifically for platforms such as TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts.
  • Strong understanding of mobile-first and social-first storytelling, including hooks, pacing, visual sequencing, captions, graphics, and audience retention.
  • Excellent editorial judgment and a strong understanding of journalistic principles, ethics, accuracy, attribution, and standards.
  • Demonstrated ability to work with reporters, producers, editors, and other editorial stakeholders to shape stories during the editing process.
  • Strong storytelling instincts and the ability to identify the most compelling narrative within interviews, field footage, archival material, and other source materials.
  • Ability to edit quickly and accurately under tight deadlines, including the ability to respond to breaking or developing news.
  • Strong sound editing and mixing skills, including dialogue cleanup, music, sound effects, and overall audio balancing.
  • Experience with color correction and basic motion graphics.
  • Strong understanding of video codecs, resolutions, frame rates, aspect ratios, audio formats, and technical requirements for digital and social video.
  • Ability to create accessible video content, including accurate captions and clear audio.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, including the ability to manage multiple projects and maintain organized media and edit projects.
  • Ability to work independently while also collaborating closely with a multidisciplinary newsroom and video team.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to respond constructively to editorial feedback and iterate quickly.
  • Commitment to KQED’s mission and journalistic standards.

Knowledge/Experience Desired:
  • Experience working in a newsroom or other journalistic environment.
  • Experience editing breaking news, current affairs, documentary, explanatory, or other journalism-focused video.
  • Experience developing repeatable social video formats, templates, or post-production workflows.
  • Advanced After Effects and motion graphics skills.
  • Experience incorporating animation, data visualization, maps, screenshots, social posts, and other visual journalism techniques into video.
  • Experience working with user-generated content and third-party video materials.

  • Familiarity with KQED, public media, or mission-driven journalism.

Work at CBC/Radio-Canada

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we create content that informs, entertains and connects Canadians on multiple platforms. Our successes and accomplishments are driven by embodying and upholding values, which include creativity, integrity, inclusiveness and relevance. 
 
Do you think you have the ability and drive to keep up with this exciting, ever-changing industry? Whether it be in front of the camera, on air, online or behind the scenes, you would be joining a team that thrives on making connections and telling stories that are important to Canadians.

Unposting Date:

2026-10-27 11:59 PM

This position will not be filled until consideration has been made by the CBC/Radio-Canada / APS Workforce Adjustment Committee.

 

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we all have a story to tell. What’s yours?

 

If you share our passion for Canadian storytelling, and you wish to help us engage with individuals and communities across our various digital platforms, this is where you’ll want to be!

 

Every day, you will have an opportunity to shape the way in which Canadians see themselves reflected in our digital services. Your work will have a direct impact on how millions of Canadians from various communities connect with our products, with one another, and with the diverse voices that make our country so unique.

 

You will have the opportunity to play a part in enlightening and entertaining Canadians through our innovative work in building the mediums that deliver our content. We are an innovative hub, where the talented professionals we work with are respected and valued for their contributions. Our product teams are vibrant and our work culture strives to achieve the highest standards of diversity and inclusion. We believe that hiring people with different career paths and backgrounds is fundamental in our shared success and in building healthy and highly performant teams.

 

When you join our mission, you are not only shaping the vision of CBC/Radio-Canada, but the future of our country.

 

We know that commitment to equity, inclusion and diversity is essential to creating content that mirrors and resonates with the rich and evolving makeup of our country.  We’re also committed to reaching out and connecting with our audience on multiple platforms this includes creating virtual places where communities can come together.

This is a hybrid position with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

 

Why is this role important?

 

You will be an important element of our over-the-top platform team. As such, working closely with the product owners, architects and technical managers, your role is to ensure the smooth execution of product front-end development and coordinate the technical work required to deliver requested features, while adhering to the standards and practices agreed to by the development management team.

 

The team you will be part of is in charge of an harmonized product, powering CBC Gem and ICI TOU.TV.


Perks you can look forward to:

  • Flexible work schedules, allowing you to prioritize yourself, your family and your work.
  • Work from home opportunities.
  • Competitive total rewards package.
  • Opportunities to work with cutting edge technology.
  • Opportunities for continued learning and professional development.
  • Opportunities to become a member of our Employee Resource Groups.
  • Pair programming and mentorship opportunities, where you can learn from the best in the industry and help coach new talent.
  • A creative and dynamic work environment, where your ideas and contributions can be heard, valued and respected.
  • A supportive management team committed to upholding the highest standards of diversity and inclusivity.
  • An environment which favours experimentation and an iterative approach in order to achieve the highest form of technical innovation.

 

Your responsibilities:

  • Design and/or modify reusable components for Radio-Canada's digital platforms; such as the audio/video player.
  • Ensure compliance with standards and control the quality of the product throughout the project's execution.
  • Stay informed of new trends in the various fields of digital development.
  • By being proactive, propose solutions to the challenges encountered.
  • Participate in Agile Scrum activities designed to review ongoing production projects in order to make necessary corrections and adjustments, or completed projects to measure their results.
  • Participate in the development of user stories for our various products.
  • Ensure the good performance of developed applications to handle high loads.
  • Participate in sprint planning, retrospectives, and application deployments.
  • Participate in code reviews and solution deployments.

We are looking for a candidate matching the following profile:

  • University degree or equivalent experience.
  • At least 3 years of experience in software development.
  • Experience in developing complex and high-performance mobile applications.
  • Proficiency in Android Studio, Git, and the Kotlin language.
  • Experience in developing an application published on Google Play.
  • Experience in developing within code review context (pull request).
  • Knowledge of programming patterns (such as MVP or MVVM).
  • Knowledge of SOLID architecture principles is an asset.
  • Ability to read, produce, and adhere to software architecture diagrams (UML, sequence diagram, etc.).
  • Interest in working on an application available on multiple form factors (mobile/tablet/TV).
  • Knowledge of Jetpack Compose, Exoplayer, Kotlin Multiplatform is an asset.
  • Knowledge of the libraries Dagger, Hilt, Koin is an asset.
  • Knowledge of Google architecture components is an asset.
  • Knowledge of Maven (including the design/maintenance of internal libraries) is an asset.
  • Knowledge of audio-video broadcasting on the web (streaming) is an asset.
  • Knowledge of other programming languages is an asset.
  • Knowledge of design patterns is an asset.
  • Good general knowledge and strong intellectual curiosity (to acquire and develop new knowledge and skills).
  • Critical thinking (to question and propose new ideas).
  • A keen interest in the major trends and challenges of the digital world.
  • Meticulousness, independence, and resourcefulness.
  • Excellent stress management and priority setting.
  • Analytical and conceptual thinking skills.
  • Flexibility, initiative, and dynamism.
  • Ability to work in a team, excellent communicator.
  • Bilingualism (English and French) spoken and written is mandatory.

 

Please note that due to the nature of the mandates and responsibilities of this role, all candidates will be required to work in a multilingual environment, where business will be conducted in both official languages (English and French). Therefore, employees working in this role will be expected to make the required efforts and adjustments to navigate this multilingual environment in a respectful manner for all.

 

Please note this is a 12-month contract position, renewable annually. This regular position is not a consulting assignment but a long-term opportunity with attractive CBC/Radio-Canada employee benefits.

Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.
 

We thank all applicants for their interest, but only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

As part of our recruitment process, candidates who advance to the next

step will be asked to complete a background check. This includes:  

  • A mandatory Criminal record check. 

  • Other background checks may be conducted based on the operational requirements of the position.


CBC/Radio-Canada is committed to being a leader in reflecting our country’s diversity. That’s because we can only create and tell the stories that connect Canadians, by having a workforce that mirrors the ever-changing makeup of our country. That’s why we, as an employer, value equal opportunity and nurture an inclusive workplace where our individual differences are not only recognized and valued, but also extend to and pervade all the services we provide as Canada’s public broadcaster. For more information, visit the Diversity and Inclusion section of our website. If you have accommodation needs at this stage of the recruitment process, please inform us as soon as possible by sending an e-mail to recruitment@cbc.ca.
 
You are invited to consult and familiarize yourself with our Code of Conduct, which can be found on our corporate website. All employees must adhere to the Code as a condition of employment. Your role:


As Supervising Technician, you plan, co-ordinate, assign, review and monitor the work of technicians reporting to you within your delegated authority; advise technical, production and other staff on the best operating, installation and technical/artistic production methods for achieving production goals. Provide engineers and other workers with specialized assistance and make recommendations for technical equipment purchases.


Key Tasks:

  • Plan, co-ordinate, assign, review and monitor, based on production needs and departmental objectives, the work of technicians reporting to you, and report on performance, discipline and safety matters.
  • Advise technical, production or other staff on workforce, training, installation and equipment requirements for technical operations; prepare detailed reports and make recommendations.
  • Advise technical, production or other staff on technical operations.
  • Act as a consultant to production, technical and other staff on technical operations and in evaluating new technical equipment; report your findings.
  • Evaluate operations and technical maintenance, and review operating methods and technical standards; submit recommendations for improving or modifying them.
  • Provide engineers, project leads and other workers with specialized assistance.
  • Plan, test and configure technical equipment on projects; make recommendations; track and upgrade software.
  • Ensure that the complex system checks and adjustments required for optimal performance of technical setups are carried out.
  • Anticipate and determine, in conjunction with management or other key contacts, training requirements to refresh the knowledge of technical or other staff in response to changing needs and technologies.
  • Design, draft, organize and deliver technical training courses or seminars and guide workers in performing their duties.
  • Co-ordinate, review and assess the work of trainees and report on their progress.
  • Design, administer and grade tests for technical staff and job applicants; check, assess and report on their competence.
  • Design and draft documents (such as reference or training manuals) and operating procedures; catalogue and update these materials and ensure their availability.
  • Plan, determine and distribute to the relevant people the technical equipment required for production; monitor that equipment and ensure it is in good working order.
  • Enforce safety measures for all workers and make recommendations to this effect.
  • Maintain, where necessary, an inventory of parts, modules, equipment, spare equipment and other supplies, ensuring, per established procedures, that sufficient quantities are in stock for operations to run smoothly.
  • Investigate, verify and review reported defects, taking or recommending any necessary corrective action.
  • Commit the Corporation, per your delegated authority or in consultation with your supervisor, to agreements with vendors, firms and contractors for the procurement of services or equipment; ensure that services rendered and equipment ordered meet the requirements of the initial agreement.
  • Perform site surveys, as needed, to identify locations and technical requirements for productions.
  • Keep your knowledge current so that you can perform your assigned duties and stay abreast of changing technology.
  • Provide maintenance technicians with ongoing operational advice, direction, guidance and encouragement to ensure a healthy work environment and maintain service quality; onboard and follow up with new employees.
  • Perform the technical duties of the technicians reporting to you.
  • Prepare, maintain and renew the ATA Carnet required to transport equipment outside Canada.
  • In case of technical failure, take the necessary corrective action to restore service and inform the relevant people.
  • Attend planning and production meetings as needed.
  • Report any breakdowns or defects in equipment or material to the relevant people.
  • Complete the appropriate forms and documents; share information verbally or in writing to ensure proper followup and to keep others informed.
  • Familiarize other employees with their duties and the work environment.
  • Carry out, as needed, all or part of the duties of another job classification within an equivalent or lower salary group, as well as other related duties.

This role requires full time on-site presence.


This is an on call position.


You must be available to work early mornings, evenings, nights, weekends, or any other schedule.

Qualifications:

  • College diploma (DCS) in TV production and post-production or in electronics.
  • Seven (7) years’ experience required to perform the job satisfactorily, given that you play an operational consulting role in addition to co-ordinating work.

Skills:

  • Extensive experience in the distribution and management of video signals within both traditional and digital television production environments.
  • Advanced expertise in multiplatform digital workflow management and production standards.
  • Knowledge of IP networking, PC/Mac environments and collaborative tools, with a strong ability to explain complex technical concepts to non-technical audiences clearly.
  • Functional knowledge of programming protocols and logic as applied to audio and video systems.
  • Significant experience in television production.
  • Proven ability to lead, supervise and upskill technical teams in a fast-paced production environment.
  • Solid understanding of audio, lighting and camera operations.
  • Ability to work well under pressure for extended periods with multiple people.
  • Judgment, leadership and decision-making skills.
  • Initiative.
  • Ability to be a self-starter.
  • Interpersonal skills.
  • Good knowledge of spoken and written French.
  • English is an asset.

Location: GA-Atlanta

Job Title:  Promotions Editor - WSB TV

 

Position Overview

WSB TV Channel 2, the #1 television station in Atlanta, Georgia is seeking a dedicated and creative video editor and motion designer to join its marketing & creative services team. You'll edit news promotions, image campaigns, and social content while creating motion graphics and branded assets for marketing campaigns across broadcast, streaming, digital, and social platforms. Your work will help shape how one of the country's leading local television brands connects with its audience.

 

The Promotions Editor works primarily in Adobe Premiere Pro, After Effects, and Avid Media Composer to turn news stories and station initiatives into polished promotions and marketing content. The ideal candidate is a strong visual storyteller who can manage multiple projects and collaborate with marketing producers and other stakeholders in a fast-paced local news environment.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Promotional Editing & Storytelling

  • Edit compelling promotional content for daily news, severe weather, investigations, special programming, station branding, and community initiatives.
  • Edit image campaigns for broadcast, streaming, social media, digital platforms, and paid marketing in formats suited to each channel.
  • Use music, pacing, sound design, and visual storytelling to maximize audience engagement.

Motion Design & Visual Branding

  • Design and animate high-quality motion graphics using Adobe After Effects.
  • Develop branded graphics, typography, transitions, and promotional assets for television, streaming, web, and social platforms.
  • Maintain a consistent and polished WSB-TV look across marketing channels.

Content Creation & Digital Media

  • Edit and adapt platform-specific content for Instagram Reels, TikTok, YouTube Shorts, Facebook, and emerging platforms.
  • Repurpose broadcast campaigns into social-first content designed to reach and engage more viewers.
  • Stay current on creative trends, editing techniques, storytelling styles, and social media best practices.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities (continued)

Creative Development & Collaboration

  • Collaborate with marketing producers, news leadership, digital teams, on-air talent, photographers, and other stakeholders to develop campaigns that connect with viewers.
  • Contribute fresh ideas for station initiatives, ratings periods, major news events, and community campaigns.
  • Help bring campaign concepts to life through editing, motion design, and content tailored to each platform.

Asset & Workflow Management

  • Organize and maintain project files, graphic templates, media libraries, and creative assets.
  • Manage multiple assignments while maintaining high creative standards.
  • Ensure deliverables meet technical specifications, brand standards, and platform requirements.
  • Prepare and deliver campaign assets to external media partners and agencies.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 2+ years of professional experience in video editing, motion design, creative services, broadcast promotion, digital media, or a related field.
  • Advanced proficiency in Adobe Premiere Pro and Adobe After Effects, with experience using Avid Media Composer.
  • Strong understanding of color correction, audio mixing, visual storytelling, branding, typography, composition, and motion design.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
  • Excellent communication, organization, and time-management skills.
  • Strong portfolio or demo reel showcasing editing, motion graphics, and creative storytelling.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in local television, news promotion, digital media, agency creative services, or content marketing.
  • Proficiency in Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator, or similar creative tools.
  • Knowledge of sound design and audience engagement best practices.
  • Photography, videography, or field production experience for assisting on occasional shoots is a plus.

  • Build strong partnerships across marketing, technology, BI, and data engineering as a trusted analytics voice in the room.

  • Champion data quality and integrity across every initiative you touch

job.title: Sales and Marketing Specialist
job.description:
This Job Description May Cause Extreme Excitement and Career Growth 

At AMP Sales & Marketing Solutions, we believe a great workplace isn't just something we say — it's something you can feel when you join the team. Here, it's all about great collabs, ambition, and results but most importantly, we grow here, and we enjoy here.  We're searching for that special someone — a driven, talented individual to join our innovative media sales team. In this role, you'll engage with new and existing clients and show them how our innovative media solutions can amplify their brands and deliver measurable success. If you're energized by building relationships, closing deals, and making an impact, we'd love to hear from you. 

 

Sound like the right fit? Check out the checklist below and if it sounds like you, hit "Apply Now" and let's chat. 

 

Your Day-to-Day (aka the Playbook) 

Help Brands Thrive: 

Join our media sales team and play a pivotal role in helping brands and companies grow. By identifying new opportunities, building strong client relationships, and delivering impactful solutions, you'll showcase how our multi-media content platforms and digital assets can drive meaningful results for our partners. 

 

Your focus will be on helping clients achieve their goals, ensuring that every campaign is a success. When our clients win, we win—and we believe in celebrating those victories together! 

  

Make Connections: Embrace your powers of persuasion and make every handshake and meeting count! Every interaction is a chance to build a genuine connection and show clients how we can help them succeed. You're not just selling; you're building partnerships. You're helping businesses find the right audience in the right place at the right time. When we say One Partner, Endless Possibilities, we mean it! 

 

Be A Trusted Guide: In this role, you'll connect with clients on a human level, understand their unique needs, and craft tailored sales and marketing solutions that deliver results. As their trusted advisor, you'll help them navigate the ever-evolving marketing landscape, ensuring every step of the journey is planned with care and precision.  

 

Shake Things Up: Bring your creativity and fresh ideas to the table! We're looking for someone who challenges the status quo, embraces innovation, and finds new ways to connect with our audience. Your contributions will help elevate our brand and drive meaningful results for your clients.  

 

Join us and Conquer the Media Landscape: You'll be part of a dedicated team of A1 media sales professionals, committed to achieving market leadership. Together, we amplify our impact, deliver exceptional outcomes, and help our clients succeed in ways that truly matter. 

 

Identify Emerging Opportunities: It's about being able to see what others can't, anticipating market shifts, analyzing data and predicting the next big thing. Your insights will position our clients and AMP for long-term success.  

  

What We're Looking For 

Proven Sales Ability (or an Unstoppable Desire to Learn) 

Whether you're a seasoned sales professional or just getting started, we value your drive, energy, and passion for achieving results. 

 

Strong Communication Skills: You're a natural at building relationships and communicating effectively. Proficiency with digital tools and applications is a must. 

 

A Passion for helping Others: You're committed to understanding clients' needs, providing top-notch customer service and making a difference. You're not just selling a product; you're providing a solution.  

 

A Competitive Spirit: Do you get a little boost when you achieve a goal (especially if it was a tough one)? We love that for you (and us)!  We want someone who's driven to excel but also knows how to celebrate the victories (big and small) with their team. That drive makes you a valuable part of our organization.  

 

A Willingness to Grow: Do you thrive in environments where you're always learning something new? Excellent, you'll fit right in! The media world is constantly evolving, and the ability to learn, adapt, and embrace challenges in a fast-paced, digital-first environment is key.  

 

The Practical Stuff 

A valid driver's license, up-to-date insurance, and reliable transportation are necessary for connecting with clients in your community. 

 

Why Join AMP Sales & Marketing Solutions? / The Reasons You Should Hit "Apply Now" 

 

Serious Work, Seriously Cool People: Be part of a dynamic team that values creativity, collaboration, and fun! We are all for work that is rewarding.  

 

The Compensation Package: 

This is a 100% commission-based role with a minimum salary compensation range between $50,000 - $60,000. Final compensation for this role will be determined by various factors such as a candidates’ relevant work experience, skills, certifications, and geographic location. Full time positions are eligible for benefits that include participation in a retirement plan, life and disability insurance, health, dental and vision plans, flexible spending accounts, sick leave, vacation time, personal time, parental leave and employee stock purchase plan.

 

We Make a Real Difference (Not Just Talk About It): At AMP, we help local businesses thrive through advertising strategies that create tangible impacts. Our media sales specialist isn't just selling ads; they're the boots on the ground, making a real difference where it counts. (And yes, it feels pretty good.) 

 

Top-Notch Training and Support: We're not the kind of company that hires you and then disappears into the corporate abyss. We carefully select candidates for a cohort-based training program, where you'll join a group of sales professionals from all over the country. From onboarding to ongoing mentorship, we invest in your success with training programs that set you up for long-term growth. 

 

Career Growth Opportunities: We believe in investing in you. That's why you'll have access to training, mentorship, and career advancement opportunities to help you thrive. We are a leader in our industry, flexing our local charm and national muscle, providing you with options to amplify your career in your local market or join one of our AMP Sales & Marketing Solutions teams in another city.  

 

Comprehensive Media Education (We Are Your Power Source!): New to the industry? We've got you covered with training programs that turn curiosity into expertise.   

 

AMP is us. It's you. It isn't just a name; it's a mission. A promise to amplify our reach, amplify our innovation, and most importantly, amplify you. If you're ready to grow your career and help businesses achieve their goals, we'd love to hear from you.  

 

EEO AND INCLUSIVITY

Employment practices will not be inﬂuenced or aﬀected by virtue of an applicant's or employee's race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity, and sexual orientation), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, military or veteran status or any other characteristic protected by law.

job.description:
Senior Product Manager, Revenue and Ad Tech

Seattle, WA (Local Hybrid)

Sinclair Inc. Is seeking a Senior Product Manager, Revenue and Ad Tech. This role is responsible for Sinclair's digital advertising technology and programmatic revenue systems. This role combines people leadership, product-minded planning, revenue governance, and technical oversight to deliver reliable, scalable, resilient, and cost-effective monetization capabilities across digital platforms.

The manager establishes quarterly goals and releases, ensures the accuracy of revenue reporting, oversees key vendor services, and maintains clear communication with stakeholders. The role is also accountable for team performance, professional development, and fostering a culture of collaboration and continuous improvement.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead, coach, and develop Revenue and Ad Tech team members; set expectations and manage performance.
  • Build and maintain the Revenue and Ad Tech roadmap, release plan, quarterly goals, and success measures.
  • Oversee Ad Tech and programmatic advertising systems, services, and vendor relationships.
  • Establish controls that support accurate, timely, and defensible revenue reporting.
  • Ensure systems and operating processes are reliable, scalable, resilient, and cost-effective.
  • Prioritize initiatives based on revenue impact, customer needs, effort, risk, and strategic alignment.
  • Communicate progress, tradeoffs, risks, and decisions to leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Advertising Operations, Data, Finance, Legal, and business teams.
  • Guide incident response and root-cause follow-up for material ad delivery or revenue issues.
  • Promote documentation, feedback, knowledge sharing, and continuous process improvement.

 

Qualifications:

  • Demonstrated experience leading people and complex technical or revenue-focused work.
  • Deep understanding of digital advertising, programmatic monetization, and ad-serving ecosystems.
  • Strong working knowledge of Google Ad Manager and related measurement, reporting, and partner platforms.
  • Ability to manage roadmaps, releases, quarterly goals, dependencies, risks, and competing priorities.
  • Experience establishing revenue reporting controls and translating data into business decisions.
  • Sound vendor management, negotiation, and service governance skills.
  • Clear executive communication and the ability to make technical concepts actionable for varied audiences.
  • Strong judgment, accountability, and commitment to developing others.

 

Please note that this position is not eligible for visa sponsorship, including employer sponsorship for an H-1B visa, OPT-STEM employment, etc.

job.title: Senior Union Payroll Associate
job.description:
The Senior Union Payroll Associate performs a variety of functions necessary for the accurate and timely processing of multi-state, multi-company, weekly and bi-weekly payrolls for union and non-union freelance employees. The Senior Union Payroll Associate coordinates, validates, and implements work procedures that require comprehensive operational knowledge of union collective bargaining agreements and federal and state regulations related to wage garnishment, taxation and wage‐hour law.


While there are no direct people responsibilities, the Senior Union Payroll Associate will coordinate independently with other associates, leaders, and teams outside of Payroll Shared Services to accomplish tasks, meet deadlines, champion process improvement initiatives, and enhance the employee experience.


A SNAPSHOT OF YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Perform all duties necessary to ensure timely and accurate processing of multi-state, multi-company weekly and bi-weekly payrolls for union and non-union freelance employees in accordance with collective bargaining agreements and other contracts and in compliance with applicable FOX policies and federal, state, and local regulations
  • Process on demand payments, retroactive payments, one-time payments, tax adjustments, stop payments, void checks, direct deposit reversals, and overpayment collections in accordance with FOX policies, collective bargaining agreements, and in compliance with federal, state, and local regulations
  • Interpret and set up withholding orders for levies, garnishments, child support, and other involuntary wage assignment orders in the payroll system within the regulated period
  • Understand union pay and paid time off rules and the timekeeping system and address employee questions as needed
  • Provide testing support during the implementation of the new timekeeping system and assist with team training
  • Perform detailed pre-payroll processing audits of earnings, deductions, benefits, garnishments, and tax setups to prevent pay-impacting errors when payroll is processed
  • Audit and reconcile union-related inputs, including union dues, initiation fees, and retirement contributions, to ensure accuracy and strict adherence to collective bargaining agreements
  • Understand proper taxation of all employee payments, including employer paid union benefits, and address employee questions as needed
  • Review, test, and update Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) regularly to ensure operational accuracy, compliance, and continuous process efficiency
  • Provide subject matter expertise on union timekeeping rules and processes, to include paid time off plans. This requires the ability to interpret rules outlined in collective bargaining agreements (CBAs) and other union related documents
  • Assist employees and management with questions, concerns, or requests regarding union payroll. This includes properly applying technical knowledge and skills, communicating, and listening effectively
  • Serve as a go-to expert for union payroll questions, managing the timely resolution of customer issues, including handling customer escalations, performing and documenting Root Cause Analysis, and implementing remedial procedures to close gaps identified
  • Ensure compliance with all company policies, internal controls, and SOX controls

WHAT YOU WILL NEED

  • 4+ years hands-on union payroll processing experience, preferably with IBEW, IATSE, AFTRA, and/or NABET collective bargaining agreements
  • Experience with interpreting and setting up withholding orders for levies, garnishments, child support, and other involuntary wage assignment orders
  • Experience and knowledge of automated time and attendance systems
  • Experience with initiating and leading standardization and process improvement initiatives
  • Strong working knowledge of FLSA, federal, state, and local wage and hour and tax regulations. 
  • Ability to interpret collective bargaining agreements for pay and paid time off rules.
  • Strong interpersonal skills – you are approachable, responsive, and team focused
  • Intermediate Excel using VLOOKUP and pivots.
  • Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written
  • Excellent judgment, analytical and problem-solving skills
  • High degree of professionalism and solid ability in delivering high quality customer service and establishing/maintaining effective and collaborative working relationships

NICE TO HAVE BUT NOT A DEALBREAKER

  • Fundamental Payroll Certification (FPC) or Certified Payroll Professional (CPP) designation
  • Experience with Workday Payroll

We will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories consistent with applicable law.

job.title: Manager, Corporate Audit
job.description:
The Manager, Corporate Audit, will be a key member of FOX's Corporate Audit Department. Reporting to the Senior Director, Internal Controls, the Manager will be responsible for the execution of various fieldwork components of the Corporate Audit Plan and SOX Program. This role would be based out of FOX's New York Office, with ongoing collaboration with the team members in Los Angeles.

A SNAPSHOT OF YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

job.title: Regional Streaming Director
job.description:
FOX Television Stations is growing its streaming operation, and the Florida region is a critical part of that growth. This role sits at the center of that effort — serving as the streaming authority for FOX Tampa (WTVT) and FOX Orlando (WOFL), responsible for building and evolving a high-performing local streaming operation across both markets.

Reporting to the News Director(s) at WTVT & WOFL, this position works in close partnership with FTS Streaming and weather leadership to align regional execution with broader FTS strategy and the Executive Producers of both FL stations. As the streaming team grows and the business evolves, so will this role — expanding in scope, team size, and responsibility. The right candidate is someone who is ready to grow with it.

This is a role for a streaming-first leader who understands where the industry is heading, knows how to bring a newsroom along on that journey, and has the editorial instincts, technical fluency, and analytical rigor to drive measurable growth across the full streaming universe — CTV, FAST channels, and social video.

A Snapshot of Your Responsibilities - Editorial & Content Leadership

  • Lead with a streaming-first mindset across both newsrooms, driving editorial vision, cultural adoption, and a commitment to continuous content improvement.
  • Make fast, sound editorial decisions in breaking news environments, balancing urgency with accuracy.
  • Manage and evolve streaming programming schedules across Tampa and Orlando, working toward expanded hours and a long-term 24/7 weather and streaming operation at both stations.
  • Elevate content quality at every level — from live breaking news to long-form storytelling — with an eye toward what works for a streaming-native audience.
  • Operate fluidly across digital and streaming, shaping content intentionally for each format and platform.

Team Development & Newsroom Adoption

  • Motivate, coach, and develop a team of streaming journalists and producers in Tampa, and support alignment with the Orlando & Tampa Executive Producers of Streaming.
  • Serve as the leading voice in both newsrooms for streaming adoption — building buy-in, growing participation, and helping teams evolve their workflows and mindset to support expanded streaming output.
  • Partner with the station and FTS Executive Director of Streaming to identify opportunities to grow the team and the operation over time.

Analytics & Performance Reporting

  • Own streaming performance data and reporting for the FL region across all platforms — including FOX Local CTV, FAST channels, YouTube, social video, and weather.
  • Produce regular growth reports for both stations, surfacing trends, opportunities, and areas that need attention.
  • Use real-time and historical data to inform editorial decisions, optimize audience engagement, and support the case for expanded resources and investment in the region.
  • Provide regular performance and strategy updates to FTS Streaming leadership to ensure regional activity is visible and aligned with company goals.

Technology & Distribution

  • Master and expand the use of TriCaster and all streaming production technology across both markets.
  • Maintain a comprehensive understanding of the full streaming distribution landscape — CTV, FAST channels, and social video — and ensure both stations are operating effectively across all surfaces.
  • Prioritize the CTV viewer experience: ensure content is surfaced intentionally, programming decisions are made with audience growth in mind, and both stations are actively working to drive viewers toward longer-form, high-value content.
  • Stay attuned to how platforms, discovery mechanisms, and viewer habits are shifting, and bring that awareness into day-to-day and long-term planning.

Strategy & Industry Awareness

  • Serve as the regional expert on streaming industry trends — platform evolution, audience behavior, competitive landscape, and emerging opportunities.
  • Develop and execute short- and long-term streaming growth strategies for the FL region, aligned with FTS goals and built to adapt as the industry and business change.
  • Collaborate across FOX and with external content partners, contributors, and creators to expand live coverage opportunities.

What You Will Need

  • 5+ years in a digital or broadcast news leadership role; live streaming or CTV experience strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of the full streaming landscape: CTV, FAST channels, OTT platforms, social video, and mobile apps.
  • Proven ability to lead teams through high-stakes breaking news and live events.
  • Strong analytical skills with experience building and presenting performance reports across multiple streaming platforms and distribution surfaces.
  • Deep understanding of CTV user experience and content distribution strategy, with a viewer-first approach to programming and platform decisions.
  • Proficiency with streaming production technology; TriCaster experience strongly preferred.
  • A streaming-first editorial mindset with the ability to work fluidly across digital, and streaming formats.
  • Current knowledge of streaming industry trends, audience behavior shifts, and platform evolutions.
  • Excellent editorial judgment and strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to drive newsroom culture change and build enthusiasm for streaming at all levels.
  • Flexibility to work varied hours, weekends, and holidays as news demands.
