job.title: Customer Support Specialist
job.description:
We are UMG, the Universal Music Group. We are the world’s leading music company. In everything we do, we are committed to artistry, innovation and entrepreneurship. We own and operate a broad array of businesses engaged in recorded music, music publishing, merchandising, and audiovisual content in more than 60 countries. We identify and develop recording artists and songwriters, and we produce, distribute and promote the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful music to delight and entertain fans around the world.
 

CD Baby is the world’s largest digital distribution platform for independent artists. For more than 20 years, we’ve empowered creators to release their music to Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, Amazon Music, Instagram, TikTok, and 150+ other platforms worldwide—paying out nearly $1 billion in earnings directly to independent artists.


Built by artists, for artists, we’re a mission-driven, artist-first company, and we’re expanding our Support team with experienced, detail-oriented problem-solvers who care deeply about helping creators succeed.


How we LEAD:

As a Customer Support Specialist, you’ll handle our most complex support inquiries, serving as an escalation point for high-impact issues involving royalties, metadata, distribution workflows, rights management, account configuration, and platform compliance.


You’ll be an expert in the independent music ecosystem and CD Baby’s product suite, capable of diagnosing nuanced, multi-layered problems and communicating solutions clearly and empathetically.


You’ll report to our Customer Support Manager, and work closely with the rest of the Customer Support team and cross-functional partners to improve workflows, provide insights, and elevate the overall quality and consistency of the CD Baby artist experience.


How You’ll CREATE:

Expert Support & Escalation Handling

  • Manage complex customer cases, including advanced revenue issues, delivery failures, content policy blocks, and technical issues.
  • Troubleshoot multi-product, multi-stakeholder issues requiring deep system knowledge and cross-team coordination.
  • Provide accurate, timely, empathetic email support that upholds CD Baby’s artist-first values.
  • Maintain expert-level knowledge of CD Baby’s products, distribution pipelines, publishing, copyright, monetization, and related industry topics.
  • Communicate with professionalism, clarity, and empathy in every interaction.

Operational & Process Improvement

  • Identify recurring issues, workflow gaps, and opportunities for automation or simplification.
  • Surface actionable insights to the Customer Support Manager, CX Operations Manager, and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Contribute to improving policies, SOPs, and troubleshooting frameworks.

Knowledge & Documentation

  • Maintain expert-level knowledge of CD Baby’s distribution pipelines, monetization, and digital service provider (DSP) requirements.
  • Collaborate on updates to macros, internal SOPs, and customer-facing documentation to ensure clarity and accuracy.
  • Contribute to support documentation and internal resources (macros, SOPs, training guides).

Cross-functional Collaboration

  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Digital Operations, and Marketing to resolve escalations that involve system bugs, content policy questions, or distribution exceptions.
  • Participate in case reviews and knowledge-sharing sessions to strengthen Support team expertise.
  • Provide insight into recurring customer pain points, workflow gaps, product issues, and documentation needs.

Customer Experience Leadership

  • Model best-in-class communication standards across empathy, clarity, tone, and personalization.
  • Mentor associates through shadowing, pairing, and informal guidance as needed.
  • Help uphold a culture of continuous learning, artist advocacy, and operational excellence.
  • Collaborate with the Customer Support Manager on quality assurance, training opportunities, and improvements to customer experience.

Bring your VIBE:

  • 2–4 years experience in customer support, operations, or technical troubleshooting—preferably in music, tech, SaaS, or digital media.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to break down complex issues into clear next steps.
  • Exceptional written communication—concise, empathetic, and tailored to artist needs.
  • Familiarity with digital music distribution, publishing, copyright, royalties, or DSP ecosystems (a strong plus).
  • Comfort working in ticketing systems and internal tooling (e.g., Zendesk, Jira, CRM platforms).
  • Detail-oriented, organized, and able to thrive in a fast-paced, high-volume environment.
  • A passion for helping independent artists succeed and a deep respect for the artist community.

Perks Playlist:

Join an entrepreneurial, global organization where authenticity, boldness, creativity, connection, drive, and insight aren’t just values—they’re how we work every day. Here are some of the ways we support you along the way (and just a few of the benefits we offer):

  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage

  • Including 100% coverage for out-patient in-network mental health services

  • Fertility coverage for eligible medical plan participants

  • Wellbeing reimbursements for fitness classes, spa treatments, meal services, travel, and so much more (up to $720/year)

  • Student Loan Repayment Assistance and Tuition Reimbursement

  • 401(k) with 100% immediate vesting on the first 5% of your contributions, plus an additional UMG contribution

A variety of ways to prioritize much-needed time away from work including:

  • Flexible Paid Time Off (PTO) for exempt employees

  • 3-weeks PTO for non-exempt employees

  • 2-weeks paid Winter Break

  • 10 Company Holidays (including Juneteenth and Wellbeing Day)

  • Summer Fridays (between Memorial Day and Labor Day)

  • Generous paid parental leave for every type of parent

job.title: Graphics Multimedia Editor, Open-source Reporting
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times Graphics team is looking for a reporter with extensive open-source and investigative reporting skills to turn raw evidence into impactful visual stories. You have a track record for uncovering exclusive information off the news.

The Graphics team is a leader in using spatial and visual techniques on investigative stories, and we're looking for someone who is passionate about accountability journalism using cutting-edge reporting techniques.

Below are a few examples of the kinds of stories that you will be a part of:
  • An exclusive look at the failed columns of the Midtown Manhattan near-collapse
  • A 3-D analysis of why firefighters' lines of sight were limited in the deadly LaGuardia Crash
  • An investigation into the mass graves in Syria
  • An investigation into the causes of a Miami building collapse
  • A spatial investigation into a deadly fire in the Bronx
  • A forensic analysis of an apartment building collapse in the Turkey earthquake
Working with journalists on the Graphics team and across the newsroom, you will play an important role in shaping visual reconstructions and investigations that rely on spatial analysis or use 3-D modeling. You will gather and analyze evidence for stories across a wide range of topics for both quick-turn stories as well as longer-term enterprise.

You will be expected to take the initiative in leading major storylines, with the goal of uncovering new or exclusive findings across multiple visual story formats. You should be curious and driven, and be comfortable with moving between solo deep dives and fast-paced, cross-desk collaborations.

This is an in-office position based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days a week.

Responsibilities:
  • Bring core OSINT fluency to the desk's coverage: geolocation, chronolocation, satellite/aerial imagery analysis, audio-video research, and more.
  • Analyze a variety of data sources, including satellite and aerial imagery, flight/vessel tracking data, social media platforms and radio scanner data.
  • Vet and build relationships with a network of sources on stories.
  • Generate ideas that help the team develop custom tooling to automate open-source reporting for analyzing and visualizing evidence.
  • Find new ways to report beyond the standard OSINT toolkit, by using computational techniques, including through machine learning, computer vision and approved AI tools.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to an Assistant Editor on the Graphics desk.
Basic Qualifications:
  • 5+ years of relevant experience as an investigative reporter, open-source researcher or forensic expert.
  • Proven experience conducting open-source investigations by sourcing audio and visual evidence across a variety of platforms.
  • Experience producing accountability journalism, with a strong portfolio.
  • Experience producing clear copy about the visual evidence on tight deadlines.
  • Experience verifying user-generated content from social media for authenticity.
  • Skilled in building timelines using a variety of sources, including official statements and metadata from user-generated content.
  • Familiarity with open-source intelligence tools and techniques like Google Earth, satellite imagery platforms, scanner audio data, flight or vessel tracking, or similar.
Preferred Qualifications:
  • Experience working both independently and collaboratively while managing multiple research threads.
  • Experience with advanced tools for reporting, such as QGIS, Blender for 3-D scene reconstructions, data analysis methods, audio and image forensics tools.
  • Adept at creating clear, visual explainers piecing together complex findings.
  • Familiarity with programming and custom tool development.
  • Familiarity with Adobe Suite and Figma.
  • Experience with web scraping tools and working with APIs.
  • Experience using command line tools.
  • Willingness and flexibility to work evenings and weekends as needed.
This position is represented by the NewsGuild of NY.   REQ-020693

job.title: Staff Software Engineer, Application Delivery
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role

The Developer Platforms mission at The New York Times builds the foundational platforms, tooling, and paved paths that help product teams ship high‑quality experiences quickly and safely. Our Application Delivery team owns the shared software delivery platform (CI/CD, artifact management) and deployment workflows used by hundreds of engineers across News, Cooking, Games and Audio to ship software.

As the Times leans into AI‑assisted and agentic development, Application Delivery is where those changes become real. You will set the technical direction for how AI‑generated and agent‑driven change flows safely, observably, and at scale through CI/CD.

You'll help teams reduce release risk with modern deployment patterns, and turn effective delivery practices into reusable pipelines and templates that scale across the organization, much like our GenAI platform roles turn internal practices into reusable tools and agents. When you improve this platform, you change how The New York Times ships software.

You will report to the Engineering Manager of the DevEx Application Delivery team. This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days/week.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the technical direction of software delivery as a shared product: shape paved paths in our shared platform that improve code health, release quality, and delivery speed for product teams.

  • Set the technical direction for agent‑ready delivery: design the policy, guardrails, and paved paths that turn AI‑generated and agent‑driven changes (migrations, test generation, pipeline maintenance) into safe, observable releases at scale by partnering with our Developer AI team.

  • Collaborate with Product, engineering leaders, and internal users to shape the roadmap for the delivery platform and bring measurable impact on quality and speed.

  • Deliver scalable, secure, and observable software delivery systems and workflows that improve reliability, and overall software quality and velocity.

  • Champion engineering excellence in delivery by setting best practices for testing, deployment strategies, progressive delivery, and observability that are easy to adopt through the platform.

  • Mentor engineers across the mission, contribute to hiring, and help foster an inclusive, collaborative engineering culture centered on shared platforms and high‑quality software delivery.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our mission and values and a commitment to our purpose to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience building the technical strategy and driving software delivery (Github Actions, Argo CD or equivalent CI/CD systems) or similar platform work with broad organizational impact beyond operations.

  • Experience building and scaling a platform as a product for internal engineers with multi-tenancy serving many teams through self‑service paved paths, with attention to adoption, backward compatibility, and isolation/guardrails between tenants

  • Demonstrated proficiency in building and maintaining production services in one or more general‑purpose programming languages (e.g., Go, Python, TypeScript/Node.js, or Java), including code review and debugging complex issues.

  • 5+ years of experience with containers, Kubernetes, package management tools(Helm or equivalent), IAC tools(Terraform or equivalent), Gitops‑based deployment workflows and cloud services such as AWS, GCP.

  • Experience using delivery and productivity metrics (e.g., DORA, SPACE) and platform observability to measure and improve release quality and delivery.

  • Proficiency with GenAI‑assisted developer tooling (e.g., Cursor, Copilot, or Claude Code) and judgment about how to integrate agentic workflows into CI/CD safely.

  • Experience leading cross‑team technical work, communicating trade‑offs, and building understanding among diverse partners including Product, platform, and product engineering teams.

  • Experience mentoring engineers and contributing to an inclusive, collaborative engineering culture.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Exposure to artifact/package management (e.g., Artifactory or similar) with attention to security, retention, cost, and ease of use for engineers.

Benefits include medical, dental and vision benefits, Flexible Spending Accounts (F.S.A.s), a company-matching 401(k) plan, employee stock purchase plan, paid vacation, paid sick days, paid parental leave, tuition reimbursement and professional development programs.

job.title: Sr. Manager, Policy
job.description: About Suno We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world. Building the future of entertainment requires ambition. The pace is fast, the problems are hard, and the work demands ownership and intensity. For the right people, it’s incredibly rewarding: a chance to shape a new medium, work with a small team that cares deeply about quality, make music, drink too much coffee, and build something that millions of people use to express themselves in ways that were never before possible. Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA). Suno exists to unlock the joy of making music. Millions of people use Suno to turn ideas into songs, and our platform generates music at a scale no moderation playbook was written for. We believe AI amplifies and empowers the people who make music, and keeping that ecosystem safe, fair, and trusted is core to the product, not a cost center bolted onto it. Listen to the Suno version of this role! https://suno.com/s/4IWNXlPv9MXDsCQe The role You will lead Trust & Safety Policy at Suno. Directly building and shaping our policies, you will also partner with PM, Eng, and Legal to understand the impact policies have on detection and remediation of violative content, fraud, bots, and identity issues, while also navigating music rights and our regulatory obligations. Generation volume grows faster than any human review model can, so we focus on policies that enable our enforcement systems to scale with the platform, hold it to a high degree of accuracy, and understand what decisions cost. You will report to the Head of Trust & Safety and partner regularly with Comms, Product, Engineering, ML, and Legal. What you'll do Own the Trust & Safety policy portfolio end to end: content and behavior policies, enforcement standards, and the policy roadmap as generation volume and product surface area grow. Write policy that machines can enforce: translate principles into decision criteria, model thresholds and reviewer guidance that produce consistent outcomes at millions of generations per day. Own policy for the hard genAI music problems: artist voice impersonation, rights-adjacent abuse, synthetic content disclosure and prompt-level misuse, in partnership with Legal. Turn regulatory obligations (DSA, OSA and emerging AI-content regimes) into enforceable internal policy and audit-ready documentation, in partnership with Legal. Run the policy development lifecycle: risk assessment, stakeholder review, launch guidance, enforcement calibration and post-launch measurement of policy effectiveness. Set the escalation and edge-case framework: who decides what, on what timeline, with what precedent, so novel cases become policy instead of one-off judgment calls. Publish externally when it counts: community guidelines, transparency reporting inputs, and policy explanations creators can actually understand. Partner with Product and Engineering early so policy shapes features before launch rather than cleaning up after them. What you'll bring 7+ years in trust & safety, platform policy, or integrity work, including 3+ years owning a policy domain at a UGC or generative AI platform. A portfolio of policies you wrote that shipped and held up: you can walk through the risk assessment, the enforcement design, and what you changed after launch data came in. Demonstrated experience making policy machine-enforceable: decision trees, model threshold input, labeling taxonomies or reviewer guidance that produced measurable consistency gains. Fluency in the regulatory landscape shaping platform policy (DSA, OSA and emerging AI-content regimes) and a record of converting obligations into operational requirements rather than memos. Working knowledge of music rights, IP or media licensing sufficient to write credible policy alongside Legal without needing them to hold the pen. Evidence of moving Product, Engineering and Legal to adopt policy positions they did not start with. Writing that operators, executives and regulators can each use: precise enough to enforce, clear enough to defend publicly. Nice to have Music, media, or IP-adjacent platform experience and fluency in rights-matching abuse patterns. Direct exposure to DSA, OSA, or emerging AI-content regulatory regimes as operational requirements. job.description:

Job Description

Are you passionate about the chance to bring your analysis experience to a world class organization that is leading the way in both content and technology to serve and protect our citizens home and abroad?  Do you have the skills necessary provide research and expertise to the national security community, the US military, law enforcement, and the private sector? job.description:
Job Description


As a Software Engineer on the Litigation Drafting team you will be building the next generation of AI agentic product for legal professionals. The team takes early Labs concepts and turns them into scalable, production-ready features.  You will be developing a product which is pushing the boundaries of agentic design by incorporating an complex workflow UI and a specialized Legal agent.

This role is aimed at someone early in their career who wants to move quickly. You will get real ownership sooner than is typical, you will be expected to use AI tooling to multiply what one engineer can deliver - your ceiling is set by how fast you learn rather than by how long you have been doing this. This role is focused on back-end skills but there is the opportunity to get front end developer experience to develop into a full-stack engineer


We are looking for team players with a strong sense of urgency and a desire to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment who will drive the delivery of timely solutions.  You are empowered to try new approaches and learn new technologies. You will have agency to contribute innovative ideas, create solutions, and will be accountable for end-to-end deliveries. 


Key Responsibilities:

  • Build and ship AI Agentic features end to end: Take a feature from a written requirement through design, implementation, code review and production. You will operate with a moderate level of guidance and own straightforward projects outright.
  • Design and build backend services using Python, FastAPI, and PostgreSQL to support real-time AI interactions and large-scale data flows, with direct contribution to AI-powered capabilities such as agentic workflows, LLM orchestration, and content pipelines. 
  • Productionize AI Capabilities: Integrate with modern LLM providers (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic) and implement reliable orchestration, routing, error handling, guardrails, telemetry, and deep observability for performance and reliability. Strengthen CI/CD pipelines and DevOps automation to support fast, stable, cloud‑native development workflows.
  • Use AI as a force multiplier: Apply AI coding and testing tooling to your own work, and help build AI capabilities into the product itself. Translate business requirements into solutions that use AI where it is the right answer, and do not where it is not.
  • Diagnose and fix: Read unfamiliar code, run root cause analysis, troubleshoot production behavior, and act on issues raised by automated code quality inspection.
  • Raise the quality bar: Contribute to automated testing strategy and to continuous integration and delivery pipelines, treating test coverage as part of a feature rather than as a follow-up.
  • Collaborate across functions: Participate actively in design discussions, agile ceremonies and cross-team work with Product, design and Labs teams
  • Help others as you grow: Share what you learn, support colleagues on problems you have already solved, and contribute to a team culture where learning out loud is normal.

Required Qualifications

  • Technical Experience; 1-3+ years of professional software development experience.
  • Backend & Cloud Skills: Working knowledge of Python, and experience in AWS, Azure or GCP Cloud services. Solid understanding of RESTful API design, distributed systems and microservices architecture. Experience working with SQL and NoSQL databases.
  • Technical Judgment: Excellent debugging skills and a proven ability to deliver production-ready, highly reliable systems. 
  • Collaboration & Communication: Comfortable operating in fast-paced, iterative environments, with strong cross-functional communication skills. 
  • Evidence that you learn fast. Be ready to point to something specific you taught yourself and then shipped, and to explain how you went about it.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • BA or BS in Computer Science or equivalent practical experience 
  • Experience with performance optimization for backend systems, including monitoring, profiling, and tuning for scale 
  • Hands-on experience building AI-powered product features, ideally agentic AI workflows including multi-step reasoning. Using tool/API orchestrations, LLM APIs, RAG pipelines, Claude Agent SDK / AgentCore at runtime
  • Experience with Agentic UI - SSE/AG-UI streaming semantics, TypeScript/React
  • Experience with Datadog (logs/RUM/traces), CloudWatch Log Insights, and Braintrust
  • Familiarity with AI/ML infrastructure including vector databases, model serving, and cost/latency optimization for LLM-powered features 
  • Experience testing, automation, and operational robustness

job.title: Senior Software Engineer, Full Stack
job.description:
Senior Software Engineer, Full Stack

The global capital markets are among the largest markets in the world valued at $50T+ and growing. Transactions in these markets are complex. Critical, nuanced legal terms are woven into lengthy documents. These documents must be digested and analyzed by many different parties over the course of a single transaction and multiple decisions are made based on the terms laid out and quantitative and qualitative attributes within. This fundamental need plus a booming market drives enormous demand for precise extraction and benchmarking of legal terms.

As a Senior Software Engineer, Full Stack at Thomson Reuters - Noetica, you'll help build robust backend systems and APIs that power our search-centric web experience that’s core to the workflow of our end users. This role is backend-leaning — you'll spend most of your time on server-side architecture, data processing, and API design, while also contributing to frontend features as needed. You will collaborate with a talented team of AI/ML PhDs, legal SMEs, and market strategists to design, build, and maintain scalable backend services. The backend service you will contribute to is the critical piece between our data product and our end users. Its system architecture decisions will influence the technical direction of our platform and decide our velocity of making impacts. Your contributions will directly impact the performance and reliability of Noetica's core infrastructure.

 

About the role,

As a Senior Software Engineer, Full Stack, you will:

  • Design and build scalable backend services and APIs that power our document analysis platform

  • Write maintainable, high-performance server-side code and data processing pipelines

  • Define clear, efficient API contracts and contribute to service architecture decisions

  • Design and craft compositional API primitives to expedite the productionization of our ever growing list of document insights.

  • Build and maintain integrations with third-party services and internal ML systems

  • Contribute to frontend features and components as needed to deliver features end to end

  • Work on performance optimization for data-intensive backend operations

  • Take ownership in engineering excellence and collaborate on code practices and design patterns to ensure long-term maintainability and scalability.

  • Take ownership in developer experience by improving/automating CI/CD and other day to day production operations.

About You:
You’re fit for the role of Senior Software Engineer, Full Stack if your background includes:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field (or equivalent experience)

  • 4+ years of professional full-stack development experience with a strong focus on backend systems

Senior Counsel, Engineering & Technology 

  

Are you looking for an opportunity to provide practical legal counsel on cutting-edge engineering initiatives, emerging technologies, and strategic technology investments? Thomson Reuters is seeking a Senior Counsel, Engineering & Technology to join our General Counsel’s Office. In this role, you will support Thomson Reuters’ Engineering and Technology organization, including our Innovation Labs, by advising on legal, regulatory, and reputational risks across the technology development lifecycle, including software engineering, platform architecture, emerging technology research, technology partnerships, and emerging areas of law. This position may be based in our U.S. offices in Minneapolis or Dallas, or in our Canadian office in Toronto.

In this opportunity as a Senior Counsel, Engineering & Technology, you will: 

  • Advise engineering and technology partners on legal issues arising across the technology development lifecycle, from concept through deployment, for new platforms, systems, and technical capabilities across Thomson Reuters’ products and services.

  • Build scalable legal resources: Create, update, and deliver training materials, playbooks, templates, and other legal resources for engineering, technology, and Innovation Labs partners.

job.description:
Thomson Reuters is looking for a Staff Software Engineer, AI Product Engineering to help shape and build the next generation of AI-powered software for tax and accounting professionals. You will join the CoCounsel for Tax & Accounting organization, working in a fast-moving, product-focused environment that combines startup-style ownership with the scale and resources of Thomson Reuters.

This is a highly hands-on Staff-level engineering role for someone who thrives in greenfield and 0→1 product development. You will be expected to take ambiguous product and technical problems, define the right architecture, build critical parts of the solution yourself, and help guide other engineers from prototype through production.

This is a hybrid role, with opportunities based in New York City, Minneapolis–St. Paul, or Toronto. Candidates should be comfortable working onsite as part of the team’s hybrid schedule. Final interviews may also be conducted onsite at the hiring hub associated with the candidate’s location.

About the Role

As a Staff Software Engineer, AI Product Engineering, you will:

  • Own greenfield and 0→1 AI systems, taking ambiguous product problems from technical discovery and architecture through implementation, production launch, monitoring, and iteration.

  • Design and build production backend services using Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, and AWS.

  • Build and evolve AI-native applications incorporating large language models, AI agents, orchestration, retrieval, tool/function calling, and real-time AI workflows.

  • Integrate models and services from providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, and other foundation-model platforms.

  • Design scalable APIs, data models, asynchronous workflows, and distributed services for high-volume, production-grade AI applications.

  • Establish reusable engineering patterns and technical standards that improve consistency and velocity across multiple teams or workstreams.

  • Evaluate AI behavior in production and build mechanisms for quality measurement, experimentation, evaluation, guardrails, and continuous improvement.

  • Partner closely with Product and Design to translate complex customer problems into simple, scalable technical solutions.

  • Provide technical leadership across complex, cross-functional initiatives while remaining hands-on in design, implementation, debugging, and code review.

  • Mentor engineers, raise the technical bar, and help teams make sound architectural and engineering trade-offs.

  • Identify technical risks early and drive solutions across multiple systems or teams.

You are a strong fit for this role if you have:

  • Significant software engineering experience building and operating large-scale, production-grade backend systems.

  • Strong, recent hands-on development experience with Python.

  • Production experience with backend frameworks such as FastAPI, Flask, or Django, with FastAPI strongly preferred.

  • Experience designing APIs, backend services, data models, asynchronous systems, and distributed architectures.

  • Experience with relational databases such as PostgreSQL and building production systems on a major cloud platform; AWS experience is strongly preferred.

  • Demonstrated experience personally designing, building, and launching greenfield or 0→1 products and systems, with clear ownership from architecture through production.

  • Experience making architecture decisions that affect multiple systems, teams, or major product capabilities.

  • Strong system-design skills with the ability to reason through scalability, reliability, performance, failure modes, and operational trade-offs.

  • Experience taking software through the full lifecycle, including architecture, implementation, deployment, observability, debugging, incident response, and production iteration.

  • Demonstrated ability to influence technical direction without relying on formal authority.

  • Strong communication skills and experience partnering effectively across Engineering, Product, Design, AI/ML, and other technical stakeholders.

  • Ability to operate effectively in ambiguous, fast-moving environments and turn incomplete requirements into clear technical direction.

  • Hands-on production experience building generative AI or AI-native applications is strongly preferred.

  • Experience with LLM-powered agents, agent orchestration, tool/function calling, RAG, embeddings, vector search, retrieval systems, or real-time AI interactions is preferred.

  • Experience integrating commercial or open foundation models, including OpenAI, Anthropic, or similar providers, is preferred.

job.description:
Thomson Reuters is building the AI platform that will power the next decade of tax, accounting and audit products, including CoCounsel Audit, a suite of AI‑native products used by accountants on real client work every day. As a Lead Software Engineer (Staff Engineer), you will own core backend and AI orchestration systems that turn frontier models into reliable, production‑grade workflows at scale. This role is for the CoCounsel for Audit team, formed from the recent acquisition of the startup Materia.

About the role:

You will be a Lead Software Engineer (Staff Engineer) responsible for the backend and orchestration layer powering AI agents, conversations, workspaces, and knowledge base across CoCounsel for Audit.

  • Shape the team's AI platform and patterns: Define patterns for building MCP servers, designing agents, novel uses of LLMs, experimentation, and scalable infrastructure. Your decisions will influence your product area and adjacent teams, not just a single feature.
  • Shape the platform integration strategy across new and existing Thomson Reuters audit systems to provide world-class content and solutions for our customers.
  • Work at real production scale: Build and evolve systems that operate over millions of documents, highly structured tax data, ever-changing laws, and thousands of concurrent AI interactions from accountants doing time‑sensitive work.
  • Small team, big surface area: Join a tight group of senior engineers and researchers shipping quickly, with direct access to product leadership and customers. Think ownership of a startup with the runway of a public company.
  • Great fit for people who enjoy and thrive at setting technical direction, mentoring senior engineers, and spending most of their time in the code and architecture of AI systems.

What you'll do:

Technical leadership and cross‑functional influence

  • Lead multi‑quarter initiatives that cut across AI, product, and infra (e.g., a new orchestration layer, a low-latency retrieval system, or a unified knowledge base).
  • Mentor senior and mid-level engineers, raising the bar on system design, code quality, and AI integration practices across the org.
  • Be a go-to expert in new model capabilities, collaborating closely with AI/ML engineers, researchers, designers, and PMs to translate industry improvements into reliable, user‑facing workflows that accountants trust.
  • Help shape the team’s roadmap, technical strategy, and engineering culture – from experimentation practices to testing, rollout, and postmortems.

Design and own AI‑first backend systems

  • Provide your technical POV on architecting and implementing backend services (Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, AWS, Vercel) that power generative AI agents, complex workflows (e.g., tax filing, advisory, audit), and document‑centric experiences.
  • Build and evolve AI orchestration: routing, tool calling, MCP servers, multi‑step workflows, safety and guardrails, and robust error handling around third‑party LLMs (OpenAI, Anthropic, and others).

Scale, reliability, and performance

  • Design for high‑throughput, low‑latency AI workloads: caching, queuing, rate‑limiting, model failover, and cost/performance trade-offs.
  • Work with large‑scale data: millions of documents, retrieval and search, vector stores, and indexing strategies tailored to tax and accounting use cases.
  • Establish and refine SLOs, observability, and incident response for AI systems that must be correct, auditable, and trustworthy in professional workflows.

  • Deep Python expertise and experience with production systems using frameworks like FastAPI (or similar), relational databases (PostgreSQL or equivalent), and a major cloud provider (AWS preferred).
  • Strong background in distributed systems: data modeling, API contracts, observability, resilience patterns, and performance tuning under load.
  • Proven track record leading large, complex projects end‑to‑end: architecture, execution, rollout, and long‑term operation.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to partner with product, design, and ML teams in a fast‑moving environment.
  • Demonstrated interest in AI systems and new engineering paradigms: LLMs, agents, retrieval, or similar – you care about what “AI‑native” software should look like.

Preferred Skills & Experience

  • Hands‑on experience integrating LLM APIs (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic) into production applications, including prompt/response management, cost controls, and safety considerations.
  • Experience with AI‑adjacent infrastructure: vector databases, embeddings, semantic search, or custom retrieval pipelines.
  • Opinions and experience around automated testing, reliability, and release practices for systems with non-deterministic model behavior.

job.title: Lead Software Development Engineer
job.description:
Lead Software Development Engineer

Thomson Reuters is looking for a Lead Software Engineer to join a highly dynamic team developing our next generation Global Trade Management application suite. Our engineers come from a broad range of backgrounds and experience levels, united by a shared drive to build exceptional software.

Successful candidates will be passionate about software engineering, measure success through working software and end user satisfaction, and have a desire to reimagine our business for the customer's benefit. We look for people who are comfortable with ambiguity and leverage an agentic AI-First approach across all SDLC operations.

Thomson Reuters ONESOURCE Global Trade is a comprehensive software suite designed to streamline and automate international trade management for businesses. It simplifies complex global trade operations by ensuring compliance with ever-changing regulations, optimizing supply chains, and reducing costs and risks associated with cross-border transactions. The platform integrates seamlessly with existing ERP systems to manage import/export processes, automate trade documentation, and provide real-time visibility into global shipments. By leveraging up-to-date regulatory content and advanced analytics, ONESOURCE empowers companies to enhance operational efficiency, mitigate compliance risks, and accelerate global growth in a fast-paced, highly regulated trade environment


About the role

In this role as a Lead Software Development Engineer you will:

  • Develop software applications using best practices in coordination with a distributed team.
  • Apply mastery-level understanding of software development methodologies to design and build complex SaaS systems.
  • Drive design decisions including platform selection, coding standards, and technical implementation.
  • Contribute across all aspects of an Agile development process, design, programming, testing, documentation, QA, and implementation.
  • Lead code reviews to enforce standards and provide constructive feedback.
  • Mentor junior team members to reinforce best practices and support their growth.
  • Ensure development efforts are properly estimated and delivered on time and to quality standards.
  • Collaborate with internal and external end users on requirements gathering and application design.
  • Provide technical guidance to management and help shape the technical direction for new product development.
  • Leverage innovation time to explore pet projects and areas of special interest.

About you

You’re fit for the role of Lead Software Development Engineer if your background includes:

  • 5+ years of experience developing software for the Global Trade industry, specifically in logistics, customs, or supply chain management.
  • 10+ years of software development experience across multiple programming languages, with a demonstrated ability to quickly learn new ones.
  • Proficiency in .NET development (C#, VB.NET).
  • Proficiency in responsive front-end / single page application development using Angular.
  • Proficiency developing and consuming REST APIs, including documentation tooling (Swagger, Postman).
  • Experience with both SQL and NoSQL data persistence systems (MSSQL, PostgreSQL, DynamoDB).
  • Working knowledge of DataDog for observability, APM, and RUM.
  • AWS and/or GCP cloud-native development experience.
  • 3+ years of hands-on experience with agentic AI-First development tools and processes.
  • Comfort with iterative, spec-light design. You'll need to think things through, fill in the blanks, and adapt across sprints based on customer feedback.

  • Lead-level understanding of design patterns and N-Tier architecture.
  • Strong debugging and troubleshooting skills.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills.
  • SaaS development experience on large to enterprise-class applications.
  • Strong grasp of object-oriented design, algorithms, data structures, and CS fundamentals.
  • Ability to produce clean, efficient, and concise code.

job.title: Contract Administrator - Special Events
job.description:
Company Information

AEG brings music, sports, and live entertainment together to create moments people remember around the world. Each year, more than 100 million fans experience live events across five continents—from global touring, concerts, and festivals to iconic sports and entertainment destinations.

Through our music division, AEG Presents, one of the world’s leading operators of tours, concerts, and music festivals, we help shape the sound of now. We work with artists at every stage of their careers to bring live music to life, connecting artists with fans on stages around the world.

Headquartered in Los Angeles, AEG Presents is driven by creativity, innovation, and purpose, and powered by people who want their work to show up in the real world.

If you’re ready to help create moments that matter, there’s a place for you here. Because it happens here.

Job Summary

The Contract Administrator will work closely with legal, operations, accounting and production teams to review artist, venue, co-promotion, vendor, locations and sponsor agreements. Additionally, this position will work closely with Manager of Contract Administration and/or accounting team to process wire requests and deposits for artists and venues. The Contract Administrator will review venue insurance requirements per contract obligations and ensure needs are met on an event-by-event basis.

Essential Functions

 

  • Manage the full lifecycle of Special Events agreements, including drafting, issuing, negotiating, reviewing, executing, and maintaining venue license agreements.
  • Draft, review, and administer ancillary agreements, including vendor agreements, data-sharing agreements, preferred catering agreements, and other event-related contracts.
  • Collaborate with Sales, Finance, Legal, and other internal stakeholders to ensure accuracy of event details, contractual terms, and operational requirements.
  • Review, collect, and approve certificates of insurance and related compliance documentation from clients, vendors, and third-party contractors.
  • Develop, implement, and continuously improve contract administration processes, workflows, and communication channels between field teams and corporate offices.
  • Maintain accurate and organized event files, ensuring all contracts, amendments, insurance documents, and related records are current and properly archived.
  • Train and mentor new employees on contract administration processes, systems, and best practices.
  • Serve as a primary point of contact for clients regarding contractual requirements, event documentation, and venue policies, ensuring timely and professional communication.
  •  Support business operations initiatives by identifying process improvements, enhancing reporting capabilities, and driving operational efficiencies across the Special Events division

 

Required Qualifications

  • High School Diploma or its equivalency (BA/BS Degree Preferred)
  • 2-4 years Of related work experience
  • Paralegal, legal experience preferred
  • Basic knowledge of contract administration and legal language
  • Strong attention to detail and highly organized
  • Ability to compare/analyze documentation
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Knowledge of Microsoft Office programs (Excel, Outlook, Word) and Adobe software
  • Ability to prioritize, multi-task and perform well under pressure
  • Interest/knowledge of music industry preferred

Payscale: $27.44 - $29.85

Bonus: This position is not eligible for a bonus under the current bonus plan requirements.

Benefits: Full-time: We offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes: medical, dental and vision insurance, paid holidays, vacation and sick time, company paid basic life insurance, voluntary life insurance, parental leave, 401k Plan (with a current employer match of 3%), flexible spending and health savings account options, and wellness offerings.

AEG reserves the right to change or modify the employee’s job description whether orally or in writing, at any time during the employment relationship.  AEG may require an employee to perform duties outside their normal description.

AEG's policy is to hire the most qualified applicants, and we comply with all applicable federal, state and local employment laws in making hiring and employee decisions.  We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate against applicants or employees on the basis of race, color, marital status, disability, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected status recognized by applicable federal, state or local law.

 

Employer does not offer work visa sponsorship for this position.

Owned by AEG, the LA Galaxy are powered by teams who bring energy, creativity, and commitment to everything they do, from matchday operations and fan engagement to the work that happens behind the scenes. Every role plays a part in shaping the experience on and off the pitch and building a club that reflects the city it represents.   If you want to be part of a team where your work shows up live, in real time, and in front of passionate fans, there’s a place for you here. Job Summary

The incumbent will lead the end‑to‑end production of original content, oversee post‑production workflows, manage video platforms, and support broadcast and external partners with footage requests. Responsibilities include filming, lighting design, audio recording, and conducting interviews for video productions.

job.title: Sr. Director, Business Development - AXS
job.description:
AXS connects fans with the artists and teams they love. Each year we sell millions of tickets to thousands of incredible events – from concerts and festivals to sports and theater – at some of the most iconic venues in the world. Since our founding in 2011, we’ve consistently pushed the industry forward and improved experiences for fans, making it easier than ever to discover events, find the perfect seats, and enjoy unforgettable live entertainment, and we continue to lead the evolution of our industry today.

We’re passionate about improving the fan experience and providing game-changing solutions for our clients, and we’re always looking for smart, motivated people to help make it happen. Bring your enthusiasm, your big ideas, and your desire to team up with some of the best and brightest in technology and entertainment.  

The Role

The Senior Director of Business Development will drive AXS’s growth across the sports industry by identifying, developing, and closing new partnerships with teams, leagues, venues, and other rights holders. Reporting to the Vice President of Business Development, this role will manage the full business development lifecycle, from market development and prospecting through solution design, financial modeling, negotiation, contracting and transition to implementation.

The Senior Director will build trusted relationships with senior decision makers, develop customized partnership strategies, and clearly communicate AXS’s ticketing capabilities. This individual will work closely with Product, Technology, Finance, Legal, Marketing, and Operations to create compelling proposals, structure commercially sound agreements, and ensure organizational alignment through the sales process.

The ideal candidate combines deep sports industry knowledge, strong commercial judgement, and a proven ability to navigate complex, long-term sales cycles involving multiple stakeholders.

What Will You Do?

  • Financial Proposals and Negotiations: Manage financial proposals and lead contract negotiations for new partnerships and renewals, ensuring terms that support long-term objectives.
  • Revenue Growth: Contribute to achieving and surpassing revenue targets by identifying key opportunities within all verticals.
  • CRM Leadership: Oversee CRM system use, including account maintenance, report generation, and workflow management. Ensure data integrity and process optimization.
  • Industry Representation: Represent AXS at industry events and tradeshows. Facilitate strategic meetings and events with external partners and prospects.
  • Executive Support: Assist the Business Development leadership team with strategic tasks and ad-hoc initiatives that drive growth.
  • Data Integrity: Ensure CRM data accuracy and advocate for best practices in data management, facilitating smooth handoffs to Customer Success.
  • Partnership Development: Cultivate relationships with potential partners and lead efforts to secure and coordinate meetings that drive business opportunities.
  • Sales Tools and Resources: Evolve sales tools, presentations, and contracts to meet marketplace needs and communicate AXS's value proposition.
  • Messaging and Content: Develop messaging and content that clearly articulate AXS's unique value across products, services, and verticals.

 

What Will You Bring?

  • 6+ years' experience in Business Development and ticketing or live entertainment
  • Strong experience with identifying opportunities, developing strategies, and negotiating creative solutions
  • Experience negotiating and executing contracts.
  • Experience in evolving sales tools, presentations, and messaging to align with market trends.
  • Experience representing a company at industry events and tradeshows, with the ability to network and generate leads.
  • Strong understanding of the sports and live entertainment ecosystem, including teams, leagues, venues, promoters, and other rights holders.
  • Knowledge of ticketing technology, primary and secondary distribution, pricing, inventory management, data, marketing, sponsorship, and venue operations.
  • Strong commercial and financial acumen, with the ability to evaluate opportunities, develop revenue models, and structure mutually beneficial agreements.
  • Consultative selling skills and the ability to translate a prospective partner’s business objectives into a customized solution

job.title: Senior Brand Marketing Manager, Social and Community
job.description:
WHO WE ARE:  

Splice is a creative platform for people who make music. Serious producers choose Splice Sounds to bring their ideas to life. A subscription to Splice inspires and accelerates creative success for digital music creators with an industry-leading catalog of sounds and samples and an expanding AI stack. With a rent-to-own marketplace of DAWs and plugins, the Splice experience seamlessly integrates into any music production workflow, regardless of DAW (Digital Audio Workstation). Via Splice, an unparalleled team of sound designers and sample creators are fueling the success of a growing global community of chart-topping producers, students, and DIY creators.

HOW WE WORK:  

At Splice, DISCO is a rallying cry for collaboration, accountability, and unity within our organization; Direct, Inclusive, Splice Together, Creator Centric, and Optimistic. Our shared success depends on our ability to support one another, work well together, and communicate directly. By embracing flexibility and a unified approach, we can navigate anything that’s thrown at us.

Splice embraces a culture of remote work. You’ll see your colleagues showing up from across the US and the UK. In order to keep us working well as a team, we have regular communication, including Town Halls, departmental all-hands and get-togethers.

When you join Splice, you join a network of colleagues, peers, and collaborators. Are you ready?

SENIOR BRAND MARKETING MANAGER, SOCIAL & COMMUNITY

LOCATION: Remote (US) — Los Angeles preferred, but not required

THE ROLE

Splice is looking for a full-time Senior Social & Community Manager to own the voice of Splice across our organic social portfolio and our Discord community. This is one of the most visible roles on the team and is central to the strategic direction of Splice: what you publish, how you show up, and what you learn from our audience shapes how the business thinks about creators. You’ll plan and publish content, run programming that brings producers together, engage directly with them in the comments, DMs, and Discord, and use performance data to sharpen what we make next. This is a hands-on role for someone who lives in the culture of music production. You make music yourself, you know what resonates with creators, and you can turn that instinct into content and community moments that earn attention. You’ll work closely with our brand, community, and product teams to translate what’s happening at Splice into things our community actually wants to see and take part in. As our portfolio grows, so does the role, with the opportunity to take on social and community channels for additional Splice brands.

WHO WE ARE

Splice is a creative platform for people who make music. Serious producers choose Splice Sounds to bring their ideas to life. A subscription to Splice inspires and accelerates creative success for digital music creators with an industry-leading catalog of sounds and samples and an expanding AI stack. With a rent-to-own marketplace of DAWs and plugins, the Splice experience seamlessly integrates into any music production workflow, regardless of DAW (Digital Audio Workstation). Via Splice, an unparalleled team of sound designers and sample creators are fueling the success of a growing global community of chart-topping producers, students, and DIY creators.

HOW WE WORK

At Splice, DISCO is a rallying cry for collaboration, accountability, and unity within our organization; Direct, Inclusive, Splice Together, Creator Centric, and Optimistic. Our shared success depends on our ability to support one another, work well together, and communicate directly. By embracing flexibility and a unified approach, we can navigate anything that's thrown at us. Splice embraces a culture of remote work. You'll see your colleagues showing up from across the US and the UK. In order to keep us working well as a team, we have regular communication, including Town Halls, departmental all-hands and get-togethers. When you join Splice, you join a network of colleagues, peers, and collaborators. Are you ready?

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Social

  • Own the organic social strategy and publishing calendar across all Splice channels, from ideation through scheduling, posting, and platform-native optimization, and decide where we show up as platforms and audience behavior change
  • Create and edit content yourself, from concept to final cut, with a fast turnaround and a strong point of view on what will land
  • Show up in the comments, DMs, and replies as the voice of Splice, engaging producers directly, surfacing their work, and building real relationships in the process
  • Spot and act on cultural moments, trends, and sounds in real time, including reactive posting outside of the calendar
  • Partner with brand, product, and community teams to turn launches, artist packs, and platform news into content that feels native to each channel rather than an announcement
  • Source and amplify community and creator-generated content, coordinating directly with producers and artists

Community

  • Manage and grow the Splice Discord server, keeping conversation active and welcoming day to day
  • Plan and run recurring community programming, including beat battles, community challenges, and remix competitions, from concept and rules through promotion, judging, and recognition of winners
  • Start and sustain regular conversations that give producers a reason to come back, share their work, and give each other feedback
  • Work with moderators and internal teams to keep the community healthy, and bring what you hear in Discord back to the wider business

Data and reporting

  • Track performance across social and community channels and translate the numbers into clear recommendations: what to double down on, what to stop, and what to test next
  • Use data to make decisions on content, programming, and channel investment, and report on channel health, community growth, and engagement to the business on a regular cadence
  • Develop workflows to move faster and produce more, across ideation, scripting, editing, asset generation, and analysis

Growth

  • As the Splice portfolio grows, take on strategy and management of social and community channels for additional brands, with the scope of the role growing alongside the portfolio

JOB REQUIREMENTS

  • 5+ years managing social channels for a brand, artist, label, or creator-facing company, with examples of work you can point to
  • Experience owning a multi-channel organic social presence, not a single platform
  • Experience speaking directly to a creator audience, ideally in music, but adjacent creative categories will be considered
  • You make music with a DAW. You understand production workflows from the inside and can talk to producers as a peer
  • A proven track record of building and engaging a community, not just growing follower counts, including hands-on experience running a Discord server or a comparable community space
  • Experience planning and running community programming such as contests, challenges, or competitions
  • Native fluency across the major social platforms, including the formats, editing conventions, and publishing tools for short-form video, long-form video, and text-based channels
  • Strong comfort with social and community analytics, and the ability to turn data into decisions and clear reporting for a business audience
  • Hands-on experience and a genuine appetite for new tools as they emerge
  • Strong writing and a natural instinct for tone. You can be funny, direct, and human without sounding like a brand account

NICE TO HAVES

  • Based in Los Angeles, with the ability to attend shoots, sessions, and creator meet-ups in person
  • Experience with Blender or other 3D rendering/animation tools, and the ability to create original content with them
  • Comfortable being on camera and featured in Splice content
  • Existing relationships in the producer, artist, or label community
  • Motion design, photography, or audio editing chops

SPLICE BENEFITS: 

  • Compensation & Equity: Competitive pay with annual reviews and equity opportunities.
  • Time Off: Unlimited PTO to recharge and thrive.
  • Health & Wellness: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents.
  • Retirement Savings: 401(k) plan with immediate vesting and company match.
  • Parental Support: 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave for non-birthing parents, and 18-20 weeks for birthing parents.
  • Flexible Work Options: Work remotely or connect at our office hubs and creative spaces worldwide.
  • Professional Growth: Annual learning budget, leadership programs, and team ambassador opportunities.
  • Community & Connection: Inclusive events, team meet-ups, and vibrant Employee Resource Groups.



The national pay range for this role is $112,000 - $140,000 Individual compensation will be commensurate with the candidate's experience.

As the infrastructure behind a family of companies spanning management, advisory, marketing and live experiences, backed by the reach of Live Nation Entertainment, we are uniquely positioned to deliver on that vision.

WHO ARE YOU?

Passionate and motivated. Driven, with an entrepreneurial spirit. Resourceful, innovative, forward thinking and committed. At Live Nation Entertainment, our people embrace these qualities, so if this sounds like you then please read on! 

 

THE ROLE

Reporting to the Vice President, Operations Finance, the Senior Director, Operations Finance owns operational accounting for Live Nation Canada. This is the senior operating leader of a function that accounts for every show, venue and festival we run in this country; tens of thousands of transactions a year, settled under contract in a fast-paced environment where the work is visible and the stakes are real.


The Senior Director’s mission will be to elevate the function by building a high-performing team and setting standards nationally for how shows and venues are accounted for. They will be responsible to evolve current processes toward greater automation, control and scale. Success in the first 12 months will be clear and measurable: a functioning management layer that consistently delivers on deadlines; a faster, cleaner close with a defensible timetable and fewer post-close adjustments; one written national process standard in use across all markets; an automated end-to-end workflow that is live, adopted and measurably reducing manual effort or error; and a strong control environment where audit findings are closed promptly and none repeat. Working in close partnership with the Vice President, the Senior Director will help shape the direction and priorities of the function. They will be the trusted go-to partner for the business on all matters of operational accounting. 


This is a great opportunity to own a national function, build a team around it, and elevate how Live Nation Canada does its accounting.


WHAT THIS ROLE WILL DO

Leadership

  • Own the structure, capability and performance of a ~12-person operational accounting team spanning show settlement, venue accounting and financial close
  • Lead through managers: develop the management layer, set clear ownership accountabilities, establish performance standards and hold managers accountable for their teams' deadlines and quality
  • Own talent strategy for the function: hiring standards, onboarding, development plans, succession depth, and a coverage model that holds through peak season, festival periods and major tours

Event Reporting and Operational Accounting

  • Accountable for the completeness, accuracy and timeliness of all events, venues and festivals accounting nationally (including the integrity of reported contribution margin by show, venue and market)
  • Own the close calendar end to end and commit to the timetable; ensure corporate reporting deadlines are consistently met
  • Own the accounting treatment of show settlement: from artist final settlements against contract, withholding tax, charity and merchandise/bundle recognition, co-promoted events,  joint venture splits, venue expense settlement and shared ancillary revenue
  • Own accounting for owned and operated venues, including inventory, labour costs and cash handling
  • Own balance sheet integrity for the function: reconciliation quality, accrual adequacy, deferred revenue, AR aging and collections performance for event-related balances
  • Develop and recommend accounting positions on complex deal structures such as co-promoted events, joint ventures, festival vehicles, rental versus promoted, international artist withholding, multi-year ancillary agreements
  • Partner with regional controllers to ensure consistent application of policy across markets, and resolve differences rather than reporting them
  • Partner with VP, Operational Accounting and Corporate for all technical accounting approval
  • Accountable for the day-to-day operation of internal controls over settlement, cash floats, AP approval and wire release, including SOX-relevant controls in scope
  • Play a critical role in internal and external audits; owning remediation of findings to closure while ensuring every settlement is audit-ready with proper documentation backup
  • Proactively identify control gaps as volume, venues and deal structures change, and implement corrective action

National Responsibilities

  • Develop, implement and sustain a national operational accounting playbook: settlement process, documentation standards, close process and checklist, reconciliation methodology, escalation path.
  • Identify and improve workstreams end to end; from business case through delivery to adoption and measured benefit
  • Define and report the function's operating metrics: days to close, settlement cycle time, restatement and error rates, aged AR, control exception volume. Use them to drive decisions and continuous improvement
  • Own the data standards that allow event economics to be reported consistently

Partner with the business

  • Provide the actuals, trend data and event-level insight that Strategic Finance and FP&A build the budget and forecast on; accountable for the reliability of what they plan from
  • Support due diligence, integration planning and post-close financial integration
  • Deputize for the VP, Operational Accounting on function matters with senior leadership to set priorities for the function, and act as their delegate with senior leadership when needed 



WHAT THIS PERSON WILL BRING

  • CPA designation required; Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance or related field
  • 10–12 years of progressive accounting and finance experience, including experience leading managers and building a management layer, not only managing individual contributors
  • Demonstrated ownership of a close and control environment across multiple sites, markets or entities within a larger corporate finance organization
  • A track record of leading a process or systems improvement end to end, from business case through delivery and adoption to measured result
  • Live entertainment, hospitality, venue, sports or comparable high-volume, deal-driven, contract-settled environment strongly preferred; comfort with a pace where revenue is earned in a single night and settled quickly
  • Strong Oracle and/or Salesforce capability; advanced Excel; practical use of Claude, AI platforms, BI and automation tooling to reduce manual work
  • Ability to hold an accounting position under commercial pressure while keeping the relationship intact
  • Credibility and presence with senior commercial leadership; able to explain complex financial outcomes clearly to non-financial stakeholders and earn their trust
  • Resourceful and hands-on when it matters; this is a senior role embedded in an operating business
  • Availability for travel and on-site support for major shows and festival properties, including evenings and weekends during peak season

 

BENEFITS & PERKS

Our motto is ‘Taking Care of Our Own’ through 6 pillars of benefits:

  • HEALTH: Medical, Dental and Vision benefits for you and your family, along with Employee Assistance Programs through Modern Health and ComPsych 
  • YOURSELF:  Generous paid time off policy including holiday closures, and sick time for you and dependents, along with free concert tickets 
  • WEALTH: RRSP program with company match, Stock Program Reimbursement 
  • FAMILY: New parent programs & support including caregiver leave and baby bonus, and infertility support 
  • CAREER: Tuition reimbursement, student loan repayment, and internal growth and development programs and training

job.description:
Job Summary:



Location: Oslo

Division: Ticketmaster Norway

Contract Terms: Temporary role, full-time (37.5 hours/week), starting ASAP until 30 June 2027.



THE TEAM


The team will focus on efficiently creating consumer demand and capturing existing demand to drive sales by utilizing several digital marketing platforms. The foundation is delivery of a content rich site, optimised for SEO. Servicing client relationships is key, demonstrating the power of our reach in combination with sophisticated targeting through marketing automation and activity across CRM, paid and organic social, search and advertising. Where there is opportunity to do so, the team should sell our marketing services, ensuring clients entrust us with their marketing budgets. The team also focuses on supporting the business by acquiring new tickets and retaining existing tickets by marketing the value of Ticketmaster products and services resulting in increased client satisfaction and traffic to the B2B site.

As the client marketing assistant, you are part of the Norwegian Marketing team and report directly to the Marketing Director Norway. You will support the local Marketing team with a variety of day-to-day tasks, with a particular focus on Client Marketing and supporting the team’s commercial marketing deliveries. You will also help collect campaign materials from clients, create campaign reports and support the team with other client marketing deliverables.

Location: Manchester, United Kingdom (hybrid)

Division: Fan Support Technology

Contract Terms: Permanent, Full-time


THE TEAM


Live Nation Entertainment is the largest live entertainment company in the world, consisting of five businesses: concert promotion and venue operations, sponsorship, ticketing solutions, ecommerce, and artist management. Live Nation seeks to innovate and enhance the live entertainment experience for artists and fans: before, during and after the show.

job.title: Apprentice BI Data Analyst
job.description:
Opportunity  

Brunswick Group is seeking an enthusiastic and analytical Apprentice BI Data Analyst to join its Group Business Intelligence (BI) team.

The Group BI team plays a key role in supporting the business globally by delivering meaningful data, reporting and analysis to inform strategic decisions. Working closely with Finance, FP&A, the Commercial Hub and other business teams, the function develops and maintains reporting systems and BI dashboards, helping stakeholders better understand financial performance, revenue and recovery data.

The successful candidate will work within the BI development team, reporting to the BI Technical Support Analyst. The role involves providing technical support, investigating and resolving reporting issues, and assisting with the development and improvement of dashboards to enhance self-service reporting across the firm.

Alongside gaining hands-on experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365, Azure SQL Server and Power BI, the successful candidate will complete a Level 4 Data Analyst Apprenticeship.

We are looking for a motivated individual with strong analytical and interpersonal skills, a keen interest in data and technology, and a willingness to learn. Previous Business Intelligence experience is not required, as training and mentoring will be provided. Applicants must meet the apprenticeship eligibility requirements.

About the Role 

Your day-to-day responsibilities will include:

  • Perform daily integrity checks
  • Investigating issues raised by end-users and resolve them or escalating them to the development team
  • Provide immediate solutions to system issues and liaise with other support teams to ensure prompt resolution
  • Manage small scale changes through to completion
  • Perform quality assurance tests and assisting with new release processes
  • Automate and enhance workflows
  • Manage and administer reporting security
  • Collaborate with people across the firm to enable them to self-serve Business Intelligence through Power BI
  • Work with developers to support the technical implementation and roll-out of new reporting dashboards on Power BI
  • As skills and knowledge are gained, personally take on development work, through SQL and Power BI within the team.

What We're Looking For

At Brunswick, we seek smart and curious individuals dedicated to learning and growth. We value potential, strong work ethic, and excellent written and verbal communication skills. Standout candidates demonstrate:

  • Working knowledge of Excel, with an enthusiasm to develop more advanced skills
  • Good analytical and problem-solving skills
  • An interest in working with data and using it to solve business problems
  • The ability to communicate effectively with colleagues at all levels of the business
  • A proactive approach and willingness to learn
  • A resilient, enthusiastic team player with strong self-motivation and a collaborative, hands-on approach
  • An interest in databases and data; previous exposure to SQL would be beneficial but is not essential
  • An interest in Business Intelligence and data visualisation; previous exposure to Power BI would be beneficial but is not essential
  • An interest in developing commercial and financial understanding
  • A sense of fun

Applications close on Friday 30th October 2026 at 4.00pm.

Why Join Us

Whether you are joining a client facing team, a core services team, or starting out on your professional career journey, joining Brunswick unlocks a range of exceptional employee benefits to support your financial future, health and wellness, family and community and continuous professional development.

 

About Brunswick

Brunswick is a global advisory firm. We help companies tackle high-stakes issues, navigate complex stakeholder relationships, and deliver high-impact outcomes. 

Our clients value our ability to anticipate, shape, and respond to the key players and forces in the financial and investment arena, regulatory and geopolitical universe, NGO community, workforce and beyond. They rely on us for deep experience, fresh perspectives and original thinking. So, in Brunswick you will find an exceptional range of experience and talent with a rich mix of backgrounds. From the beginning, we have prioritized attracting, developing, and retaining the best professionals in the industry, united by a culture of inclusivity, excellence, and intellectual curiosity.

Founded in 1987 in London, the firm has organically grown to 27 offices in 18 countries across the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa, Asia and Australia. We operate as a “one-firm firm” with no individual profit centers. This allows us to assemble fully integrated, bespoke teams for each client, able to draw on the full resources of Brunswick anywhere in the world. 

 

Brunswick is an equal opportunity employer.  All qualified applicants will be considered without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, pregnancy, genetic information, or any other status protected by applicable law. Please read our Global Privacy Notice to understand how your data is managed.
